display.text:
echo "::notice::session relay: taking the session over from run ${{ inputs.handoff_from }}. Everything below is a restore of what that runner saved; its watchdog is waiting for this run to publish before it steps aside."
          fi
          # ONE clone of session-state for both restores below.
          #
          # The branch had grown past 70 MB, and each of the two restores
          # cloned all of it - twice - before the hub could publish its
          # address. About 39 MB of that is one uploaded APK under artifacts/
          # that nothing in the restore path ever reads, so the clone carries
          # the same blob filter the script does. Both calls get the tree.
          STATE_DIR="$HOME/.npm-hub/tmp/session-state"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STATE_DIR")"
          rm -rf "$STATE_DIR"
          STATE_REMOTE="https://x-access-token:${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}@github.com/${{ github.repository }}.git"
          if ! git clone -q --depth 1 --filter=blob:limit=1m --branch session-state \
               "$STATE_REMOTE" "$STATE_DIR" 2>/dev/null; then
            if ! git clone -q --depth 1 --branch session-state \
                 "$STATE_REMOTE" "$STATE_DIR" 2>/dev/null; then
              STATE_DIR=""
              echo "::notice::no session-state branch yet; starting without the saved history"
            fi
          fi
          # Restore repos before importing OpenCode sessions: opencode import
          # needs the real repository CWD, not an empty placeholder folder.
          # The fork's own history does not depend on that restore, so the two
          # run together; the hub-work chats import below waits for the repos,
          # and runs after the fork restore so the two never copy the same
          # opencode bundle at the same time.
          # Repo restore is opt-in from the hub's Snapshot tab now: pulling the
          # whole work-backup copy BEFORE the tunnel publishes cost the connect
          # page ~4 of the user's minutes at every launch. The script sees
          # WORK_BACKUP_RESTORE=0 and exits at once; everything else in this
          # step (audit/code, chat bundles) is small and stays.
          GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" WORK_BACKUP_ROOT="$HOME" \
            WORK_BACKUP_RESTORE=0 WORK_BACKUP_RESTORE_EXISTING=1 bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/restore-work.sh" \
            2>&1 | tee -a "$HUB_LOGS/restore-work.log" &
          WORK_PID=$!
          GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" STATE_DIR="$STATE_DIR" \
            bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/restore_audit_code.sh" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork" 2>&1 | tee -a "$HUB_LOGS/restore.log" || echo "::warning::fork restore failed"
          wait "$WORK_PID" || echo "::warning::hub-work restore failed"
          # Restore-chats imports the zen-panel fork only by default; the
          # hub-work call gets RESTORE_CHATS_ALL=1 so every repo the Files tab
          # cloned (and the fork itself) gets its opencode sessions back.
          RESTORE_CHATS_ALL=1 RESTORE_CHATS_ROOT="$HOME" \
            GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" STATE_DIR="$STATE_DIR" \
            bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/restore_audit_code.sh" "$HOME/hub-work" 2>&1 | tee -a "$HUB_LOGS/restore-hubwork.log" || echo "::warning::hub-work chats restore failed"
          rm -rf "$STATE_DIR"

      - name: Start the hub and open the tunnel
        env:
          NGROK_AUTHTOKEN: ${{ secrets.NGROK_AUTHTOKEN }}
        run: |
          export HUB_LOGS="$HOME/.npm-hub/logs"; mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS" 2>/dev/null || true
          echo "HUB_LOGS=$HUB_LOGS HOME=$HOME $(ls -ld "$HUB_LOGS" 2>&1)"
          cd "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/npm-hub"
          export HUB_LOGS="$HOME/.npm-hub/logs"; mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS" 2>/dev/null || true
          HUB_PORT=8090
          HUB_TOKEN_VALUE='${{ inputs.token }}'
          HUB_PID_FILE="$HUB_LOGS/hub.pid"
          if [ -f "$HUB_PID_FILE" ]; then
            OLD_PID="$(tr -dc '0-9' < "$HUB_PID_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            if [ -n "$OLD_PID" ] && kill -0 "$OLD_PID" 2>/dev/null \
              && tr '\0' ' ' < "/proc/$OLD_PID/cmdline" 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'src/server.js'; then
              kill "$OLD_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
            fi
          fi
          pkill -f "cloudflared [t]unnel --url http://127.0.0.1:$HUB_PORT" 2>/dev/null || true
          for i in $(seq 1 15); do
            curl -sf -m 2 "http://127.0.0.1:$HUB_PORT/api/tools" >/dev/null 2>&1 || break
            sleep 1
          done
          hub_ready() {
            local body
            body="$(curl -sf -m 15 -H "x-hub-token: $HUB_TOKEN_VALUE" "http://127.0.0.1:$HUB_PORT/api/tools" 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
            echo "$body" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); raise SystemExit(0 if str(d.get("runId", "")) == sys.argv[1] else 1)' "$GITHUB_RUN_ID"
          }
          SESSION_FILE="$HOME/.npm-hub/session-start"
          date +%s000 > "$SESSION_FILE"
          HUB_PORT_STRICT=1 HUB_TOKEN="$HUB_TOKEN_VALUE" HUB_LABEL='${{ inputs.label }}' GH_TOKEN='${{ inputs.gh_token }}' PORT="$HUB_PORT" SESSION_STARTED_MS="$(cat "$SESSION_FILE")" SESSION_LIMIT_MS=21600000 nohup node src/server.js > "$HUB_LOGS/hub.log" 2>&1 &
          HUB_PID=$!
          echo "$HUB_PID" > "$HUB_PID_FILE"
          for i in $(seq 1 60); do
            hub_ready && break
            sleep 2
          done
          if ! hub_ready; then
            echo "::error::the hub did not start for run $GITHUB_RUN_ID."
            tail -40 "$HUB_LOGS/hub.log"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "hub is up on $HUB_PORT for run $GITHUB_RUN_ID"
          # Start audit/code snapshot daemon (audit.json = chat, code.json = diff + sessions), plus chats for every repo
          export SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL=120
          # Also keep chats/<name>.json for every repo fresh every ~20 min,
          # so an interrupted runner still hands sessions to the next one.
          export SNAPSHOT_EXPORT_ALL_CHATS=1
          nohup env GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" GITHUB_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/snapshot-audit-code.sh" hub "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork" > "$HUB_LOGS/snapshot-hub.log" 2>&1 &
          echo $! > "$HUB_LOGS/snapshot.pid"
          echo "snapshot daemon: audit.json + code.json every 120s -> session-state"
          # Durable work backup: every repo under HOME becomes a git bundle plus
          # its WIP diff and untracked files on the work-backup branch, so a
          # runner that dies with unpushed work loses nothing.
          nohup env GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" GITHUB_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" WORK_BACKUP_ROOT="$HOME" WORK_BACKUP_INTERVAL=300 bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/backup-work.sh" >> "$HUB_LOGS/work-backup.log" 2>&1 &
          echo $! > "$HUB_LOGS/work-backup.pid"
          echo "work-backup daemon: HOME snapshot every 300s -> work-backup branch"
          # Rescue channels (they outlive the hub web stack): a tmate SSH/web
          # shell and a whitelisted command queue on the session-state branch -
          # so a runner with a dead hub and a dead tunnel stays steerable from
          # GitHub alone instead of being a closed box until the 6h cap.
          if [ "${{ inputs.rescue_ssh }}" = "true" ]; then
            GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" GITHUB_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" CONTROL_TARGET=hub \
              nohup bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/rescue_ssh.sh" >> "$HUB_LOGS/rescue-ssh.log" 2>&1 &
            echo $! > "$HUB_LOGS/rescue-ssh.pid"
            echo "rescue ssh daemon: tmate shell published -> control/rescue-hub.json"
          fi
          if [ "${{ inputs.command_queue }}" = "true" ]; then
            GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" GITHUB_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" CONTROL_TARGET=hub \
              HUB_TOKEN_VALUE='${{ inputs.token }}' HUB_LABEL='${{ inputs.label }}' \
              nohup bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/hub_control.sh" >> "$HUB_LOGS/hub-control.log" 2>&1 &
            echo $! > "$HUB_LOGS/hub-control.pid"
            echo "control daemon (hub VM): control/queue.json + heartbeat; ops: ping, backup-now, restart-hub, up-hub, reopen-tunnel, handoff-save"
          fi

          URL=$(bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/open_tunnel.sh" 8090 $HUB_LOGS/tunnel.log)
          if [ -z "$URL" ]; then
            echo "::error::no tunnel came up."
            tail -25 $HUB_LOGS/tunnel.log
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "$URL" > $HUB_LOGS/hub-url

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Restore the working tree from the newest `work-backup` snapshot.
#
# Runs at hub startup, after restore_audit_code.sh, so a runner that died with
# unpushed work comes back with that work in place: each repo is rebuilt from
# its git bundle, the uncommitted diff is reapplied and untracked files are
# unpacked. Small non-repo files are restored only when missing.
#
# SAFETY
#   An existing directory that is already a git repo is never touched: it holds
#   newer work than the snapshot and clobbering it would be the very data loss
#   this is meant to prevent. Restore only fills in paths that are absent.
#
# ENV
#   WORK_BACKUP_ROOT        root to restore into   (default $HOME)
#   WORK_BACKUP_BRANCH      source branch          (default work-backup)
#   WORK_BACKUP_SNAPSHOT    explicit snapshot dir  (default: newest)
#   SESSION_STATE_URL       git remote override for local tests
#   WORK_BACKUP_RESTORE=0   skip entirely
#
# WHAT TO RESTORE (all optional; unset means everything, which is what the
# automatic restore at hub start wants. The hub's snapshot tab ticks these.)
#   WORK_BACKUP_ONLY_REPOS      set: newline-separated `rel` paths, * for all,
#                               empty string for none. Unset = everything.
#   WORK_BACKUP_SKIP_CHATS=1     no opencode chat sessions
#   WORK_BACKUP_SKIP_SETTINGS=1  no opencode settings
#   WORK_BACKUP_SKIP_FILES=1     no loose home files, no chunked big files
#   WORK_BACKUP_SKIP_SESSIONS=1  no terminal descriptors / TUI snapshots
set -uo pipefail

ROOT="${WORK_BACKUP_ROOT:-$HOME}"
BRANCH="${WORK_BACKUP_BRANCH:-work-backup}"
HUB_LOGS="${HUB_LOGS:-$HOME/.npm-hub/logs}"
if ! mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS" 2>/dev/null; then
  printf '%s\n' "restore-work: cannot create log directory" >&2
  exit 1
fi
log() { echo "[restore-work $(date -u '+%H:%M:%S')] $*" | tee -a "$HUB_LOGS/restore-work.log"; }
# Same shape as backup-work.sh's sanitize: the chat bundle name is derived from
# this on both sides, so the two must agree exactly.
sanitize() { printf '%s' "$1" | tr -c 'A-Za-z0-9._-' '_' | cut -c1-160; }

[ "${WORK_BACKUP_RESTORE:-1}" = "0" ] && { log "disabled"; exit 0; }

# Apply the WIP/untracked part without replacing a repo that the workflow
# checked out freshly. This is enabled explicitly for the Hub checkout: the
# old runner's local edits must come back on top of the new checkout.
apply_payload() {
  local dir="$1" repodir="$2" label="$3" result=0
  if [ -s "$repodir/wip.patch" ]; then
    if ( cd "$dir" && git apply --whitespace=nowarn "$repodir/wip.patch" 2>/dev/null ); then
      log "applied uncommitted changes to $label"
    else
      log "could not reapply uncommitted changes to $label (kept at $repodir/wip.patch)"
      result=1
    fi
  fi
  if [ -s "$repodir/untracked.tar.gz" ]; then
    if extract_keep_old "$dir" "$repodir/untracked.tar.gz"; then
      log "restored untracked files for $label"

Repo: /home/runner/work/zen-panel/zen-panel/fork. Diagnose only, do NOT edit. Report back a design.

## The user's complaint (three related symptoms)

1. **cloudflared flaps even though ngrok exists.** In their words: «несмотря на нгрок все равно cloudflared со своими сбоями открывается». ngrok is supposed to be the stable primary leg and cloudflare the reserve, but cloudflare keeps dying/reopening.
2. **No visible tunnel addresses in the journal.** «нету в приложении видимых адресов в журнале» — the panel's journal never shows the actual tunnel URL, so the user cannot see or manually use an address.
3. **VPN interference.** «мне постоянно приходится менять впн из за этого так как он большинство попросту не принимает либо отказуется принимать а без впн только может включить а потом сразу же падает». Some VPNs reject/can't establish the tunnel; with no VPN cloudflared comes up and immediately dies. The user has to keep toggling VPN, which is maddening.

## Files

- `tools/tunnel_keeper.sh` (139 lines) — dual-tunnel keeper. Header says: main = the workflow's own address, refreshed by the watchdog "only fills in when the address dropped and stayed dropped for ~a minute"; reserve = `TUNNEL_TAG=reserve`, republished straight into the session descriptor. `INTERVAL="${KEEPER_INTERVAL:-20}"`. Has `MAIN_FAILS=0` and a comment "After a reserve open fails, stop retrying every loop. A quick tunnel that…". Ports 8090 (hub) / 6081 (vnc).
- `tools/ngrok_keeper.sh` (196 lines) — the ngrok leg.
- `tools/open_tunnel.sh` (147 lines) — opens a quick tunnel (cloudflare).
- `tools/hub_control.sh` (220 lines) — control daemon; `reopen-tunnel` at lines 119-131 kills cloudflared and reopens.
- `tools/publish_session.sh` — writes the session descriptor to the `session-state` branch.
- `.github/workflows/hub.yml` — the workflow; installs/starts the keepers. Check for the known notice «NGROK_AUTHTOKEN secret is empty - the ngrok reserve leg is off».
- Session file shape consumed by the panel: `hub/src/main/assets/hub/index.html`, `sessionBases()` at line 842 (order: `s.ngrok`, then `s.hubUrl || s.url`, then `s.url2`), `hubCandidates()` at line 813, `firstReachableBase()` at line 685, `preflightHub()` at line 662.
- The panel's journal logger: `log(...)` in the same file — find its definition and every call site that emits a tunnel address or deliberately withholds one.

## Key observation to verify or refute

From the user's screenshot log there is exactly ONE line «Основной адрес молчит — пробую резервный…». That string is emitted at `index.html:689` **only when `i > 0`**. Therefore `sessionBases()` returned exactly 2 bases, i.e. **`s.ngrok` was empty**. So in that run ngrok was NOT actually up, and the "dual tunnel" degraded to cloudflare-only — which is exactly symptom 1. Verify this inference and explain precisely which condition produces an empty `s.ngrok` (missing `NGROK_AUTHTOKEN` secret, keeper crash, auth failure, publish omission, or something else). Check `hub.yml` and `publish_session.sh` for how `ngrok=` gets into the descriptor and whether a failure is silent.

## What I need from you

1. **Explain symptom 1 mechanically.** Why does cloudflare die and reopen when ngrok is supposed to be primary? Read `tunnel_keeper.sh` fully. Is the keeper itself causing churn — e.g. a health check that fails spuriously and reopens, a `MAIN_FAILS` threshold that resets, a reserve/main mix-up, or the `reopen-tunnel` op racing the keeper? Note that `hub_control.sh`'s `reopen-tunnel` and `tunnel_keeper.sh` both restart cloudflared — check whether they can fight each other (two owners of one pidfile).

2. **Diagnose symptom 3 (VPN).** cloudflared quick tunnels (`trycloudflare.com`) are notorious for being blocked/rate-limited by VPN egress IPs, and for dying when the VPN's MTU or the network path flaps. Concretely: does `open_tunnel.sh` do any retry, any local-interface pinning, any MTU setting, any `--protocol`, any region/`--edge` selection? Does anything bind cloudflared to a specific network interface or bypass a proxy? Does the keeper distinguish "VPN broke it" from "the hub died"? Give the concrete hardening options for this repo, ranked by cost/benefit, and say which one kills symptom 3 outright rather than just making it rarer.

3. **Diagnose symptom 2 (no visible addresses).** Find every place the panel knows a tunnel base and decide whether to surface it. Propose the exact journal lines, where to emit them, and at what verbosity — they must be useful on a phone screen without spamming. Note the panel already logs «Адрес получен: …» at `index.html:952` inside `afterDispatch` — check why that is NOT visible in the user's journal (is `afterDispatch` even reached in their failing path?). Give the full set of places that should log an address.

4. **Design the fix**, priority-ordered, with the specific functions/lines to change and the behavioural contract. Include: how the keeper should behave when ngrok is present vs absent; how to avoid two owners killing one tunnel; whether `sessionBases()` should be taught to treat a missing ngrok leg explicitly (an honest "primary leg absent" log line rather than silently walking to cloudflare); and what the panel should log.

5. **Risks/regressions.** Tunnel churn costs GitHub API quota (every republish is a branch write). Doubling owners doubles republish rate. Changing the primary-leg order changes which address the user lands on and therefore which one dies.

6. **Test plan.** Read `TESTING.md`, `.github/workflows/tests.yml`, `tests/` (`hub-connect-e2e.js` is the jsdom harness that loads `hub/src/main/assets/hub/index.html`; there are also `*.sh` tests). Specify tests for the keeper scripts (bash) and for the panel logging (jsdom), with file paths, in the repo's existing style.

<content>
1: #!/usr/bin/env bash
2: # Dual-tunnel keeper (Z11): one endpoint, TWO public addresses, all the time.
3: #
4: # WHY
5: #   A quick tunnel dies eventually; when it is the only address the user's
6: #   phone instantly shows «Не открывается» until somebody repairs it. With a
7: #   reserve address always warm, the app just walks over to it (see the hub
8: #   APK: url2 fallback) while this daemon resurrects the main one. Repair no
9: #   longer depends on the job's keep-alive step being alive: this loop owns
10: #   both addresses by itself.
11: #
12: # WHAT IT OWNS
13: #   main    the workflow's own address (opened by the job, refreshed by the
14: #           watchdog when that survives - this daemon only fills in when the
15: #           address dropped and stayed dropped for ~a minute)
16: #   reserve TUNNEL_TAG=reserve, its own pid/url/log files, refreshed here on
17: #           every death and republished straight into the session descriptor
18: #
19: # PUBLISHED KEYS (preserved by url2-merge upstream in this workflow)
20: #   hub: url, hubUrl, desktop, mobile + url2 (reserve base)
21: #   vnc: url, novncUrl (+ url /vnc.html) + url2 (reserve base)
22: set -uo pipefail
23: 
24: VM="${1:-hub}"          # hub | vnc
25: HUB_LOGS="${HUB_LOGS:-$HOME/.npm-hub/logs}"
26: mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS" 2>/dev/null || true
27: TOOLS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
28: TOKEN="${GH_TOKEN:-${GITHUB_TOKEN:-}}"
29: [ -z "$TOKEN" ] && { echo "[tunnel-keeper] no token" >&2; exit 1; }
30: 
31: if [ "$VM" = "vnc" ]; then
32:   PORT=6081; SLOT=vnc; URLFILE="$HUB_LOGS/vnc-url"; HEALTH_PATH="/vnc.html"
33:   R_URLFILE="$HUB_LOGS/vnc-url2"
34: else
35:   PORT=8090; SLOT=hub-linux; URLFILE="$HUB_LOGS/hub-url"; HEALTH_PATH="/"
36:   R_URLFILE="$HUB_LOGS/hub-url2"
37: fi
38: INTERVAL="${KEEPER_INTERVAL:-20}"
39: MAIN_FAILS=0
40: # After a reserve open fails, stop retrying every loop. A quick tunnel that
41: # Cloudflare refuses (HTTP 429, "too many tunnels") only gets angrier when asked
42: # every 20 seconds; waiting minutes is what lets it succeed. The count is also
43: # how many loops to skip before touching the reserve again.
44: RESERVE_COOLDOWN="${KEEPER_RESERVE_COOLDOWN:-15}"
45: RESERVE_SKIP=0
46: 
47: log() { echo "[tunnel-keeper:$VM $(date -u '+%H:%M:%S')] $*" | tee -a "$HUB_LOGS/tunnel-keeper.log"; }
48: 
49: healthy() {  # $1 = url
50:   [ -n "$1" ] && bash "$TOOLS_DIR/tunnel_health.sh" "$1" "$HEALTH_PATH" >/dev/null 2>&1
51: }
52: 
53: url_for_pidfile() {  # $1 = pidfile path
54:   local p
55:   [ -f "$1" ] || return 1
56:   p="$(tr -dc '0-9' < "$1" 2>/dev/null || true)" || true
57:   [ -n "${p:-}" ] && kill -0 "$p" 2>/dev/null || return 1
58:   cat "${1%.pid}.url" 2>/dev/null || true
59: }
60: 
61: publish_pair() {  # args k=v ... (always includes both base urls we know)
62:   local main reserve
63:   main="$(cat "$URLFILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
64:   reserve="$(cat "$R_URLFILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
65:   if [ "$SLOT" = "hub-linux" ]; then
66:     GH_TOKEN="$TOKEN" bash "$TOOLS_DIR/publish_session.sh" \
67:       "slot=hub-linux" "kind=NPM-Hub" "os=linux" \
68:       ${main:+"url=$main"} ${main:+"hubUrl=$main"} ${main:+"desktop=$main/d"} ${main:+"mobile=$main/m"} \
69:       ${reserve:+"url2=$reserve"} \
70:       "auth=без пароля" "label=${HUB_LABEL:-hub}" 2>&1 | tail -1
71:   else
72:     GH_TOKEN="$TOKEN" bash "$TOOLS_DIR/publish_session.sh" \
73:       "slot=vnc" "kind=Linux-VNC" "os=linux" \
74:       ${main:+"url=$main/vnc.html"} ${main:+"novncUrl=$main/vnc.html"} \
75:       ${reserve:+"url2=$reserve"} \
76:       "label=${HUB_LABEL:-hub}" 2>&1 | tail -1
77:   fi
78: }
79: 
80: open_reserve() {
81:   local url
82:   # Drop any previously published reserve BEFORE opening: if this open fails the
83:   # client must not keep probing a dead address (a stale url2 is exactly what
84:   # made the panel report «ни основной, ни резервный адрес не отвечает»).
85:   rm -f "$R_URLFILE"
86:   url="$(TUNNEL_TAG=reserve bash "$TOOLS_DIR/open_tunnel.sh" "$PORT" "$HUB_LOGS/tunnel-reserve.log" 2>/dev/null || echo)"
87:   if [ -n "$url" ]; then
88:     echo "$url" > "$R_URLFILE"
89:     log "reserve tunnel up: $url"
90:     RESERVE_SKIP=0
91:     return 0
92:   fi
93:   RESERVE_SKIP="$RESERVE_COOLDOWN"
94:   log "reserve tunnel reopen failed; backing off $RESERVE_COOLDOWN loops (see tunnel-reserve.log)"
95:   return 1
96: }
97: 
98: open_main() {
99:   local url
100:   url="$(bash "$TOOLS_DIR/open_tunnel.sh" "$PORT" "$HUB_LOGS/keeper-tunnel.log" 2>/dev/null || echo)"
101:   if [ -n "$url" ]; then
102:     echo "$url" > "$URLFILE"
103:     log "main tunnel resurrected: $url (the keep-alive step was not up to it)"
104:   else
105:     log "main tunnel reopen failed (retry next loop)"
106:   fi
107: }
108: 
109: trap 'log "stopped"; exit 0' TERM INT
110: log "keeper up ($VM, port $PORT; reserve pid via TUNNEL_TAG=reserve)"
111: while true; do
112:   sleep "$INTERVAL"
113:   # ── reserve ──
114:   if [ "$RESERVE_SKIP" -gt 0 ]; then
115:     RESERVE_SKIP=$((RESERVE_SKIP - 1))
116:   else
117:     r_pid_ok=0; r_url="$(url_for_pidfile "$HUB_LOGS/cloudflared-$PORT-reserve.pid" || true)"
118:     [ -n "${r_url:-}" ] && healthy "$r_url" && r_pid_ok=1
119:     if [ "$r_pid_ok" = "0" ]; then
120:       open_reserve
121:       publish_pair || true
122:     fi
123:   fi
124:   # ── main (only kick it after several consecutive dead probes: a busy CPU
125:   # can make a single probe time out, same rule as the job watchdog) ──
126:   m_pid_ok=0; m_url="$(url_for_pidfile "$HUB_LOGS/cloudflared-$PORT.pid" || true)"
127:   if [ -n "${m_url:-}" ] && healthy "$m_url"; then
128:     [ "${m_url:-}" != "$(cat "$URLFILE" 2>/dev/null)" ] && echo "$m_url" > "$URLFILE" || true
129:     MAIN_FAILS=0
130:   else
131:     MAIN_FAILS=$((MAIN_FAILS + 1))
132:   fi
133:   if [ "$MAIN_FAILS" -ge 3 ]; then
134:     log "main tunnel dead $MAIN_FAILS probes in a row; reserve keeps serving - reopening main"
135:     open_main
136:     publish_pair || true
137:     MAIN_FAILS=0
138:   fi
139: done

#   phone instantly shows «Не открывается» until somebody repairs it. With a
#   reserve address always warm, the app just walks over to it (see the hub
#   APK: url2 fallback) while this daemon resurrects the main one. Repair no
#   longer depends on the job's keep-alive step being alive: this loop owns
#   both addresses by itself.
#
# WHAT IT OWNS
#   main    the workflow's own address (opened by the job, refreshed by the
#           watchdog when that survives - this daemon only fills in when the
#           address dropped and stayed dropped for ~a minute)
#   reserve TUNNEL_TAG=reserve, its own pid/url/log files, refreshed here on
#           every death and republished straight into the session descriptor
#
# PUBLISHED KEYS (preserved by url2-merge upstream in this workflow)
#   hub: url, hubUrl, desktop, mobile + url2 (reserve base)

display.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Dual-tunnel keeper (Z11): one endpoint, TWO public addresses, all the time.
#
# WHY
#   A quick tunnel dies eventually; when it is the only address the user's
#   phone instantly shows «Не открывается» until somebody repairs it. With a
#   reserve address always warm, the app just walks over to it (see the hub
#   APK: url2 fallback) while this daemon resurrects the main one. Repair no
#   longer depends on the job's keep-alive step being alive: this loop owns
#   both addresses by itself.
#
# WHAT IT OWNS
#   main    the workflow's own address (opened by the job, refreshed by the
#           watchdog when that survives - this daemon only fills in when the
#           address dropped and stayed dropped for ~a minute)
#   reserve TUNNEL_TAG=reserve, its own pid/url/log files, refreshed here on
#           every death and republished straight into the session descriptor
#
# PUBLISHED KEYS (preserved by url2-merge upstream in this workflow)
#   hub: url, hubUrl, desktop, mobile + url2 (reserve base)
#   vnc: url, novncUrl (+ url /vnc.html) + url2 (reserve base)
set -uo pipefail

VM="${1:-hub}"          # hub | vnc
HUB_LOGS="${HUB_LOGS:-$HOME/.npm-hub/logs}"
mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS" 2>/dev/null || true
TOOLS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
TOKEN="${GH_TOKEN:-${GITHUB_TOKEN:-}}"
[ -z "$TOKEN" ] && { echo "[tunnel-keeper] no token" >&2; exit 1; }

if [ "$VM" = "vnc" ]; then
  PORT=6081; SLOT=vnc; URLFILE="$HUB_LOGS/vnc-url"; HEALTH_PATH="/vnc.html"
  R_URLFILE="$HUB_LOGS/vnc-url2"
else
  PORT=8090; SLOT=hub-linux; URLFILE="$HUB_LOGS/hub-url"; HEALTH_PATH="/"
  R_URLFILE="$HUB_LOGS/hub-url2"
fi
INTERVAL="${KEEPER_INTERVAL:-20}"
MAIN_FAILS=0
# After a reserve open fails, stop retrying every loop. A quick tunnel that
# Cloudflare refuses (HTTP 429, "too many tunnels") only gets angrier when asked
# every 20 seconds; waiting minutes is what lets it succeed. The count is also
# how many loops to skip before touching the reserve again.
RESERVE_COOLDOWN="${KEEPER_RESERVE_COOLDOWN:-15}"
RESERVE_SKIP=0

log() { echo "[tunnel-keeper:$VM $(date -u '+%H:%M:%S')] $*" | tee -a "$HUB_LOGS/tunnel-keeper.log"; }

healthy() {  # $1 = url
  [ -n "$1" ] && bash "$TOOLS_DIR/tunnel_health.sh" "$1" "$HEALTH_PATH" >/dev/null 2>&1
}

url_for_pidfile() {  # $1 = pidfile path
  local p
  [ -f "$1" ] || return 1
  p="$(tr -dc '0-9' < "$1" 2>/dev/null || true)" || true
  [ -n "${p:-}" ] && kill -0 "$p" 2>/dev/null || return 1
  cat "${1%.pid}.url" 2>/dev/null || true
}

publish_pair() {  # args k=v ... (always includes both base urls we know)
  local main reserve
  main="$(cat "$URLFILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  reserve="$(cat "$R_URLFILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  if [ "$SLOT" = "hub-linux" ]; then
    GH_TOKEN="$TOKEN" bash "$TOOLS_DIR/publish_session.sh" \
      "slot=hub-linux" "kind=NPM-Hub" "os=linux" \
      ${main:+"url=$main"} ${main:+"hubUrl=$main"} ${main:+"desktop=$main/d"} ${main:+"mobile=$main/m"} \
      ${reserve:+"url2=$reserve"} \
      "auth=без пароля" "label=${HUB_LABEL:-hub}" 2>&1 | tail -1
  else
    GH_TOKEN="$TOKEN" bash "$TOOLS_DIR/publish_session.sh" \
      "slot=vnc" "kind=Linux-VNC" "os=linux" \
      ${main:+"url=$main/vnc.html"} ${main:+"novncUrl=$main/vnc.html"} \
      ${reserve:+"url2=$reserve"} \
      "label=${HUB_LABEL:-hub}" 2>&1 | tail -1
  fi
}

open_reserve() {
  local url
  # Drop any previously published reserve BEFORE opening: if this open fails the
  # client must not keep probing a dead address (a stale url2 is exactly what
  # made the panel report «ни основной, ни резервный адрес не отвечает»).
  rm -f "$R_URLFILE"
  url="$(TUNNEL_TAG=reserve bash "$TOOLS_DIR/open_tunnel.sh" "$PORT" "$HUB_LOGS/tunnel-reserve.log" 2>/dev/null || echo)"
  if [ -n "$url" ]; then
    echo "$url" > "$R_URLFILE"
    log "reserve tunnel up: $url"
    RESERVE_SKIP=0
    return 0
  fi
  RESERVE_SKIP="$RESERVE_COOLDOWN"
  log "reserve tunnel reopen failed; backing off $RESERVE_COOLDOWN loops (see tunnel-reserve.log)"
  return 1
}

open_main() {
  local url
  url="$(bash "$TOOLS_DIR/open_tunnel.sh" "$PORT" "$HUB_LOGS/keeper-tunnel.log" 2>/dev/null || echo)"
  if [ -n "$url" ]; then
    echo "$url" > "$URLFILE"
    log "main tunnel resurrected: $url (the keep-alive step was not up to it)"
  else
    log "main tunnel reopen failed (retry next loop)"
  fi
}

trap 'log "stopped"; exit 0' TERM INT
log "keeper up ($VM, port $PORT; reserve pid via TUNNEL_TAG=reserve)"
while true; do
  sleep "$INTERVAL"
  # ── reserve ──
  if [ "$RESERVE_SKIP" -gt 0 ]; then
    RESERVE_SKIP=$((RESERVE_SKIP - 1))
  else
    r_pid_ok=0; r_url="$(url_for_pidfile "$HUB_LOGS/cloudflared-$PORT-reserve.pid" || true)"
    [ -n "${r_url:-}" ] && healthy "$r_url" && r_pid_ok=1
    if [ "$r_pid_ok" = "0" ]; then
      open_reserve
      publish_pair || true
    fi
  fi
  # ── main (only kick it after several consecutive dead probes: a busy CPU
  # can make a single probe time out, same rule as the job watchdog) ──
  m_pid_ok=0; m_url="$(url_for_pidfile "$HUB_LOGS/cloudflared-$PORT.pid" || true)"
  if [ -n "${m_url:-}" ] && healthy "$m_url"; then
    [ "${m_url:-}" != "$(cat "$URLFILE" 2>/dev/null)" ] && echo "$m_url" > "$URLFILE" || true
    MAIN_FAILS=0
  else
    MAIN_FAILS=$((MAIN_FAILS + 1))
  fi
  if [ "$MAIN_FAILS" -ge 3 ]; then
    log "main tunnel dead $MAIN_FAILS probes in a row; reserve keeps serving - reopening main"
    open_main
    publish_pair || true
    MAIN_FAILS=0
  fi
done

    "auth=без пароля" "label=${HUB_LABEL:-hub}" 2>&1 | tail -1
}

start_agent() {  # echoes the new URL on success, nothing on failure
  local pid url i
  [ -f "$HOME/.config/ngrok/ngrok.yml" ] || ngrok config add-authtoken "$AUTHTOKEN" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  # Static reserved domain (free tier, claimed in the dashboard): the address
  # survives every agent restart, so the panel can treat this leg as PRIMARY.
  # --url is the current v3 flag (supersedes --domain); empty = old behaviour.
  local domain="${NGROK_DOMAIN:-filly-above-terrapin.ngrok-free.app}"
  nohup ngrok http ${domain:+--url="https://$domain"} "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT" --log=stdout >"$LOG" 2>&1 &
  pid=$!
  echo "$pid" > "$PIDFILE"
  url=""
  for i in $(seq 1 20); do
    kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || break
    url="$(agent_url || true)"
    [ -n "$url" ] && break
    sleep 2
  done
  if [ -z "$url" ]; then
    log "no address after 40s (agent tail: $(tail -c 300 "$LOG" 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' '))"
    kill "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
    rm -f "$PIDFILE"
    return 1
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$url"
}

trap 'log "stopped"; exit 0' TERM INT
log "keeper up (port $PORT; publishes .ngrok into the live session descriptor)"
install_ngrok || { log "ngrok download failed; retrying every loop"; }

LAST_URL="$(cat "$NGROK_URLFILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
FAILS=0
UNHEALTHY=0
while true; do
  sleep "$INTERVAL"
  install_ngrok || continue
  pid=""
  [ -f "$PIDFILE" ] && pid="$(tr -dc '0-9' < "$PIDFILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  if [ -n "${pid:-}" ] && kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
    url="$(agent_url || true)"
    if [ -n "$url" ] && healthy "$url"; then
      UNHEALTHY=0
      if [ "$url" != "$LAST_URL" ]; then
        echo "$url" > "$NGROK_URLFILE"
        LAST_URL="$url"
        log "ngrok address changed: $url - republishing"
        publish_full "$url" || true
      fi
      continue
    fi
    UNHEALTHY=$((UNHEALTHY + 1))
    if [ "$UNHEALTHY" -ge 3 ]; then
      log "ngrok leg unhealthy $UNHEALTHY probes in a row - restarting the agent"
      kill "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
      rm -f "$PIDFILE"
      UNHEALTHY=0
    fi
    continue
  fi
  url="$(start_agent || true)"
  case "$url" in https://*) ;; *) url="" ;; esac
  if [ -n "$url" ]; then
    FAILS=0
    echo "$url" > "$NGROK_URLFILE"
    if [ "$url" != "$LAST_URL" ]; then
      LAST_URL="$url"
      log "ngrok tunnel up: $url"
      publish_full "$url" || true
    else
      log "ngrok tunnel up (same address): $url"
    fi
  else
    FAILS=$((FAILS + 1))
    wait_s="$COOLDOWN"
    if [ "$FAILS" -ge "$FAILS_REST" ]; then wait_s=$((COOLDOWN * 30)); fi
    log "agent start failed #$FAILS; backing off ${wait_s}s (see ngrok.log)"
    sleep "$wait_s"
  fi
done

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Put a local HTTP port on the public internet with a Cloudflare quick tunnel.
#
# The URL printed by this script is usable only while the cloudflared process
# below is alive. A quick-tunnel hostname may appear in the log before the
# Cloudflare edge has a connector, so this script waits for a real HTTP answer
# and refuses to publish an Error 1033 page.
#
# Usage: open_tunnel.sh <local-port> [log-file]
# Prints one ready https URL on stdout, or nothing and exit 1.

set -uo pipefail

PORT="${1:?usage: open_tunnel.sh <local-port> [log]}"
case "$PORT" in
  ''|*[!0-9]*) echo "open_tunnel: invalid port: $PORT" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac
if [ "$PORT" -lt 1 ] || [ "$PORT" -gt 65535 ]; then
  echo "open_tunnel: invalid port: $PORT" >&2
  exit 1
fi

HUB_LOGS="${HUB_LOGS:-$HOME/.npm-hub/logs}"
HUB_TMP="${HUB_TMP:-$HOME/.npm-hub/tmp}"
mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS" "$HUB_TMP"
# A second tunnel on the SAME local port (the Z11 reserve address) passes
# TUNNEL_TAG=reserve: it gets its own pid/url/log files and skips the shared
# port-wide pkill, so maintaining the reserve never shoots the main tunnel.
TAG="${TUNNEL_TAG:-}"
LOG="${2:-$HUB_LOGS/cloudflared-$PORT${TAG:+-$TAG}.log}"
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$LOG")" 2>/dev/null || true
PIDFILE="$HUB_LOGS/cloudflared-$PORT${TAG:+-$TAG}.pid"
URLFILE="$HUB_LOGS/cloudflared-$PORT${TAG:+-$TAG}.url"
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# Kill only the connector for this origin. The bracket in the pattern keeps
# pkill from matching the shell that is executing this script. The pidfile is
# preferred because it cannot accidentally match another tunnel.
kill_old() {
  local old=""
  old="$(cat "$PIDFILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  if [ -n "$old" ] && kill -0 "$old" 2>/dev/null; then
    kill "$old" 2>/dev/null || true
    for _ in 1 2 3 4 5; do
      kill -0 "$old" 2>/dev/null || break
      sleep 1
    done
  fi
  rm -f "$PIDFILE" "$URLFILE"
  if [ -z "$TAG" ]; then
    pkill -f "cloudflared [t]unnel --url http://localhost:$PORT" 2>/dev/null || true
    pkill -f "cloudflared [t]unnel --url http://127[.]0[.]0[.]1:$PORT" 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
}
kill_old

if ! command -v cloudflared >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  download="$HUB_TMP/cloudflared.$$"
  if ! curl -fL --retry 3 --connect-timeout 15 -o "$download" \
      https://github.com/cloudflare/cloudflared/releases/latest/download/cloudflared-linux-amd64; then
    rm -f "$download"
    echo "open_tunnel: cloudflared download failed" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  chmod +x "$download"
  if sudo -n mv "$download" /usr/local/bin/cloudflared 2>/dev/null; then
    :
  else
    mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/bin"
    mv "$download" "$HOME/.local/bin/cloudflared"
    export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
  fi
fi

CF="$(command -v cloudflared 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [ -z "$CF" ] || [ ! -x "$CF" ]; then
  echo "open_tunnel: cloudflared is not executable" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# Use IPv4 explicitly. On some hosts localhost resolves to ::1 while the
# service listens only on IPv4; cloudflared then stays alive with a dead origin.
#
# --protocol http2 is deliberate and not cosmetic. cloudflared defaults to QUIC,
# which rides on UDP; on a cloud runner that UDP path is often throttled,
# blackholed or duplicated, and the symptom is precisely "the address stays the
# same but every WebSocket dies after half a minute". http2 runs over the same
# TCP the rest of the job already uses, so a tunnel drop now means the whole
# runner lost the network - which is the truth we want to see in a log.
nohup "$CF" tunnel --url "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT" \
  --protocol http2 --no-autoupdate --loglevel info >"$LOG" 2>&1 &
PID=$!
echo "$PID" > "$PIDFILE"

URL=""
# The quick-tunnel hostname normally appears in 10–20 seconds. Keep polling
# for up to 80 seconds, but stop immediately if the connector exits.
for _ in $(seq 1 40); do
  if ! kill -0 "$PID" 2>/dev/null; then
    if grep -qE '429|too many|rate.?limit' "$LOG" 2>/dev/null; then
      echo "open_tunnel: Cloudflare refused a new quick tunnel (HTTP 429 rate limit)" >&2
    else
      echo "open_tunnel: cloudflared exited before reporting an address" >&2
    fi
    tail -30 "$LOG" >&2 2>/dev/null || true
    rm -f "$PIDFILE" "$URLFILE"
    exit 1
  fi
  URL="$(grep -Eo 'https://[a-zA-Z0-9-]+[.]trycloudflare[.]com' "$LOG" 2>/dev/null | head -1 || true)"
  [ -n "$URL" ] && break
  sleep 2
done

if [ -z "$URL" ]; then
  echo "open_tunnel: no address after 80s" >&2
  tail -30 "$LOG" >&2 2>/dev/null || true
  kill "$PID" 2>/dev/null || true
  rm -f "$PIDFILE" "$URLFILE"
  exit 1
fi

# The hostname existing in DNS is not enough. Wait until a request reaches the
# origin; this is what prevents publishing the exact URL that shows Error 1033.
READY=0
for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
  if "$SCRIPT_DIR/tunnel_health.sh" "$URL" "/"; then
    READY=1
    break
  fi
  if ! kill -0 "$PID" 2>/dev/null; then break; fi
  sleep 2
done

if [ "$READY" != 1 ]; then
  echo "open_tunnel: Cloudflare edge never became ready (possible Error 1033)" >&2
  tail -30 "$LOG" >&2 2>/dev/null || true
  kill "$PID" 2>/dev/null || true
  rm -f "$PIDFILE" "$URLFILE"
  exit 1
fi

# after the health check and atomically so a concurrent reader never sees a
# half-written hostname.
printf '%s\n' "$URL" > "$URLFILE.tmp.$$"
mv -f "$URLFILE.tmp.$$" "$URLFILE"
printf '%s\n' "$URL"

1: #!/usr/bin/env bash
2: # Remote-control + heartbeat daemon for one runner VM (Z10 round 2).
3: #
4: # WHY ROUND 2
5: #   Round 1 proved the queue works, but run 175 showed it lives on the wrong
6: #   assumption: the workflow starts TWO VMs (hub web + VNC desktop) and the
7: #   hub VM's agent itself can die, taking every step with it while detached
8: #   daemons keep breathing. So now:
9: #     - BOTH VMs run this daemon, each with its own CONTROL_TARGET
10: #     - liveness is verifiable from outside: control/heartbeat-<vm>.json is
11: #       rewritten every 2 minutes with a process census
12: #     - this daemon can REPAIR, not only report: reopen-tunnel and up-hub fix
13: #       the exact failure mode of a dead cloudflared / dead hub server without
14: #       needing the job's keep-alive step at all
15: #
16: # CHANNEL (session-state branch)
17: #   control/queue.json             one slot: { seq, op, target?, from? }
18: #                                  target = hub | vnc | any (default any)
19: #   control/results/<seq>-<vm>.json per-VM ack
20: #   control/heartbeat-<vm>.json    liveness + process census every 2 min
21: #
22: # WHITELIST (never arbitrary shell)
23: #   ping, backup-now, handoff-save, restart-hub, up-hub, reopen-tunnel
24: set -uo pipefail
25: 
26: HUB_LOGS="${HUB_LOGS:-$HOME/.npm-hub/logs}"
27: mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS" 2>/dev/null || true
28: VM="${CONTROL_TARGET:-hub}"
29: log() { echo "[hub-control:$VM $(date -u '+%H:%M:%S')] $*" | tee -a "$HUB_LOGS/hub-control-$VM.log"; }
30: 
31: TOKEN="${GH_TOKEN:-${GITHUB_TOKEN:-}}"
32: if [ -z "$TOKEN" ]; then
33:   log "no token - the command queue stays cold"
34:   exit 1
35: fi
36: REPO="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:-sj0404-collab/zen-panel}"
37: BRANCH="${CONTROL_BRANCH:-session-state}"
38: INTERVAL="${CONTROL_INTERVAL:-20}"
39: HEARTBEAT_SEC="${CONTROL_HEARTBEAT_SEC:-120}"
40: API="https://api.github.com/repos/$REPO/contents"
41: QUEUE_PATH="control/queue.json"
42: SEEN_FILE="$HUB_LOGS/hub-control-$VM.seen"
43: SEEN="$(cat "$SEEN_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
44: TOOLS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
45: HUB_PORT="${HUB_PORT:-8090}"
46: 
47: trap 'log "stopped"; exit 0' TERM INT
48: 
49: api_get() {
50:   local body
51:   body="$(curl -sf -m 20 -H "Authorization: token $TOKEN" "$API/$1?ref=$BRANCH" 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
52:   echo "$body"
53: }
54: 
55: api_put() {
56:   local b64 sha
57:   b64="$(printf '%s' "$2" | base64 -w0)"
58:   sha="$(api_get "$1" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin).get("sha",""))' 2>/dev/null || echo)"
59:   if [ -n "$sha" ]; then
60:     curl -sf -m 25 -X PUT -H "Authorization: token $TOKEN" "$API/$1" \
61:       -d "{\"message\":\"control: ack $1\",\"content\":\"$b64\",\"branch\":\"$BRANCH\",\"sha\":\"$sha\"}" >/dev/null
62:   else
63:     curl -sf -m 25 -X PUT -H "Authorization: token $TOKEN" "$API/$1" \
64:       -d "{\"message\":\"control: ack $1\",\"content\":\"$b64\",\"branch\":\"$BRANCH\"}" >/dev/null
65:   fi
66: }
67: 
68: publish_url() {  # $1 = slot, $2 = new tunnel base url (no trailing slash)
69:   local slot="$1" base="$2" rv
70:   if [ "$slot" = "hub-linux" ]; then
71:     rv="$(cat "$HUB_LOGS/hub-url2" 2>/dev/null || true)"
72:     GH_TOKEN="$TOKEN" bash "$TOOLS_DIR/publish_session.sh" \
73:       "slot=hub-linux" "kind=NPM-Hub" "os=linux" \
74:       "url=$base" "hubUrl=$base" "desktop=$base/d" "mobile=$base/m" \
75:       ${rv:+"url2=$rv"} \
76:       "auth=без пароля" "label=${HUB_LABEL:-hub}" 2>&1 | tail -1
77:   else
78:     rv="$(cat "$HUB_LOGS/vnc-url2" 2>/dev/null || true)"
79:     GH_TOKEN="$TOKEN" bash "$TOOLS_DIR/publish_session.sh" \
80:       "slot=vnc" "kind=Linux-VNC" "os=linux" \
81:       "url=$base/vnc.html" "novncUrl=$base/vnc.html" \
82:       ${rv:+"url2=$rv"} \
83:       "label=${HUB_LABEL:-hub}" 2>&1 | tail -1
84:   fi
85: }
86: 
87: run_op() {
88:   local pid url
89:   case "$1" in
90:     ping)
91:       echo "pong from $VM $(date -Iseconds)"
92:       ;;
93:     backup-now)
94:       GH_TOKEN="$TOKEN" GITHUB_TOKEN="$TOKEN" WORK_BACKUP_ROOT="$HOME" \
95:         bash "$TOOLS_DIR/backup-work.sh" --once
96:       ;;
97:     restart-hub)
98:       pid="$(tr -dc '0-9' < "$HUB_LOGS/hub.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
99:       if [ -n "${pid:-}" ] && kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
100:         kill "$pid" && echo "hub pid $pid signalled"
101:       else
102:         echo "no live hub pid (already down?)"
103:       fi
104:       ;;
105:     up-hub)
106:       if [ "$VM" != "hub" ]; then echo "the npm-hub server lives on the hub VM not $VM"; return 0; fi
107:       pid="$(tr -dc '0-9' < "$HUB_LOGS/hub.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
108:       [ -n "${pid:-}" ] && kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null && { echo "hub already running (pid $pid)"; return 0; }
109:       (
110:         cd "$TOOLS_DIR/../npm-hub" || exit 1
111:         HUB_PORT_STRICT=1 HUB_TOKEN="${HUB_TOKEN_VALUE:-}" HUB_LABEL="${HUB_LABEL:-hub}" \
112:           GH_TOKEN="$TOKEN" PORT="$HUB_PORT" \
113:           SESSION_STARTED_MS="$(cat "$HOME/.npm-hub/session-start" 2>/dev/null || date +%s000)" \
114:           SESSION_LIMIT_MS=21600000 nohup node src/server.js >> "$HUB_LOGS/hub.log" 2>&1 &
115:         echo $! > "$HUB_LOGS/hub.pid"
116:       )
117:       sleep 2; echo "hub relaunched (pid $(cat "$HUB_LOGS/hub.pid" 2>/dev/null))"
118:       ;;
119:     reopen-tunnel)
120:       local port slot
121:       if [ "$VM" = "hub" ]; then port=8090; slot=hub-linux; else port=6081; slot=vnc; fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Remote-control + heartbeat daemon for one runner VM (Z10 round 2).
#
# WHY ROUND 2
#   Round 1 proved the queue works, but run 175 showed it lives on the wrong
#   assumption: the workflow starts TWO VMs (hub web + VNC desktop) and the
#   hub VM's agent itself can die, taking every step with it while detached
#   daemons keep breathing. So now:
#     - BOTH VMs run this daemon, each with its own CONTROL_TARGET
#     - liveness is verifiable from outside: control/heartbeat-<vm>.json is
#       rewritten every 2 minutes with a process census
#     - this daemon can REPAIR, not only report: reopen-tunnel and up-hub fix
#       the exact failure mode of a dead cloudflared / dead hub server without
#       needing the job's keep-alive step at all
#
# CHANNEL (session-state branch)
#   control/queue.json             one slot: { seq, op, target?, from? }
#                                  target = hub | vnc | any (default any)
#   control/results/<seq>-<vm>.json per-VM ack
#   control/heartbeat-<vm>.json    liveness + process census every 2 min

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Remote-control + heartbeat daemon for one runner VM (Z10 round 2).
#
# WHY ROUND 2
#   Round 1 proved the queue works, but run 175 showed it lives on the wrong
#   assumption: the workflow starts TWO VMs (hub web + VNC desktop) and the
#   hub VM's agent itself can die, taking every step with it while detached
#   daemons keep breathing. So now:
#     - BOTH VMs run this daemon, each with its own CONTROL_TARGET
#     - liveness is verifiable from outside: control/heartbeat-<vm>.json is
#       rewritten every 2 minutes with a process census
#     - this daemon can REPAIR, not only report: reopen-tunnel and up-hub fix
#       the exact failure mode of a dead cloudflared / dead hub server without
#       needing the job's keep-alive step at all
#
# CHANNEL (session-state branch)
#   control/queue.json             one slot: { seq, op, target?, from? }
#                                  target = hub | vnc | any (default any)
#   control/results/<seq>-<vm>.json per-VM ack
#   control/heartbeat-<vm>.json    liveness + process census every 2 min
#
# WHITELIST (never arbitrary shell)
#   ping, backup-now, handoff-save, restart-hub, up-hub, reopen-tunnel
set -uo pipefail

HUB_LOGS="${HUB_LOGS:-$HOME/.npm-hub/logs}"
mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS" 2>/dev/null || true
VM="${CONTROL_TARGET:-hub}"
log() { echo "[hub-control:$VM $(date -u '+%H:%M:%S')] $*" | tee -a "$HUB_LOGS/hub-control-$VM.log"; }

TOKEN="${GH_TOKEN:-${GITHUB_TOKEN:-}}"
if [ -z "$TOKEN" ]; then
  log "no token - the command queue stays cold"
  exit 1
fi
REPO="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:-sj0404-collab/zen-panel}"
BRANCH="${CONTROL_BRANCH:-session-state}"
INTERVAL="${CONTROL_INTERVAL:-20}"
HEARTBEAT_SEC="${CONTROL_HEARTBEAT_SEC:-120}"
API="https://api.github.com/repos/$REPO/contents"
QUEUE_PATH="control/queue.json"
SEEN_FILE="$HUB_LOGS/hub-control-$VM.seen"
SEEN="$(cat "$SEEN_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
TOOLS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
HUB_PORT="${HUB_PORT:-8090}"

trap 'log "stopped"; exit 0' TERM INT

api_get() {
  local body
  body="$(curl -sf -m 20 -H "Authorization: token $TOKEN" "$API/$1?ref=$BRANCH" 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
  echo "$body"
}

api_put() {
  local b64 sha
  b64="$(printf '%s' "$2" | base64 -w0)"
  sha="$(api_get "$1" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin).get("sha",""))' 2>/dev/null || echo)"
  if [ -n "$sha" ]; then
    curl -sf -m 25 -X PUT -H "Authorization: token $TOKEN" "$API/$1" \
      -d "{\"message\":\"control: ack $1\",\"content\":\"$b64\",\"branch\":\"$BRANCH\",\"sha\":\"$sha\"}" >/dev/null
  else
    curl -sf -m 25 -X PUT -H "Authorization: token $TOKEN" "$API/$1" \
      -d "{\"message\":\"control: ack $1\",\"content\":\"$b64\",\"branch\":\"$BRANCH\"}" >/dev/null
  fi
}

publish_url() {  # $1 = slot, $2 = new tunnel base url (no trailing slash)
  local slot="$1" base="$2" rv
  if [ "$slot" = "hub-linux" ]; then
    rv="$(cat "$HUB_LOGS/hub-url2" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    GH_TOKEN="$TOKEN" bash "$TOOLS_DIR/publish_session.sh" \
      "slot=hub-linux" "kind=NPM-Hub" "os=linux" \
      "url=$base" "hubUrl=$base" "desktop=$base/d" "mobile=$base/m" \
      ${rv:+"url2=$rv"} \
      "auth=без пароля" "label=${HUB_LABEL:-hub}" 2>&1 | tail -1
  else
    rv="$(cat "$HUB_LOGS/vnc-url2" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    GH_TOKEN="$TOKEN" bash "$TOOLS_DIR/publish_session.sh" \
      "slot=vnc" "kind=Linux-VNC" "os=linux" \
      "url=$base/vnc.html" "novncUrl=$base/vnc.html" \
      ${rv:+"url2=$rv"} \
      "label=${HUB_LABEL:-hub}" 2>&1 | tail -1
  fi
}

run_op() {
  local pid url
  case "$1" in
    ping)
      echo "pong from $VM $(date -Iseconds)"
      ;;
    backup-now)
      GH_TOKEN="$TOKEN" GITHUB_TOKEN="$TOKEN" WORK_BACKUP_ROOT="$HOME" \
        bash "$TOOLS_DIR/backup-work.sh" --once
      ;;
    restart-hub)
      pid="$(tr -dc '0-9' < "$HUB_LOGS/hub.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
      if [ -n "${pid:-}" ] && kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
        kill "$pid" && echo "hub pid $pid signalled"
      else
        echo "no live hub pid (already down?)"
      fi
      ;;
    up-hub)
      if [ "$VM" != "hub" ]; then echo "the npm-hub server lives on the hub VM not $VM"; return 0; fi
      pid="$(tr -dc '0-9' < "$HUB_LOGS/hub.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
      [ -n "${pid:-}" ] && kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null && { echo "hub already running (pid $pid)"; return 0; }
      (
        cd "$TOOLS_DIR/../npm-hub" || exit 1
        HUB_PORT_STRICT=1 HUB_TOKEN="${HUB_TOKEN_VALUE:-}" HUB_LABEL="${HUB_LABEL:-hub}" \
          GH_TOKEN="$TOKEN" PORT="$HUB_PORT" \
          SESSION_STARTED_MS="$(cat "$HOME/.npm-hub/session-start" 2>/dev/null || date +%s000)" \
          SESSION_LIMIT_MS=21600000 nohup node src/server.js >> "$HUB_LOGS/hub.log" 2>&1 &
        echo $! > "$HUB_LOGS/hub.pid"
      )
      sleep 2; echo "hub relaunched (pid $(cat "$HUB_LOGS/hub.pid" 2>/dev/null))"
      ;;
    reopen-tunnel)
      local port slot
      if [ "$VM" = "hub" ]; then port=8090; slot=hub-linux; else port=6081; slot=vnc; fi
      pid="$(tr -dc '0-9' < "$HUB_LOGS/cloudflared-$port.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
      [ -n "${pid:-}" ] && kill "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
      pkill -f "cloudflared [t]unnel --url http://127.0.0.1:$port" 2>/dev/null || true
      sleep 1
      url="$(bash "$TOOLS_DIR/open_tunnel.sh" "$port" "$HUB_LOGS/control-tunnel.log" 2>/dev/null || echo)"
      if [ -z "$url" ]; then echo "open_tunnel gave no URL"; return 1; fi
      [ "$VM" = "hub" ] && echo "$url" > "$HUB_LOGS/hub-url" || echo "$url" > "$HUB_LOGS/vnc-url"
      echo "tunnel up: $url"
      publish_url "$slot" "$url"
      ;;
    handoff-save)
      [ "$VM" = "hub" ] || { echo "handoff-save runs on the hub VM"; return 0; }
      GH_TOKEN="$TOKEN" GITHUB_TOKEN="$TOKEN" WORK_BACKUP_ROOT="$HOME" \
        bash "$TOOLS_DIR/handoff.sh"
      ;;
    *)
      echo "unknown op: $1" >&2
      return 64
      ;;
  esac
}

heartbeat() {
  local hb
  hb="$(python3 - <<PYH 2>/dev/null || echo ""
import json, subprocess, datetime
def pc(pat):
    try:
        return subprocess.run(["pgrep","-fc",pat], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10).stdout.strip()
    except Exception:
        return "?"
print(json.dumps({
    "vm": "$VM", "runId": "${GITHUB_RUN_ID:-local}",
    "at": datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"),
    "procs": {
        "hub_server": pc("node src/server.js"),
        "cloudflared": pc("cloudflared [t]unnel"),
        "backup_daemon": pc("[b]ackup-work.sh"),
        "snapshot_daemon": pc("[s]napshot-audit-code.sh"),
        "control_daemon": pc("[h]ub_control.sh"),
        "rescue_ssh": pc("[r]escue_ssh.sh"),
        "tunnel_keeper": pc("[t]unnel_keeper.sh"),
        "ngrok_keeper": pc("[n]grok_keeper.sh"),
    },
}, ensure_ascii=False))
PYH
)"
  [ -n "$hb" ] && api_put "control/heartbeat-$VM.json" "$hb" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
}

log "queue daemon up ($VM) on $BRANCH:$QUEUE_PATH (every ${INTERVAL}s; seen=$SEEN)"
boot_slot="$(api_get "$QUEUE_PATH" || true)"
if [ -n "$boot_slot" ]; then
  boot_seq="$(python3 -c 'import json,sys,base64; print(json.loads(base64.b64decode(json.load(sys.stdin)["content"])).get("seq",0))' <<<"$boot_slot" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
  if [[ "$boot_seq" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [ "$boot_seq" -gt "$SEEN" ] 2>/dev/null; then
    SEEN="$boot_seq"; echo "$SEEN" > "$SEEN_FILE"
    log "queue baseline set to #$SEEN (stale command - not executing)"
  fi
fi
heartbeat
LAST_BEAT=$SECONDS
while true; do
  sleep "$INTERVAL"
  if [ $((SECONDS - LAST_BEAT)) -ge "$HEARTBEAT_SEC" ]; then
    heartbeat; LAST_BEAT=$SECONDS
  fi
  slot="$(api_get "$QUEUE_PATH" || true)"
  [ -n "$slot" ] || continue
  read -r seq op target < <(python3 -c '
import json, sys
try:
    d = json.loads(sys.stdin.read())
    print(int(d.get("seq", 0)), str(d.get("op", ""))[:64], str(d.get("target", "any"))[:16])
except Exception:
    print(0, "", "any")
' <<<"$(python3 -c 'import json,sys,base64; c=json.load(sys.stdin)["content"]; print(base64.b64decode(c).decode(), end="")' <<<"$slot" 2>/dev/null)" 2>/dev/null || echo "0  any")
  [[ "$seq" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || continue
  [ "$seq" -le "$SEEN" ] 2>/dev/null && continue
  [ -n "$op" ] || continue
  { [ "$target" = "any" ] || [ "$target" = "$VM" ]; } || { log "skip #$seq ($op for target=$target)"; echo "$seq" > "$SEEN_FILE"; SEEN="$seq"; continue; }
  log "command #$seq: $op (target=$target)"
  out="$(run_op "$op" 2>&1 | tail -c 3000)"; rc=$?
  log "command #$seq rc=$rc"
  ack="$(python3 -c '
import json, sys, datetime
print(json.dumps({
    "seq": int(sys.argv[1]), "op": sys.argv[2], "vm": sys.argv[4],
    "ok": sys.argv[3] == "0", "rc": int(sys.argv[3]),
    "at": datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"),
    "runId": sys.argv[5],
    "out": sys.stdin.read()[-2800:],
}, ensure_ascii=False))
' "$seq" "$op" "$rc" "$VM" "${GITHUB_RUN_ID:-local}" <<<"$out" 2>/dev/null || echo "{\"seq\":$seq,\"ok\":false}")"
  if api_put "control/results/$seq-$VM.json" "$ack"; then
    echo "$seq" > "$SEEN_FILE"; SEEN="$seq"
  else
    log "ack push failed - the command WILL rerun until pushed"
  fi
done

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Return success only when a public tunnel reaches the local service.
# Cloudflare can resolve a quick-tunnel hostname before a connector is ready;
# that page is HTTP 530 / Error 1033 and must not be treated as healthy.
set -uo pipefail

URL="${1:?usage: tunnel_health.sh <url> [path]}"
PATH_SUFFIX="${2:-/}"
case "$PATH_SUFFIX" in
  /*) ;;
  *) PATH_SUFFIX="/$PATH_SUFFIX" ;;
esac

TMP_DIR="${HUB_TMP:-${HOME:-/tmp}/.npm-hub/tmp}"
mkdir -p "$TMP_DIR" 2>/dev/null || TMP_DIR="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}"
BODY="$TMP_DIR/tunnel-probe.$$"
trap 'rm -f "$BODY"' EXIT

code=$(curl -sS -L --max-time "${TUNNEL_PROBE_TIMEOUT:-15}" \
  -A 'zen-panel-tunnel-health/1' -o "$BODY" -w '%{http_code}' \
  "${URL%/}${PATH_SUFFIX}" 2>/dev/null || true)

# A 401/403/404 proves that the request crossed the tunnel and reached the
# application. A 5xx, or a page mentioning 1033, means the connector is dead.
if grep -Eqi '(^|[^0-9])1033([^0-9]|$)|error[[:space:]]*code[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*1033' "$BODY" 2>/dev/null; then
  exit 1
fi
case "$code" in
  2*|3*|4*) exit 0 ;;
  *) exit 1 ;;
esac

          rm -rf "$STATE_DIR"
          STATE_REMOTE="https://x-access-token:${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}@github.com/${{ github.repository }}.git"
          if ! git clone -q --depth 1 --filter=blob:limit=1m --branch session-state \
               "$STATE_REMOTE" "$STATE_DIR" 2>/dev/null; then
            if ! git clone -q --depth 1 --branch session-state \
                 "$STATE_REMOTE" "$STATE_DIR" 2>/dev/null; then
              STATE_DIR=""
              echo "::notice::no session-state branch yet; starting without the saved history"
            fi
          fi
          # Restore repos before importing OpenCode sessions: opencode import
          # needs the real repository CWD, not an empty placeholder folder.
          # The fork's own history does not depend on that restore, so the two
          # run together; the hub-work chats import below waits for the repos,
          # and runs after the fork restore so the two never copy the same
          # opencode bundle at the same time.
          # Repo restore is opt-in from the hub's Snapshot tab now: pulling the
          # whole work-backup copy BEFORE the tunnel publishes cost the connect
          # page ~4 of the user's minutes at every launch. The script sees
          # WORK_BACKUP_RESTORE=0 and exits at once; everything else in this
          # step (audit/code, chat bundles) is small and stays.
          GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" WORK_BACKUP_ROOT="$HOME" \
            WORK_BACKUP_RESTORE=0 WORK_BACKUP_RESTORE_EXISTING=1 bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/restore-work.sh" \
            2>&1 | tee -a "$HUB_LOGS/restore-work.log" &
          WORK_PID=$!
          GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" STATE_DIR="$STATE_DIR" \
            bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/restore_audit_code.sh" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork" 2>&1 | tee -a "$HUB_LOGS/restore.log" || echo "::warning::fork restore failed"
          wait "$WORK_PID" || echo "::warning::hub-work restore failed"
          # Restore-chats imports the zen-panel fork only by default; the
          # hub-work call gets RESTORE_CHATS_ALL=1 so every repo the Files tab
          # cloned (and the fork itself) gets its opencode sessions back.
          RESTORE_CHATS_ALL=1 RESTORE_CHATS_ROOT="$HOME" \
            GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" STATE_DIR="$STATE_DIR" \
            bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/restore_audit_code.sh" "$HOME/hub-work" 2>&1 | tee -a "$HUB_LOGS/restore-hubwork.log" || echo "::warning::hub-work chats restore failed"
          rm -rf "$STATE_DIR"

      - name: Start the hub and open the tunnel
        env:
          NGROK_AUTHTOKEN: ${{ secrets.NGROK_AUTHTOKEN }}
        run: |
          export HUB_LOGS="$HOME/.npm-hub/logs"; mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS" 2>/dev/null || true
          echo "HUB_LOGS=$HUB_LOGS HOME=$HOME $(ls -ld "$HUB_LOGS" 2>&1)"
          cd "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/npm-hub"
          export HUB_LOGS="$HOME/.npm-hub/logs"; mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS" 2>/dev/null || true
          HUB_PORT=8090
          HUB_TOKEN_VALUE='${{ inputs.token }}'
          HUB_PID_FILE="$HUB_LOGS/hub.pid"
          if [ -f "$HUB_PID_FILE" ]; then
            OLD_PID="$(tr -dc '0-9' < "$HUB_PID_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            if [ -n "$OLD_PID" ] && kill -0 "$OLD_PID" 2>/dev/null \
              && tr '\0' ' ' < "/proc/$OLD_PID/cmdline" 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'src/server.js'; then
              kill "$OLD_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
            fi
          fi
          pkill -f "cloudflared [t]unnel --url http://127.0.0.1:$HUB_PORT" 2>/dev/null || true
          for i in $(seq 1 15); do
            curl -sf -m 2 "http://127.0.0.1:$HUB_PORT/api/tools" >/dev/null 2>&1 || break
            sleep 1
          done
          hub_ready() {
            local body
            body="$(curl -sf -m 15 -H "x-hub-token: $HUB_TOKEN_VALUE" "http://127.0.0.1:$HUB_PORT/api/tools" 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
            echo "$body" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); raise SystemExit(0 if str(d.get("runId", "")) == sys.argv[1] else 1)' "$GITHUB_RUN_ID"
          }
          SESSION_FILE="$HOME/.npm-hub/session-start"
          date +%s000 > "$SESSION_FILE"
          HUB_PORT_STRICT=1 HUB_TOKEN="$HUB_TOKEN_VALUE" HUB_LABEL='${{ inputs.label }}' GH_TOKEN='${{ inputs.gh_token }}' PORT="$HUB_PORT" SESSION_STARTED_MS="$(cat "$SESSION_FILE")" SESSION_LIMIT_MS=21600000 nohup node src/server.js > "$HUB_LOGS/hub.log" 2>&1 &
          HUB_PID=$!
          echo "$HUB_PID" > "$HUB_PID_FILE"
          for i in $(seq 1 60); do
            hub_ready && break
            sleep 2
          done
          if ! hub_ready; then
            echo "::error::the hub did not start for run $GITHUB_RUN_ID."
            tail -40 "$HUB_LOGS/hub.log"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "hub is up on $HUB_PORT for run $GITHUB_RUN_ID"
          # Start audit/code snapshot daemon (audit.json = chat, code.json = diff + sessions), plus chats for every repo
          export SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL=120
          # Also keep chats/<name>.json for every repo fresh every ~20 min,
          # so an interrupted runner still hands sessions to the next one.
          export SNAPSHOT_EXPORT_ALL_CHATS=1
          nohup env GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" GITHUB_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/snapshot-audit-code.sh" hub "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork" > "$HUB_LOGS/snapshot-hub.log" 2>&1 &
          echo $! > "$HUB_LOGS/snapshot.pid"
          echo "snapshot daemon: audit.json + code.json every 120s -> session-state"
          # Durable work backup: every repo under HOME becomes a git bundle plus
          # its WIP diff and untracked files on the work-backup branch, so a
          # runner that dies with unpushed work loses nothing.
          nohup env GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" GITHUB_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" WORK_BACKUP_ROOT="$HOME" WORK_BACKUP_INTERVAL=300 bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/backup-work.sh" >> "$HUB_LOGS/work-backup.log" 2>&1 &
          echo $! > "$HUB_LOGS/work-backup.pid"
          echo "work-backup daemon: HOME snapshot every 300s -> work-backup branch"
          # Rescue channels (they outlive the hub web stack): a tmate SSH/web
          # shell and a whitelisted command queue on the session-state branch -
          # so a runner with a dead hub and a dead tunnel stays steerable from
          # GitHub alone instead of being a closed box until the 6h cap.
          if [ "${{ inputs.rescue_ssh }}" = "true" ]; then
            GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" GITHUB_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" CONTROL_TARGET=hub \
              nohup bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/rescue_ssh.sh" >> "$HUB_LOGS/rescue-ssh.log" 2>&1 &
            echo $! > "$HUB_LOGS/rescue-ssh.pid"
            echo "rescue ssh daemon: tmate shell published -> control/rescue-hub.json"
          fi
          if [ "${{ inputs.command_queue }}" = "true" ]; then
            GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" GITHUB_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" CONTROL_TARGET=hub \
              HUB_TOKEN_VALUE='${{ inputs.token }}' HUB_LABEL='${{ inputs.label }}' \
              nohup bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/hub_control.sh" >> "$HUB_LOGS/hub-control.log" 2>&1 &
            echo $! > "$HUB_LOGS/hub-control.pid"
            echo "control daemon (hub VM): control/queue.json + heartbeat; ops: ping, backup-now, restart-hub, up-hub, reopen-tunnel, handoff-save"
          fi

          URL=$(bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/open_tunnel.sh" 8090 $HUB_LOGS/tunnel.log)
          if [ -z "$URL" ]; then
            echo "::error::no tunnel came up."
            tail -25 $HUB_LOGS/tunnel.log
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "$URL" > $HUB_LOGS/hub-url

          TOOLS=$(python3 -c "
          import json, urllib.request
          try:
              _zt = urllib.request.Request('http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/tools', headers={'x-hub-token': '${{ inputs.token }}'})
              d = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(_zt, timeout=10))
              names = [t['name'] for t in d.get('tools', []) if t.get('installed')]
          except Exception:
              names = []
          print(', '.join(names) if names else 'none detected')
          ")
          MODELS=$(python3 -c "
          import json, urllib.request
          try:
              _zt = urllib.request.Request('http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/models/full', headers={'x-hub-token': '${{ inputs.token }}'})
              d = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(_zt, timeout=20))
              ms = d.get('models', [])
              print('%d (%d free)' % (len(ms), sum(1 for m in ms if m.get('free'))))
          except Exception:
              print('n/a')
          ")

          {
            echo "## NPM Hub"
            echo ""
            echo "**[Open the hub]($URL)** - no password, pick Desktop or Mobile."
            echo ""
            echo "| | |"
            echo "|---|---|"
            echo "| Address | \`$URL\` |"
            echo "| Desktop | \`$URL/d\` |"
            echo "| Mobile | \`$URL/m\` |"
            echo "| CLI agents | $TOOLS |"
            echo "| Models | $MODELS |"
            echo "| Label | \`${{ inputs.label }}\` |"
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

          echo "=================================================="
          echo " Hub: $URL"
          echo " Tools: $TOOLS"
          echo "=================================================="

          GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" \
            bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" \
              "slot=hub-linux" "kind=NPM-Hub" "os=linux" \
              "url=$URL" "hubUrl=$URL" "desktop=$URL/d" "mobile=$URL/m" \
              $([ -s "$HUB_LOGS/hub-url2" ] && echo "url2=$(cat "$HUB_LOGS/hub-url2")") \
              "auth=без пароля" "tools=$TOOLS" \
              "label=${{ inputs.label }}"

          # Z11 dual tunnel: a warm reserve address per endpoint + main-tunnel
          # resurrection that does not depend on the keep-alive step staying
          # alive (measured on run 175: hub VM wedged, watchdog with it).
          nohup env GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" GITHUB_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" HUB_LABEL='${{ inputs.label }}' \
            bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/tunnel_keeper.sh" hub >> "$HUB_LOGS/tunnel-keeper.log" 2>&1 &
          echo $! > "$HUB_LOGS/tunnel-keeper.pid"
          echo "tunnel keeper: hub endpoint now carries main + reserve addresses"

          # ngrok third leg: an INDEPENDENT provider address, published into the
          # live session descriptor as .ngrok (run 376: one trycloudflare
          # address died mid-session and the phone went offline on a perfectly
          # healthy hub - a different provider keeps serving through that).
          if [ -n "${NGROK_AUTHTOKEN:-}" ]; then
            nohup env GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" GITHUB_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" HUB_LABEL='${{ inputs.label }}' \
              NGROK_AUTHTOKEN="$NGROK_AUTHTOKEN" \
              bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/ngrok_keeper.sh" hub >> "$HUB_LOGS/ngrok-keeper.log" 2>&1 &
            echo $! > "$HUB_LOGS/ngrok-keeper.pid"
            echo "ngrok keeper: hub endpoint now also carries a provider-independent address"
          else
            echo "::notice::NGROK_AUTHTOKEN secret is empty - the ngrok reserve leg is off"
          fi

      - name: Start the autopilot for every repo the Files tab cloned
        run: |
          # THIS IS THE STEP THE HUB WAS MISSING. The hub clones the user's
          # repositories into ~/hub-work and the agent edits them there, but
          # hub.yml deliberately had no autosave ("it edits nothing by itself"),
          # so work done in a hub session only survived as a snapshot and
          # reached the remote only when somebody remembered to push. The panel
          # showed a runner that looked alive and produced nothing.
          #
          # One autopilot per repository: yomikai and zen-panel share neither a
          # history, nor a base branch, nor a test suite, so a single
          # repo-wide daemon would push one into the other.
          set -u
          AUTOSHIP="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/auto-ship.sh"
          mkdir -p "$HOME/.npm-hub/logs" 2>/dev/null || true
          chmod +x "$AUTOSHIP" 2>/dev/null || true
          ROOT="${HUB_WORK_DIR:-$HOME/hub-work}"
          started=0
          for gitdir in $(find "$ROOT" -maxdepth 4 -type d -name .git 2>/dev/null); do
            repo="$(dirname "$gitdir")"
            remote="$(git -C "$repo" remote get-url origin 2>/dev/null || true)"
            [ -n "$remote" ] || continue
            # Each repo's own default branch is its base. Hardcoding `main`
            # would open PRs into branches that do not exist in some repos.
            base="$(git -C "$repo" symbolic-ref --short "refs/remotes/origin/HEAD" 2>/dev/null | sed 's|^origin/||')"
            [ -n "$base" ] || base="main"
            owner="$(basename "$(dirname "$remote")")"
            name="$(printf '%s-%s' "$owner" "$(basename "$repo")" | tr -c 'A-Za-z0-9._-' '_')"
            echo "autopilot: $repo -> $base (log: ~/.npm-hub/logs/auto-ship-$name.log)"
            nohup env \
              HUB_LOGS="$HOME/.npm-hub/logs" \
              GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" \
              GITHUB_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" \
              AUTOSHIP_REPO="$repo" \
              AUTOSHIP_BASE="$base" \
              AUTOSHIP_INTERVAL=180 \
              bash "$AUTOSHIP" >"$HOME/.npm-hub/logs/auto-ship-$name.log" 2>&1 &
            started=$((started + 1))
          done
          if [ "$started" = 0 ]; then
            echo "::warning::no repository with a remote under $ROOT - nothing to autopilot"
          else
            echo "autopilot running for $started repo(s): commit -> push -> PR -> merge (never red)"
          fi

      - name: Keep the session alive
        run: |
          export HUB_LOGS="$HOME/.npm-hub/logs"
          mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS"
          HUB_PORT=8090
          HUB_TOKEN_VALUE='${{ inputs.token }}'
          HUB_PID_FILE="$HUB_LOGS/hub.pid"
          PIDFILE="$HUB_LOGS/cloudflared-8090.pid"
          hub_ready() {
            local body
            body="$(curl -sf -m 20 -H "x-hub-token: $HUB_TOKEN_VALUE" "http://127.0.0.1:$HUB_PORT/api/tools" 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
            echo "$body" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); raise SystemExit(0 if str(d.get("runId", "")) == sys.argv[1] else 1)' "$GITHUB_RUN_ID"
          }
          cleanup_watchdog() {
            local code="${1:-143}"
            trap - TERM INT
            # The two daemons below are `while true; do sleep ...` loops with no
            # trap of their own, and the runner waits for every process in the
            # job before it can close the step. Leaving them alive made
            # "Complete job" hang for ~45 minutes after a cancel - and the job
            # was recorded as `failure` instead of `cancelled`. Bracket
            # patterns: a plain one matches this shell's own command line.
            pkill -f "[s]napshot-audit-code.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
            pkill -f "[b]ackup-work.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
            # The rescue daemons below are detached background loops too - same
            # "Complete job" hang trap, same bracket-pattern kill.
            pkill -f "[h]ub_control.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
            pkill -f "[r]escue_ssh.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
            pkill -f "[t]unnel_keeper.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
            rm -f "$HUB_LOGS/cloudflared-8090-reserve.pid" 2>/dev/null || true
            tmate -S "$HUB_LOGS/tmate.sock" kill-session >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
            if [ -n "${HUB_PID:-}" ]; then kill "$HUB_PID" 2>/dev/null || true; fi
            if [ -f "$PIDFILE" ]; then
              local pid; pid="$(tr -dc '0-9' < "$PIDFILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
              [ -z "$pid" ] || kill "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
            fi
            pkill -f "cloudflared [t]unnel --url http://127.0.0.1:$HUB_PORT" 2>/dev/null || true
            # A cancelled run never reaches its `if: always()` steps - GitHub
            # stops the job right here - so the published session kept saying
            # "live" and the panel handed out a tunnel that is already dead.
            # Close the slot from the trap instead, after the writers above
            # are gone so the ended marker cannot race them.
            GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" \
              bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" "slot=hub-linux" "state=ended" \
              >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
            exit "$code"
          }
          trap 'cleanup_watchdog 143' TERM INT
          # Watch the hub and the tunnel instead of sleeping blindly: a dead
          # hub behind a live tunnel answers 502, and a dead tunnel keeps
          # resolving - both look like "the address is there but nothing
          # opens". Either one is restarted here; a new tunnel address is
          # republished so the panel never points at a corpse.
          HUBDIR="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/npm-hub"
