HUBDIR="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/npm-hub"
          # open_tunnel.sh writes the pid under $HUB_LOGS (~/.npm-hub/logs/);
          # reading those paths is what lets the watchdog verify the tunnel
          # instead of re-opening it every loop (the /tmp path never existed
          # -> the tunnel was declared dead every ~90s and reconnected
          # endlessly).
          RESTARTING=0
          FAILS=0
          HUB_PID="$(tr -dc '0-9' < "$HUB_PID_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
          for i in $(seq 1 1400); do
            sleep 15
            # The session relay wrote this marker right before it exited: the
            # work is saved and the next runner has published itself. Restarting
            # the hub now would resurrect the runner we just handed over, so the
            # watchdog ends the job cleanly instead.
            if [ -f "$HUB_LOGS/handoff-done" ]; then
              echo "handoff complete - the session lives on the next runner now."
              cleanup_watchdog 0
            fi
            # One missed probe is NOT a dead hub: the box saturates its CPU
            # launching a game / a build and a 10s curl can legitimately bleed
            # over. Only restart after several consecutive misses, so a single
            # spike doesn't kill the hub and drop every attached tab.
            if hub_ready; then
              FAILS=0
            else
              FAILS=$((FAILS + 1))
              echo "::warning::hub probe missed ($FAILS consecutive)."
            fi
            if [ "$FAILS" -ge 3 ] && [ "$RESTARTING" = "0" ]; then
              echo "::warning::hub stopped answering ($FAILS misses); restarting it."
              RESTARTING=1
              # Brackets, not a plain string: pkill -f matches its own
              # parent shell's command line too, and a plain pattern is
              # suicide - measured the hard way.
              if [ -n "${HUB_PID:-}" ]; then kill "$HUB_PID" 2>/dev/null || true; fi
              cd "$HUBDIR"
              SESSION_STARTED_MS="$(cat "$HOME/.npm-hub/session-start" 2>/dev/null || date +%s000)"
              HUB_PORT_STRICT=1 HUB_TOKEN="$HUB_TOKEN_VALUE" HUB_LABEL='${{ inputs.label }}' GH_TOKEN='${{ inputs.gh_token }}' PORT="$HUB_PORT" SESSION_STARTED_MS="$SESSION_STARTED_MS" SESSION_LIMIT_MS=21600000 nohup node src/server.js >> "$HUB_LOGS/hub.log" 2>&1 &
              HUB_PID=$!
              echo "$HUB_PID" > "$HUB_PID_FILE"
              # Wait for the new hub to serve again before probing it for
              # "dead": otherwise the first check hits it mid-boot and the
              # watchdog loops on itself forever.
              for boot in $(seq 1 12); do
                if hub_ready; then
                  FAILS=0; RESTARTING=0
                  echo "::warning::hub is back."
                  break
                fi
                sleep 5
              done
              # Boot wait exhausted: release the restart lock so a hub that
              # really died at boot is tried again (otherwise the watchdog
              # locks itself out and never recovers).
              if [ "$RESTARTING" = "1" ]; then
                echo "::warning::hub did not come back; a later restart will retry."
                RESTARTING=0; FAILS=0
              fi
            fi
            CUR=$(cat $HUB_LOGS/hub-url 2>/dev/null || echo)
            PID=$(cat "$PIDFILE" 2>/dev/null || echo)
            EDGE=""
            if [ -n "$PID" ] && kill -0 "$PID" 2>/dev/null && [ -n "$CUR" ] \
              && bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/tunnel_health.sh" "$CUR" "/"; then
              EDGE=1
            fi
            if [ -n "$EDGE" ]; then continue; fi
            # Drop the stale cloudflared before a fresh one takes the port:
            # stacking instances leaks processes and burns tunnel names.
            # Bracket pattern - a plain "cloudflared tunnel..." match is
            # suicide against this shell's own command line.
            if [ -n "$PID" ] && kill -0 "$PID" 2>/dev/null; then kill "$PID" 2>/dev/null || true; fi
            pkill -f "cloudflared [t]unnel --url http://127.0.0.1:8090" 2>/dev/null || true
            sleep 1
            echo "::warning::tunnel dead; reopening."
            URL=$(bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/open_tunnel.sh" 8090 $HUB_LOGS/tunnel2.log) || continue
            [ -n "$URL" ] || continue
            echo "$URL" > $HUB_LOGS/hub-url
            echo "back up on $URL"
            GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" \
              bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" \
                "slot=hub-linux" "kind=NPM-Hub" "os=linux" \
                "url=$URL" "hubUrl=$URL" "desktop=$URL/d" "mobile=$URL/m" \
                $([ -s "$HUB_LOGS/hub-url2" ] && echo "url2=$(cat "$HUB_LOGS/hub-url2")") \
                "auth=без пароля" "label=${{ inputs.label }}"
          done
          cleanup_watchdog 0

      - name: Final durable repository and session backup
        if: always()
        timeout-minutes: 6
        run: |
          export HUB_LOGS="$HOME/.npm-hub/logs"; mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS" 2>/dev/null || true
          GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" WORK_BACKUP_ROOT="$HOME" \
            bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/backup-work.sh" --once \
            2>&1 | tee -a "$HUB_LOGS/work-backup.log"

      - name: Clear the published session
        if: always()
        run: |
          GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" \
            bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" "slot=hub-linux" "state=ended"

      - name: Snapshot audit/code on exit
        if: always()
        run: |
          export HUB_LOGS="$HOME/.npm-hub/logs"; mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS" 2>/dev/null || true
          # --once always exports this repo's chats; SNAPSHOT_EXPORT_ALL_CHATS=1
          # additionally exports chats/<name>.json for every repo under $HOME.
          GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" GITHUB_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" SNAPSHOT_EXPORT_ALL_CHATS=1 \
            bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/snapshot-audit-code.sh" --once hub "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork" 2>&1 | tee -a "$HUB_LOGS/snapshot-hub.log"

      - name: Save the models snapshot
        if: always()
        run: |
          # Whatever the live registry learned before shutdown, in one small
          # object the panel renders as a line. The hub may already be dead
          # here (cancelled mid-run) - then the file stays empty and json=
          # is skipped with a warning.
          mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS" 2>/dev/null || true
          python3 - > $HUB_LOGS/hub-models.json <<'PY' || true
          import json, urllib.request
          _zt = urllib.request.Request('http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/models/full', headers={'x-hub-token': '${{ inputs.token }}'})
          d = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(_zt, timeout=20))
          ms = d.get('models', [])
          free = [m for m in ms if m.get('free')]
          print(json.dumps({
              'kind': 'NPM-Hub',
              'hubCount': len(ms),
              'hubFree': len(free),
              'hubTop': [(m.get('fullId') or m.get('id')) for m in free[:8]],
              'hubSelected': d.get('selected') or '',
          }))
          PY
          GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" \
            bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" \
              "slot=hub-linux" "file=models-hub-linux.json" \
               "kind=NPM-Hub" "os=linux" \
              "json=$HUB_LOGS/hub-models.json"

      - name: Record the run in the history
        if: always()
        run: |
          # One small file per run, filed under the day and the weekday it
          # belongs to: history/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<Wd>/run-<runNumber>.json - the
          # diary the panel groups by day, and unlike the Actions UI it does not
          # disappear when GitHub prunes old runs.
          STARTED=""
          if [ -f "$HOME/.npm-hub/session-start" ]; then
            STARTED="$(date -u -d "@$(( $(cat "$HOME/.npm-hub/session-start" 2>/dev/null || date +%s) / 1000 ))" '+%Y-%m-%d' 2>/dev/null || true)"
          fi
          GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" \
            bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" journal=1 \
              "slot=hub-linux" "kind=NPM-Hub" "os=linux" \
              "conclusion=${{ job.status }}" "endedAt=$(date -u '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')" \
              ${STARTED:+journal_date="$STARTED"} \
              "handoff=${{ inputs.handoff }}" \
              "runUrl=https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}" \
              2>&1 | tail -5 || echo "::warning::run history record failed"

  # ── Hub on Windows ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
  hub-windows:
    if: inputs.os == 'windows'
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner_windows }}
    timeout-minutes: 360

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          path: fork

      # The gate token is echoed into this job's logs by the shell (every
      # x-hub-token probe line). Mask it before anything prints it.
      - name: Mask the gate token in logs
        if: inputs.token != ''
        shell: bash
        env:
          ZT_MASK: ${{ inputs.token }}
          GH_MASK: ${{ inputs.gh_token }}

parts.text:
Key discovery: **the "Keep the session alive" watchdog at hub.yml lines 488-565 is a THIRD owner of cloudflared main**. It checks `hub-url` + `$PIDFILE` (cloudflared-8090.pid) + `tunnel_health.sh`. And `tunnel_keeper.sh` also opens main. And `hub_control.sh reopen-tunnel` also opens main. Three owners of one pidfile `cloudflared-8090.pid`.

Crucially:
- The watchdog (line 542) checks EDGE only if `$PID` alive AND `$CUR` non-empty AND tunnel_health passes. When the tunnel is open and healthy → `continue`. If not → kill pid, pkill, reopen with `open_tunnel.sh 8090 $HUB_LOGS/tunnel2.log`. open_tunnel.sh's `kill_old` (line 55) kills the PIDFILE pid and, when TAG empty, pkill -f "cloudflared tunnel --url http://127.0.0.1:$PORT" — that pattern only matches main since reserve uses same URL... wait. Let's check: reserve is opened with TUNNEL_TAG=reserve, but open_tunnel.sh's command line is IDENTICAL for both: `cloudflared tunnel --url http://127.0.0.1:8090 --protocol http2 ...`. The TAG only affects the file names, not the command line. So `pkill -f "cloudflared [t]unnel --url http://127.0.0.1:8090"` **kills BOTH main and reserve**! That's a huge finding.

Line 50-53 in open_tunnel.sh:
```
if [ -z "$TAG" ]; then
    pkill -f "cloudflared [t]unnel --url http://localhost:$PORT" 2>/dev/null || true
    pkill -f "cloudflared [t]unnel --url http://127[.]0[.]0[.]1:$PORT" 2>/dev/null || true
fi
```
So when the main tunnel is reopened (by keeper's open_main, or the workflow watchdog, or hub_control reopen-tunnel), the reserve cloudflared process — whose command line is byte-identical — gets killed too. Then the reserve pidfile still exists and `url_for_pidfile` returns the url... wait, url_for_pidfile checks kill -0 pid → reserve pid dead → returns 1 → so reserve gets reopened. OK so it recovers, but each main reopen costs a reserve reopen + 2 publishes. And the reserve reopen is what hits Cloudflare with a new quick-tunnel request → more likely to get 429.

Actually wait — worse. The reserve cloudflared process is killed, but `open_reserve` is only called once per loop when the pid is dead. So each loop: main dead → open_main (which pkills reserve too) → publish_pair. Next loop (20s later): reserve pid dead → open_reserve → publish_pair. So a main churn event doubles the Cloudflare quick-tunnel requests. Under VPN, Cloudflare rate-limits → 429 → both legs fail → the panel goes dark. That's the mechanical churn amplifier.

Let me double check the reserve's log file path/command. `open_reserve` calls `TUNNEL_TAG=reserve bash open_tunnel.sh "$PORT" "$HUB_LOGS/tunnel-reserve.log"`. Inside open_tunnel.sh, LOG is given as $2 = tunnel-reserve.log, PIDFILE = $HUB_LOGS/cloudflared-8090-reserve.pid. And it launches the same command line. Yes — identical command line. So the pkill in kill_old for TAG="" definitely kills the reserve.

Now, MAIN_FAILS: line 133 `if [ "$MAIN_FAILS" -ge 3 ]` → reopens. With INTERVAL=20s, that's 60s of consecutive failed health probes. The health check is `tunnel_health.sh` which does curl --max-time 15 to the public URL. Under a VPN: MTU issues / long RTT / Cloudflare edge blocking the VPN IP. tunnel_health.sh treats 5xx as unhealthy and 1033 in body as unhealthy. With http2 protocol, a VPN that blackholes long-lived connections makes the health probe fail (curl --max-time 15). VPN flapping → 3 consecutive failures in 60 s → keeper kills the (still-fine) main tunnel and opens a NEW quick tunnel, changing the address and requiring a republish. That's symptom 1 + 3 combined: "with no VPN, cloudflared comes up and immediately dies."

Also the hub_ready watchdog restart: `hub_ready` is a local probe to 127.0.0.1:8090 — local, not VPN-affected. But it saturates: `curl -sf -m 20`. Hmm, local, less VPN-related, though a VPN on the host can change routes. Actually the user's VPN is on their own machine, not the runner... wait, what does "мне постоянно приходится менять впн" mean? The user changes VPN on their own client. The effect on the tunnel is indirect: no — the tunnel runs on the GitHub runner, not the user's machine. Hmm.

Actually, wait. Let's reconsider. Is the tunnel on the GitHub runner, or is the user running the hub locally? The complaint «мне постоянно приходится менять впн из за этого так как он большинство попросту не принимает либо отказуется принимать» — "he [it] mostly simply doesn't accept, or refuses to accept" — VPN. And «без впн только может включить а потом сразу же падает» — "without VPN it can only turn on and then immediately falls."

Two readings:
(a) The user's phone VPN blocks/can't reach trycloudflare.com (many VPNs block it or Cloudflare blocks datacenter VPN egress IPs). So the user's VPN is what fails to load the tunnel address — but the user perceives it as the tunnel failing.
(b) There's a local (desktop) mode where the tunnel runs on the user's machine.

Given the panel is a phone app, (a) is most likely: the VPN's exit IP is a datacenter IP, which Cloudflare/ngrok rate-limit heavily, and the edge may refuse. But the "can only turn on and immediately falls" — that's about the tunnel itself. Hmm.

Let me check if there is a local/desktop mode that runs these scripts on the user's machine. Let's check `tools/oc_lan_start.sh`, `tools/start_desktop.sh`, and `restore-session.sh`. Also check the "VPN" mention across the repo.

Let me also grep for the journal/log in the panel index.html.

Let me read the panel code now — index.html around lines 600-1000, plus the log function.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Publish the live session's connection details so the panel can show them.
#
# The job summary already prints the address, user and password, but it is
# prose meant for a human with a browser: not machine-readable, and on a phone
# it is several taps behind the Actions UI. The panel is where the session is
# started, so it is where the credentials belong.
#
# They go to an orphan branch, session-state, as session.json. An orphan branch
# keeps this churn out of the history of main and lets the file be replaced
# wholesale every time without ever conflicting.
#
# WHO CAN READ THIS
#   On a public repository the branch is public, and so is the password in it.
#   That is the same exposure as the run summary, which is also public - but it
#   is worth being explicit, because a password on a web page feels different
#   from one in a log. Everything here dies with the runner within six hours,
#   and any secret in it is regenerated per run. If that is not acceptable,
#   make the repository private; the panel reads it with the same token either
#   way.
#
# TWO DESKS AT ONCE
#   Pass slot=linux, slot=windows or slot=agent and the entry lands in its own
#   file - session-linux.json, session-windows.json, session-agent.json,
#   session-opencode.json and session-hub.json - so
#   agent/opencode/hub take an -linux/-windows suffix (one file per OS, so two
#   runners stop overwriting each other); the bare slot stays for old runs.
#   the two desks and the agent never overwrite each other. Without a slot the
#   old single session.json is used, which keeps the older workflows working
#   unchanged.
#
#   The panel reads all three and shows whichever are live.
#
# MODELS AND SAVED SNAPSHOTS
#   Sessions alone do not survive usefully: which model answered, which died,
#   which recovered - that roster lives in ~/.zen_free_models.json on the
#   runner and dies with it. So every session also publishes its models:
#
#     publish_session.sh slot=agent file=models-agent.json \
#       kind=CLI-агент json=$HOME/.zen_free_models.json
#   file= overrides the target on the branch (validated: only the known
#   mailboxes are accepted, so a typo cannot spray files across the branch).
#   json= merges a local JSON file into the payload - with secrets scrubbed:
#   any key looking like a key/token/secret/password is dropped, because
#   opencode.json holds API keys and this branch may be public. Pass scrub=0
#   to disable.
#
# LAYOUT OF THE BRANCH (it used to be one pile in the root)
#   live/session-<slot>.json      the live descriptor, one per slot
#   live/handoff.json             the relay limits + the relay's live status
#   models/models-<slot>.json     the model roster of that session
#   snapshots/audit.json          the audit trail (was audit.json)
#   snapshots/code.json           the code snapshot (was code.json)
#   chats/<repo>.json             OpenCode chat bundles (unchanged)
#   history/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<Wd>/    everything historical, by day and weekday:
#       run-<runNumber>.json         one record per run: success or failure
#       saved-<slot>-<stamp>.json    the «Сохранить» snapshots
#       audit-<slot>-<stamp>.json
#       opencode-<stamp>.json
#   artifacts/<file>              files the user pushed from the hub
#   Every reader tries the new path first and falls back to the old root name,
#   so a branch that was never migrated keeps working.
#
#   publish_session.sh journal=1 writes the run record:
#     publish_session.sh journal=1 slot=hub-linux conclusion=success \
#       startedAt=... endedAt=...
#
# Usage: publish_session.sh key=value ...
#   Recognised keys are passed straight through to JSON, so a new session type
#   can add a field without touching this script.

set -uo pipefail

BRANCH="session-state"
FILE="live/session.json"
JOURNAL=0
# journal_date can come as an argument or from the environment; without it the
# record is filed under today (UTC).
JOURNAL_DATE="${JOURNAL_DATE:-}"

# A slot is a routing instruction, not data: pull it out of the arguments
# before they become JSON.
ARGS=()
JSON_FILES=()
FILE_OVERRIDE=""
SCRUB=1
EXPLICIT_STARTED_AT=0
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    startedAt=*)   EXPLICIT_STARTED_AT=1; ARGS+=("$arg") ;;
    journal_date=*) JOURNAL_DATE="${arg#journal_date=}" ;;
    slot=linux)    FILE="live/session-linux.json" ;;
    slot=windows)  FILE="live/session-windows.json" ;;
    slot=agent)    FILE="live/session-agent.json" ;;
    slot=agent-linux)    FILE="live/session-agent-linux.json" ;;
    slot=agent-windows)  FILE="live/session-agent-windows.json" ;;
    slot=opencode) FILE="live/session-opencode.json" ;;
    slot=opencode-linux) FILE="live/session-opencode-linux.json" ;;
    slot=opencode-windows) FILE="live/session-opencode-windows.json" ;;
    slot=hub)      FILE="live/session-hub.json" ;;
    slot=hub-linux)      FILE="live/session-hub-linux.json" ;;
    slot=hub-windows)    FILE="live/session-hub-windows.json" ;;
    slot=phone)    FILE="live/session-phone.json" ;;
    slot=vnc)      FILE="live/session-vnc.json" ;;
    slot=*)        ;;   # unknown slot: ignore rather than write a stray file
    file=*)        FILE_OVERRIDE="$arg" ;;
    journal=1)     JOURNAL=1 ;;
    scrub=0)       SCRUB=0 ;;
    json=*)        # A Windows path (C:\Users\..) breaks mingw python; slashes
                   # work for both Windows and mingw python, so normalise.
                   _jv="${arg#json=}"; _jv="${_jv//\\//}"; JSON_FILES+=("$_jv") ;;

  esac

# the branch is a fixed set of mailboxes, not a scratch disk. The caller keeps
# using the old flat names; the layout below turns them into the new folders.
if [ -n "$FILE_OVERRIDE" ]; then
  _f="${FILE_OVERRIDE#file=}"

     [[ "$_f" =~ ^(audit|code)\.json$ ]] || \
     [[ "$_f" =~ ^chats/[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,80}\.json$ ]] || \
     [[ "$_f" =~ ^saved/(audit|code)(-[a-z0-9-]+)?-[0-9]{8}T[0-9]{6}\.json$ ]] || \
     [[ "$_f" =~ ^saved/opencode-[0-9]{8}T[0-9]{6}\.json$ ]] || \
     [[ "$_f" =~ ^saved/(linux|windows|agent(-linux|-windows)?|opencode(-linux|-windows)?|hub(-linux|-windows)?)-[0-9]{8}T[0-9]{6}\.json$ ]] || \
     [[ "$_f" =~ ^history/[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}/(Mon|Tue|Wed|Thu|Fri|Sat|Sun)/[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,90}\.json$ ]]; then
    FILE="$_f"
  else
    echo "publish_session: rejected file override: $_f" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
fi

# ── the layout: one flat pile sorted into folders ─────────────────────────
# Everything used to sit in the branch root, which made "what is this file and
# when is it from" a guessing game. Now: live/ for what is alive right now,
# models/ for the roster, snapshots/ for the audit/code pair, and history/ for
# everything historical, filed under the day and the weekday it belongs to.
#
# date_of_day <YYYYMMDD or YYYY-MM-DD> -> "YYYY-MM-DD/Tue"
history_bucket() {
  local raw="$1" d=""
  if [[ "$raw" =~ ^([0-9]{4})([0-9]{2})([0-9]{2})$ ]]; then
    d="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}-${BASH_REMATCH[2]}-${BASH_REMATCH[3]}"
  elif [[ "$raw" =~ ^([0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2})$ ]]; then
    d="$raw"
  else
    d="$(date -u '+%Y-%m-%d')"
  fi
  local wd
  wd="$(date -u -d "$d" '+%a' 2>/dev/null || true)"
  case "$wd" in
    Mon|Tue|Wed|Thu|Fri|Sat|Sun) : ;;
    *) wd="$(python3 -c "import datetime,sys;print(datetime.date.fromisoformat(sys.argv[1]).strftime('%a'))" "$d" 2>/dev/null || echo "")" ;;
  esac
  [ -n "$wd" ] || wd="---"
  printf '%s/%s' "$d" "$wd"
}

# A date out of a <name>-YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS.json stamp; today when there is none.
stamp_bucket() {
  local name="$1" raw=""
  if [[ "$name" =~ ([0-9]{8})T[0-9]{6} ]]; then raw="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"; fi
  history_bucket "$raw"
}

layout_file() {
  local f="$1" bucket
  case "$f" in
    live/*|chats/*|history/*|artifacts/*) printf '%s' "$f"; return 0 ;;
  esac
  case "$f" in
    session*.json) printf 'live/%s' "$f"; return 0 ;;
    models-*.json) printf 'models/%s' "$f"; return 0 ;;
    audit.json|code.json) printf 'snapshots/%s' "$f"; return 0 ;;
    handoff.json) printf 'live/handoff.json'; return 0 ;;
  esac
  if [[ "$f" == saved/* ]]; then
    # saved/audit-hub-20260102T030405.json -> history/2026-01-02/Fri/saved-audit-hub-...
    bucket="$(stamp_bucket "${f#saved/}")"
    printf 'history/%s/saved-%s' "$bucket" "${f#saved/}"
    return 0
  fi
  printf '%s' "$f"
}

if [ "$JOURNAL" = "1" ]; then
  _num="${GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER:-0}"
  [ -n "$_num" ] || _num=0
  bucket="$(history_bucket "$JOURNAL_DATE")"
  FILE="history/$bucket/run-$_num.json"
fi
FILE="$(layout_file "$FILE")"
export SCRUB
export JSON_MERGE="$(printf '%s\n' "${JSON_FILES[@]}")" 

# A unique staging file per invocation. A fixed /tmp/session.json is shared by
# every caller on the machine, and two publishes running at once overwrote each
# other's payload - caught by a local race test, where the Windows entry ended
# up carrying the Linux address. Staged under ~/.npm-hub/tmp, never /tmp.

mkdir -p "$HOME/.npm-hub/tmp" || exit 1

  exit 1
fi
cleanup_publish() {
  cd / 2>/dev/null || true

python3 - "$@" <<'PY' > "$STAGE"
import json, os, re, sys, datetime

SECRET_RE = re.compile(r'key|token|secret|passw|auth|credential|private|bearer', re.I)

def scrub(o):
    if isinstance(o, dict):
        return {k: scrub(v) for k, v in o.items() if not SECRET_RE.search(str(k))}
    if isinstance(o, list):
        return [scrub(v) for v in o]
    return o

data = {}
# Local JSON files first, so explicit key=value arguments win over them.
for path in (os.environ.get('JSON_MERGE') or '').splitlines():
    path = path.strip()
    if not path:
        continue
    try:
        with open(path, encoding='utf-8') as f:
            merged = json.load(f)

data['repo'] = os.environ.get('GITHUB_REPOSITORY', '')

# the staging file ends up empty and the script reports "nothing to publish"

PY
    fi
  fi
fi

mkdir -p "$(dirname "$FILE")"
carry_url2
cp "$STAGE" "$FILE"
git config user.email "session@symbiosis"
git config user.name  "Session state"
git add "$FILE"

if git diff --cached --quiet; then
  echo "publish_session: unchanged"
  exit 0
fi

git commit -q -m "session $(date -u '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')"

# NOT a force push any more.
#
# Two desks publish to this branch at the same time, and -f made the second
# writer erase the first: the Linux desk cloned the branch before the Windows
# desk existed, then force-pushed its own single-file tree over it. Measured -
# session-windows.json was written by a step that reported success, and the
# branch afterwards held only session-linux.json.
#
# So: fetch, replay this one file on top of whatever is there now, push
# normally, and retry if someone else got in between. Each desk only ever
# touches its own file, so the merge is trivial and cannot conflict.
pushed=0
for attempt in $(seq 1 12); do
  if git push -q origin "HEAD:$BRANCH" 2>/dev/null; then
    pushed=1
    break
  fi
  echo "publish_session: push attempt $attempt failed; refreshing $BRANCH" >&2
  if git fetch -q origin "$BRANCH" 2>/dev/null; then
    git reset -q --hard FETCH_HEAD
    if session_publish_blocked; then
      echo "publish_session: $FILE is owned by a newer run; left alone"
      exit 0
    fi
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$FILE")"
    carry_url2
    cp "$STAGE" "$FILE"
    git add "$FILE"
    git commit -q -m "session $(date -u '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')" 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
  delay=$((attempt * 2))
  [ "$delay" -gt 30 ] && delay=30
  sleep "$delay"
done

if [ "$pushed" = 1 ]; then
  echo "publish_session: published $FILE to $BRANCH"
else
  echo "publish_session: push failed after retries" >&2
  exit 1
fi

parts.text:
Very important finding: `carry_url2` (lines 360-397) preserves `url2` AND `ngrok` from the on-branch descriptor when the incoming payload omits them AND `old_run == new_run`. Good. So tunnel_keeper's publish_pair does not erase ngrok, **as long as the runIds match**.

BUT: `data['runId'] = os.environ.get('GITHUB_RUN_ID','')` — in tunnel_keeper, `publish_pair` is called with `GH_TOKEN="$TOKEN"` only; GITHUB_RUN_ID is inherited from the keeper's environment (nohup env ... from the workflow step), so it IS set. Good.

BUT WAIT — big one. In `ngrok_keeper.sh publish_full` (line 110-115), it passes `ngrok=$ng` explicitly — fine. In tunnel_keeper's `publish_pair`, `ngrok` is carried over. OK.

Now the critical case: **`carry_url2` only preserves keys when the new payload OMITS them**. If the tunnel_keeper's `publish_pair` runs and `old.get('ngrok')` exists, it's carried. Fine.

BUT here's the thing: the reverse. `ngrok_keeper.publish_full` reads `$HUB_LOGS/hub-ngrok.url`? No — it reads `$URLFILE` (hub-url) and `$R_URLFILE` (hub-url2), and passes ngrok=$ng. If hub-url is missing/empty, it publishes without url/hubUrl → carry_url2 doesn't carry `url` (not in the list) → **the main address is ERASED from the descriptor**. That's a real hazard: `publish_full` only carries `url2` and `ngrok`, never `url`/`hubUrl`. If at the moment ngrok_keeper publishes, `$HUB_LOGS/hub-url` is empty (e.g. the main tunnel just died and the keeper's open_main hasn't rewritten it yet, or the watchdog is mid-reopen), the publish wipes url/hubUrl/desktop/mobile from the descriptor. Then the panel has ONLY url2 (+ngrok) → `sessionBases` returns 2 bases (ngrok + url2) — and `describeBaseFailure` says «Ни основной, ни резервный...». Hmm, but the panel's `readSlotRaw` checks `!(s.hubUrl || s.agentUrl || s.url || s.deskUrl)` → treats as "адрес ещё не опубликован"!

Actually wait — more important: if the ngrok leg is ABSENT (empty) and url/hubUrl are wiped, then the descriptor has only url2. Then `sessionBases` = [url2] — 1 base. Hmm, that's 1, and `i>0` never fires.

Let's reconsider the inference. The user saw exactly ONE «Основной адрес молчит — пробую резервный…». With bases = [main, url2] (2 bases), line 689 fires exactly once when i=1 — and only if main failed. If url2 also failed → describeBaseFailure → «Ни основной, ни резервный адрес не отвечает: …». The user's complaint says cloudflared "falls immediately" — so plausibly exactly that.

So the inference "s.ngrok was empty → bases.length == 2" holds for the firstReachableBase path. BUT there's an alternative: `openLast()` line 869 fires with `last.reserve` — and openLast's `last.reserve` is whatever `bases.filter(b=>b!==got)[0]` was saved as — could be url2 even when ngrok exists. And critically: in the openLast path, `last.reserve` is the SECOND base, and `lastOriginToken()` is the FIRST base. If ngrok WAS present and was base[0], then main failure → tries url2 → fails → «Последний хаб недоступен: Failed to fetch». Also exactly one such line, no address lines. So openLast gives the same observable signature.

Let me check the other index.html (app/src/main/assets/panel/index.html) since that's the "app" that the user might actually be using — the complaint says «нету в приложении видимых адресов в журнале» ("no visible addresses in the app's journal"). Let me check which panel is which and whether the hub/index.html is served at /m and the root.

Actually the task explicitly points at hub/index.html. But let me check whether app/panel/index.html also has the bootLog with sessionBases — because the "app" (APK) is the panel. Let me grep.

Let me check publish_session for `ngrok` and check hub.yml for where tunnel_keeper starts vs the first publish (order) and also check the hub.yml ngrok for the *other* job (windows).

Also very important for symptom 1: is `tunnel_keeper` even started for the hub VM? Yes, line 362. And is `ngrok_keeper` started? Only if NGROK_AUTHTOKEN secret non-empty (line 371).

Now, let me check git history for the "1.358" version comment about ngrok ordering — and check whether there's a repo-level default of NGROK_DOMAIN etc. Also check whether the repo has any record of the secret being set. The user says «несмотря на нгрок» — "despite ngrok" — implying they believe ngrok is configured. So maybe the token is set but the keeper fails.

Let me look for failure modes of ngrok_keeper:
1. `NGROK_DOMAIN` default `filly-above-terrapin.ngrok-free.app` — a **hardcoded reserved domain**. If the user's ngrok account does NOT have that domain claimed (it's a specific random name), `ngrok http --url=...` **fails outright** with ERR_NGROK_108 "domain is not available / not reserved for this account". That would make `start_agent` never get a URL → 40s timeout → kill → FAILS++. That's a silent failure (only in ngrok-keeper.log), and after 30 fails the backoff becomes COOLDOWN*30 = 1800s = 30 minutes. So the ngrok leg can be permanently dead and never visible to the user.

Actually careful: `--url` in ngrok v3 for reserved domains. If the domain isn't reserved, ngrok errors: "failed to start tunnel: domain 'x' is not reserved". The agent would exit quickly → the loop `for i in seq 1 20` breaks on `kill -0` → url empty → `log "no address after 40s"` → kill, rm pidfile, return 1. FAILS++. After 30 fails → 30 min sleeps. Silent.

2. `install_ngrok` — needs `$HOME/.local/bin` on PATH; the export PATH in the function is local to the function's subshell? No — `export PATH` inside a function affects the current shell. But the first call at line 146 is at top level so PATH persists. But if `command -v ngrok` finds it elsewhere... fine.

3. The `log()` note at 54-55: log writes to file only, good.

4. `healthy()` for ngrok: body non-empty and not ERR_NGROK. The hub returns 401 JSON for `/` — non-empty body → healthy. OK.

5. **Critical race**: `ngrok_keeper` publishes `publish_full` which re-sends url/hubUrl. Fine.

6. **Critical**: `ngrok_keeper` is started in the same step at line 371-375, but the tunnel_keeper at 362. Both start. tunnel_keeper's publish_pair does NOT include ngrok → carried. OK.

Now, symptom 1's mechanism: Let's enumerate who can kill/reopen the main cloudflared:
- A: workflow watchdog loop (hub.yml 539-564), every 15s.
- B: tunnel_keeper open_main (line 135), every ~60s of failures.
- C: hub_control reopen-tunnel (line 119-131), on demand.

All three write `$HUB_LOGS/cloudflared-8090.pid` + `.url` via open_tunnel.sh, and `$HUB_LOGS/hub-url`.

And **all three, by calling open_tunnel.sh with no TUNNEL_TAG, run kill_old() which pkills BOTH cloudflared processes on port 8090** — including the reserve, because the reserve's command line is byte-identical.

Let me verify that claim precisely: open_tunnel.sh line 90: `nohup "$CF" tunnel --url "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT" --protocol http2 --no-autoupdate --loglevel info >"$LOG" 2>&1 &`. Both main and reserve use the same $PORT and the same args. The only difference is $LOG redirect and $PIDFILE. `pkill -f "cloudflared [t]unnel --url http://127[.]0[.]0[.]1:$PORT"` matches /proc/pid/cmdline → full command line → matches BOTH. YES. The reserve dies.

Wait, but the comment at open_tunnel.sh lines 26-28 says: "A second tunnel on the SAME local port (the Z11 reserve address) passes TUNNEL_TAG=reserve: it gets its own pid/url/log files and skips the shared port-wide pkill, so maintaining the reserve never shoots the main tunnel." — the guard is one-directional: reserve-open doesn't kill main. But main-open DOES kill reserve. That is the exact asymmetry. **This is the smoking gun for symptom 1**: every main-tunnel repair/reopen (which the user's VPN triggers constantly) takes the warm reserve down with it, then the keeper's very next loop opens a NEW quick tunnel for the reserve — doubling Cloudflare quick-tunnel requests per churn event, which under a rate-limited/blocked VPN IP pushes Cloudflare into 429 ("too many tunnels"), and then BOTH cloudflare legs are gone. That is "cloudflared flaps even though ngrok exists" — because the user's traffic actually depends on cloudflare (since s.ngrok was empty).

Let me double check: after main's open_tunnel kills reserve, the reserve pidfile `cloudflared-8090-reserve.pid` still holds a dead pid → `url_for_pidfile` returns 1 → next loop `open_reserve`. And R_URLFILE (hub-url2) still holds the old reserve URL until open_reserve's `rm -f` at line 85. So between main-reopen and the next reserve loop (≤20s), the descriptor still publishes a dead url2. And open_main → publish_pair → publishes the stale dead url2. Then the panel's probe walks main→url2, url2 dead. Matches the symptom.

Now also: the pkill in the *workflow watchdog* at line 552 and in `cleanup_watchdog` line 462 — same problem (kills reserve on watchdog reopen). And hub_control line 124.

Another race: hub_control's `reopen-tunnel` (line 122-123) kills the pid, then pkill, then open_tunnel. Simultaneously tunnel_keeper may be running open_main. Two concurrent open_tunnel.sh invocations both do kill_old → they'd kill each other's newly spawned cloudflared → the last writer wins but the earlier one's URL may already have been written to hub-url and published → dangling address. Then the keeper sees dead pid → reopens → publish. Also `publish_pair` from both → duplicate branch writes.

Also: tunnel_keeper's MAIN_FAILS counter is NOT reset by open_main succeeding — line 137 resets it to 0 immediately after calling open_main, even if open_main failed (URL empty). Actually line 135 open_main; line 137 MAIN_FAILS=0. open_main returning nothing logs failure. Then next loop: 3 more failures → another attempt. So under a persistently broken path, the keeper burns a NEW quick tunnel every ~60-70s forever. Each attempt = a fresh trycloudflare allocation = guaranteed churn + 429 risk. There's no backoff for the MAIN leg at all (only RESERVE_COOLDOWN exists).

And the workflow watchdog (hub.yml 488-565) also reopens main with no backoff, every ~16s once the edge probe fails. So we have 2 processes each reopening main every 60s, plus the reserve reopen each time. Under VPN that is a quick-tunnel storm → Cloudflare 429 → total outage. That's exactly "без впн только может включить а потом сразу же падает" (without VPN it can only come up and then immediately dies).

Hmm wait — actually think about what "VPN" means here once more. The user is on Android (agent code mentions Android VPN/Termux). The panel is an APK. The user's VPN is on their phone. So how does the phone's VPN affect a cloudflared running on a GitHub runner?

Answer: it doesn't directly — but it affects what the user perceives and, critically, the panel's probe path. The phone's fetch() to trycloudflare.com through a VPN egress IP: Cloudflare often blocks/404s or the VPN provider blocks the request. The panel's preflightHub would fail → the app says «не отвечает» → the user switches VPN. So symptom 3 is mostly **client-side egress**, and the fix belongs on the panel side: order legs so ngrok (a different CDN/provider, works from more exit IPs) is tried first, and give the user a visible, copyable address so they can open it from a browser/another network instead of fighting the panel.

BUT there is a second, real server-side VPN-ish effect: none. Let me check if there's a local mode — e.g. `oc_lan_start.sh` or the `desktop/` folder, or whether hub.yml can run self-hosted ("runner_linux" input = "self-hosted"!). Look: inputs.runner_linux. If the user runs a **self-hosted runner on their own machine**, then the VPN IS on the same box as the tunnel. Let me check the workflow inputs.

That would make everything click: the user runs the hub on their own machine/runner behind a VPN; the VPN's MTU/path kills cloudflared's TCP/TLS; the tunnel comes up and dies; they toggle VPN.

Let me check hub.yml inputs and runner_linux defaults.

  HUB_LOGS: /home/runner/.npm-hub/logs

jobs:
  # ── Hub on Linux ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
  hub:
    if: inputs.os == 'linux'
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner_linux }}
    timeout-minutes: 360

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          path: fork

      # The gate token is echoed into this job's logs by the shell (every
      # x-hub-token probe line). Mask it before anything prints it.
      - name: Mask the gate token in logs
        if: inputs.token != ''
        shell: bash
        env:
          ZT_MASK: ${{ inputs.token }}
          GH_MASK: ${{ inputs.gh_token }}
        run: |
          echo "::add-mask::$ZT_MASK"
          echo "::add-mask::$GH_MASK"

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "20"

      - name: Restore the npm/pip caches
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.npm
            ~/.cache/pip
          # run_id: every run saves a fresh cache (an exact-key hit would skip
          # the save and the freshly downloaded tarballs would never persist).
          key: hub-pkg-linux-${{ github.run_id }}
          restore-keys: hub-pkg-linux-

      - name: Install the CLI agents
        if: inputs.preinstall
        run: |
          # One npm call: its downloads run concurrently, so this is minutes
          # faster than installing one by one. If it fails, fall back to
          # per-package attempts so a renamed package cannot cancel the
          # rest. Whatever lands on PATH the hub picks up; anything missing
          # still launches through `npx -y` at click time.
          export HUB_LOGS="$HOME/.npm-hub/logs"; mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS" 2>/dev/null || true
          PKGS="opencode-ai @anthropic-ai/claude-code @google/gemini-cli @openai/codex @github/copilot @qwen-code/qwen-code http-server"
          npm install -g $PKGS >$HUB_LOGS/npm-i.log 2>&1 || \
            for p in $PKGS; do npm install -g "$p" >$HUB_LOGS/npm-i.log 2>&1 \
              && echo "installed $p" || echo "skipped $p"; done
          pip install --quiet aider-chat goose-ai >$HUB_LOGS/pip-i.log 2>&1 || \
            for p in aider-chat goose-ai; do pip install --quiet "$p" >$HUB_LOGS/pip-i.log 2>&1 \
              && echo "installed $p" || echo "skipped $p"; done
          echo "--- on PATH now ---"
          for c in opencode claude gemini codex copilot qwen aider goose http-server; do
            command -v "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "  $c: $(command -v $c)" || echo "  $c: -"
          done

      - name: Install the hub dependencies
        working-directory: fork/npm-hub
        run: npm ci

      - name: Install OpenCode for session recovery
        run: |
          set -e
          echo "$HOME/.opencode/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          export PATH="$HOME/.opencode/bin:$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
          if ! command -v opencode >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash || true
          fi
          if ! command -v opencode >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            npm install -g opencode-ai
          fi
          command -v opencode
          opencode --version || true

      - name: Put zen-agent on PATH
        run: |
          printf '#!/bin/sh\nexec node "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/agent/zen-agent.js" "$@"\n' \
            | sudo tee /usr/local/bin/agent >/dev/null
          sudo chmod +x /usr/local/bin/agent

      - name: Create the work folder and restore repositories
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          export HUB_LOGS="$HOME/.npm-hub/logs"; mkdir -p ~/hub-work "$HUB_LOGS" 2>/dev/null || true; mkdir -p ~/.npm-hub/logs
          echo "logs dir ready $(ls -ld ~/.npm-hub/logs 2>&1 || ls -ld "$HUB_LOGS" 2>&1)"
          if [ "${{ inputs.handoff }}" = "true" ]; then
            echo "::notice::session relay: taking the session over from run ${{ inputs.handoff_from }}. Everything below is a restore of what that runner saved; its watchdog is waiting for this run to publish before it steps aside."

# Free vision models (no API key)

## Шаг 0 — сначала проверь, не видишь ли ты сам

Это правило важнее всех остальных в этом файле. **Никогда не зови внешний движок,
если ты сам работаешь на модели с вижном.**


- **Сначала Шаг 0.** Видишь сам — читай сам, внешние движки не трогай.

- Изображение передаётся как data URL: `data:image/png;base64,....` (jpg → `data:image/jpeg;base64,...`).

`POST https://api.kilo.ai/api/gateway/v1/chat/completions`

```bash
DATA_URL="data:image/jpeg;base64,...."
```

## 2. OVHcloud AI (резерв, 2 req/мин)


## 3. Резерв

## Не путать — текстовые (без вижн) в этих провайдерах
- Kilo текст: `nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free`, `nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:free`, `z-ai/glm-5.2:free` (на картинку 404), `qwen/qwen3.8-27b:free`, `thinkingmachines/inkling-small:free`, etc.

Now I understand the core problem. Let me look at the key bug: `tryOpenLive` at line 541.

The flow: When the user presses "Запустить хаб":
1. If there's an active hub run → `tryOpenLive(token)` 
2. `tryOpenLive` reads the session file; if state==='live' and has hubUrl → probes candidates
3. If NO reachable base → logs "Адрес хаба молчит (туннель мёртв...)" and returns false → **dead end, requires manual restart**

That's the critical bug shown in the screenshots: the app gets stuck in a loop where it says "Хаб уже запущен. Подбираю доступ…" → "Адрес хаба молчит (туннель мёртв — ран, скорее всего, остановлен извне). Нажмите «Остановить и перезапустить ранер»." — and the user must manually click restart.

But wait — there's a much worse contradiction. In screenshot 1, the session list showed "NPM Hub: Build #385, running for 5h 33m" — i.e., **the run IS alive** but the tunnel address is dead. And "Список сессий: Failed to fetch" repeats.

Critical issue #2: `readHubSessionRaw` — the raw.githubusercontent.com edge cache is stale by minutes. The comment at line 629-634 acknowledges this. But `tryOpenLive` at line 542 calls `readHubSessionRaw()` **only** — it never falls back to `readHubSessionViaApi`. So if the raw edge serves a stale `ended` file from a previous run (or a stale live file with a dead address), `tryOpenLive` reads STALE data forever and never gets fresh data. That's a genuine bug: `tryOpenLive` should use `readHubSession(token)` not `readHubSessionRaw()`.

Critical issue #3: `raw.githubusercontent.com` **does not serve the `session-state` branch by default** unless the branch is published... actually raw serves any branch ref. But it requires the repo to be public. If the repo is private, raw returns 404. Then it falls to the API path. OK.

Actually let me formulate the bugs first:

**BUG 1 (critical, the deadlock in screenshots):** `tryOpenLive()` at line 542 calls `readHubSessionRaw()` — raw.githubusercontent.com ONLY. The code's own comment at lines 629-634 documents that raw serves edge copies that are minutes stale. So `tryOpenLive` can read a **stale** `session-hub-linux.json`:
- stale `state:'ended'` → logs "Запуск уже идёт, но адрес хаб ещё не сообщил" (screenshot 3 at 01:25:16 — exactly this message!) and returns false, even though the hub is actually live and the address IS published.
- stale `state:'live'` with the OLD run's dead ngrok URL → probes dead address → "Адрес хаба молчит (туннель мёртв)" (screenshot 2 at 01:21:03) → returns false.

This is the direct cause of the screenshots' loop. Fix: use `readHubSession(token)` with the stale-detection + API fallback, same as `waitForHub`.

**BUG 2 (critical):** `tryOpenLive` has no recovery at all. When the address is provably dead (all candidates "Failed to fetch"), the correct action is to **restart the runner automatically** — the app already has `restartRunner()` right below at line 573 and `cancelAndWait()`. Instead it prints "Нажмите «Остановить и перезапустить ранер»" — manual. The user's whole request: "хочу чтобы аи мог работать автоматически без моего вмешательства". Auto-restart when the tunnel is provably dead is the fix.

**BUG 3:** `hubCandidates(s)` — when the stale raw file is read, `spare` is derived from the GitHub token. Fine.

**BUG 4:** `openLast()` at 858 — only tries `last.url` and `last.reserve`. Doesn't consult the fresh session file at all. Screenshot 1: "Открыть последний (217 мин назад)" → "Открыть не вышло: Адрес не отвечает". Fix: `openLast` should fall back to re-reading the session file and re-probing (i.e. call `tryOpenLive`), so the button self-heals instead of demanding a runner restart.

**BUG 5:** `readHubSessionRaw` reads `live/session-hub-linux.json` FIRST then `session-hub-linux.json`. But `readSlotRaw(slot)` — let me check. If both paths exist and `live/` is stale while flat is fresh (or vice versa), the wrong one wins. Need to pick the freshest by timestamp, not by order. Let me check readSlotRaw.

**BUG 6:** The screenshots show "Список сессий: Failed to fetch" — that's a *GitHub API* call failing (api() to api.github.com). Likely transient/network. But repeated every ~20-60s. Not clearly a code bug but the error message gives no guidance.


Meanwhile the "Последние запуски" card showed **NPM Hub Build #385 running for 5h33m** — i.e. the GitHub Actions run IS alive. So: run alive, but the panel can never reconnect. The user is trapped in a manual loop: press "Запустить хаб" → "Хаб уже запущен. Подбираю доступ…" → "Адрес хаба молчит (туннель мёртв)…" → dead end, must manually press "Остановить и перезапустить ранер".

## User's explicit goals
1. Fix the connection bug so it self-heals.
2. "хочу чтобы аи мог работать автоматически без моего вмешательства" — the panel must recover on its own, no manual button presses.
3. Earlier user asked: can the runner live in Docker so they connect by IP? (Not the main ask now; just context that they want the runner always-on and reachable by a stable address.)
4. Earlier: agent needs full access including /tmp, download and install packages — so full-auto operation must not be sandboxed away.

## Code facts I already established (verify, don't trust blindly)

- `tryOpenLive(token)` — index.html:541. Called from `runHubFlow('launch')` when `detectSessionConflict(token) === 'hub'` (index.html:1001-1008).
- `tryOpenLive` line 542 reads the session file via **`readHubSessionRaw()` ONLY** — never the authenticated API path.
- `readHubSessionRaw()` — index.html:591 — fetches `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/${REPO}/session-state/{live/session-hub-linux.json, session-hub-linux.json}?t=<cachebust>`, no token.
- The file itself already documents (index.html:629-634) that **raw.githubusercontent.com serves edge copies that can be minutes stale**, and that `waitForHub()` therefore switches to the REST contents API after 3 stale reads (`staleReads >= 3`). **`tryOpenLive` has no such fallback.**
- Consequence A: `tryOpenLive` reads a stale `state:'ended'` file → prints the exact 01:25:16 message "Запуск уже идёт, но адрес хаб ещё не сообщил (или он уже выключен)" → returns false, even though the hub is live and its address is published. Dead end.
- Consequence B: `tryOpenLive` reads a stale `state:'live'` file holding the PREVIOUS run's dead ngrok URL → probes it → "Failed to fetch" → prints the exact 01:21:03 message "Адрес хаба молчит (туннель мёртв...)" → returns false. Dead end.
- `firstReachableBase(bases, ztOrCandidates, runId)` — index.html:685. Walks bases × token candidates, returns `{base, zt, errors}`; every failure reason is collected in `errors[]`.
- When ALL probes fail with network-class reasons (`/failed to fetch|networkerror|load failed/i`), `tryOpenLive` lines 554-557 concludes "туннель мёртв" and tells the user to press the restart button manually. No automatic action is taken, even though `restartRunner(token, zt, runner)` (index.html:573) and `cancelAndWait(token)` (index.html:527) exist on the very same page and do exactly the needed work.
- `runHubFlow('launch')` lines 1005-1008: when `tryOpenLive` returns false it calls `progFinish(false, 'Доступ не подошёл — хаб закрыт чужим токеном запуска. Нажми «Остановить и перезапустить ранер».')` — i.e. the false diagnosis "чужим токеном" is printed even when the real cause was a dead tunnel or a stale read.
- `openLast()` — index.html:858 — only probes `last.url` and `last.reserve` from localStorage. It never re-reads the session file, so the "Открыть последний (N мин назад)" button can never self-heal. It throws "Последний хаб недоступен: ..." (and via index.html:1318-1319 the generic "Адрес не отвечает — адрес прошлого запуска уже мёртв" text).
- `readSlotRaw(slot)` — index.html:1099 — same raw-only pattern, same ordering hazard: it returns the FIRST path that parses, i.e. `live/session-<slot>.json` always wins over the flat `session-<slot>.json` even if the flat one is newer. Neither function compares `updated_at`/`runId` to pick the freshest.
- `sessionBases(s)` — index.html:842 — order is `s.ngrok`, then `s.hubUrl || s.url`, then `s.url2`.
- `hubCandidates(s)` — index.html:813 — produces token candidates incl. a `spare` derived from the GitHub token via `sha256Hex`.
- `waitForHub(token, sinceMs, sleepMs, cancelled, runId)` — index.html:614 — the good pattern: raw first, API fallback after 3 stale reads, plus `runGone()` to notice external cancellation, 240 iterations.

## What I want from you

1. **Verdict on each of my 6 findings**: confirmed / wrong / partially right, with line numbers and the evidence that settles it.
2. **Any additional critical bug in this same code path that I missed.** Look hard at: stale-vs-fresh session-file selection, the `live/` vs flat path precedence, what happens across a page reload mid-launch (`savePending`/`readPending`/`clearPending` at index.html:728-735 — `clearPending` is called on success at 567 and 958, but is the pending zt ever *used* on a later open?), the auto-lock IIFE at index.html:887-912 (it reads the module-scope `nowMs` — is that ever updated? If `nowMs` is a one-shot value the age math is permanently frozen), and whether `openSlot`'s `tokenNow()` is defined.
3. **The recommended fix design**, in priority order, with the specific functions to change and the exact behavioural contract:
   - How `tryOpenLive` should obtain a fresh session file (reuse the `readHubSession` + stale-detection logic from `waitForHub`? Extract a shared helper? What staleness signal — `updated_at`, `runId` vs the active run's id, or both?).
   - Whether and when auto-restarting the runner is safe. Key safety question: the tunnel may be dead while the run is still alive and doing real work (VNC/repos, hours). A wrong auto-restart kills a healthy run. Propose a concrete gate — e.g. only after the fresh read confirms the address is stale/dead AND a fresh `GET /repos/.../actions/runs/{runId}` confirms the run state — and say exactly what to do when the run is alive but the tunnel is dead (the screenshot-1 case: run alive 5h33m, tunnel dead). Is there a cheaper recovery than a full restart (e.g. reading a fresher session file from a different path, or the reserve base)?
   - Whether `readSlotRaw` should pick the freshest of the two paths instead of the first.
   - What `runHubFlow`'s `progFinish(false, ...)` message should say in each failure mode, given the diagnosis is wrong today.
   - Whether `openLast` should fall back to a fresh session read + probe.
4. **Risks and regressions** of each change: token-safety (the `zt` gate, the spare-token derivation — must not leak or weaken), extra GitHub API quota burn (raw is free, API costs quota; `listActiveRuns` pages up to 5×100 runs), user-visible progress/progress-bar coherence, and offline/failed-network behaviour.
5. **A concrete test plan.** The repo has `TESTING.md` and a `ci/` dir — check what test tooling exists (node? pytest? plain html?) and specify the tests you'd want, with file paths, in the repo's existing style.

Be concrete and cite line numbers. If you think I'm wrong about something, say so bluntly.

## Verdict

Your six findings are **4 confirmed, 1 wrong, 1 moot** — but they are not the worst of it. The panel has a fully implemented, whitelisted remote-repair channel on the runner (`control/queue.json` with a `reopen-tunnel` op, `tools/hub_control.sh:22,119-135`) that the panel **never touches** (`grep control/ hub/src/main/assets/hub/index.html` → zero hits). That is the correct answer to "run alive 5h33m, tunnel dead", it costs1 branch write, and it kills nothing. Everything else in this design is secondary to wiring it up.

---

## 1. Your six findings

**#1 `tryOpenLive` reads raw only — CONFIRMED.** `:542` `const s = await readHubSessionRaw();`. `readHubSessionRaw` (`:591-599`) is raw.githubusercontent only, no token, no API fallback. `waitForHub` has the stale→API switch at `:639` (`token && staleReads >= 3`). `tryOpenLive` has nothing. Settled.

**#2 Consequence A (stale `ended` → the 01:25:16 line) — CONFIRMED.** `:543-546` collapses `!s`, `s.state!=='live'` and `!(s.hubUrl||s.url)` into one message at `:544`. That is the exact 01:25:16 string, verbatim.

**#3 Consequence B (stale `live` with a dead URL → 01:21:03) — CONFIRMED.** `:551-562`, message at `:557` is verbatim.

**#4 No auto-action on total network failure — CONFIRMED.** `:554-557` prints and returns `false`. `restartRunner` (`:573`) and `cancelAndWait` (`:527`) are on the page. **But note: `restartRunner` is dead code — grep shows zero call sites.** The live restart path is an inline duplicate at `:986-998`. So "the function that does the needed work exists" is true only of `cancelAndWait`; there are two copies of the destructive operation and only one of them is wired.

**#5 `openLast` never re-reads the session file — CONFIRMED.** `:858-880` probes `last.url`, then `last.reserve`, then throws. Worse than you said: it probes with **one** token, `lastOriginToken().zt` (`:860`) — no pending, no spare, no `hubCandidates`. Even with a fresh file it would 401 after a storage wipe.

**#6 `readSlotRaw` first-wins is a hazard — WRONG IN PRACTICE. Drop this one.** Nothing writes the flat path any more: `tools/publish_session.sh` `layout_file()` maps `session*.json → live/…`, and the `file=` override whitelist (publish_session.sh, the `[[ "$FILE_OVERRIDE" =~ … ]]` block) accepts only `models-*`, `audit/code`, `chats/`, `saved-`, `history/` — **no session names**. `migrate_session_state.sh` only `git mv`s old ones into `live/`. So `live/` is unconditionally the newer file; the precedence is correct. The staleness that actually bites you is the CDN edge copy of `live/` itself, which P0 below fixes. Changing this would be churn for a case that cannot occur.

**Your two open questions, both no-ops:** `nowMs` (`:833`) is a one-shot evaluated at load, immediately after `let last = readLast()` (`:832`), and the only consumer is the `age` at `:889` — correct. The ticking branch at `:901` correctly uses `Date.now()`. Not frozen. And `tokenNow()` is defined at `:1140` as a hoisted function declaration, well before `openSlot` (`:1237`) ever runs. Both fine.

---

## 2. What you missed (ranked)

1. **The runner-side repair channel exists and is unused.** `tools/hub_control.sh` runs a 20 s daemon publishing `control/heartbeat-hub.json` (2-min process census: `hub_server`, `cloudflared`, `tunnel_keeper`, `ngrok_keeper`) and executing `control/queue.json` `{seq, op, target}` against a whitelist including **`reopen-tunnel`** (kills cloudflared, reopens, writes `hub-url`, and **republishes the session descriptor** — `publish_url`, so the panel's next raw read gets the new URL). `restart-hub` and `up-hub` are there too. The panel writes nothing to `control/`.

2. **`openSlot`'s failure message is unconditionally wrong.** `:1302` passes `candidates[candidates.length-1] || ''` as the `zt` argument. `hubCandidates` always ends with the open gate `''` (`:826`), so `zt` is **always** `''` → `describeBaseFailure` always takes the `!String(zt||'')` branch (`:709`) and always prints «Нет токена запуска (zt): адрес отвечает 401» — even when a launch token existed and was rejected. Branches `:712-714` are unreachable from this call site.

3. **`detectSessionConflict` throws away the run it just fetched.** `:532-537` reduces a full run object to the string `'hub'`, and `runHubFlow` (`:1002`) discards it. Meanwhile `s.runId` in the session file is sitting right there, and `preflightHub` already arbitrates on `j.runId` (`:672`). A free, decisive staleness signal — *does the file's runId equal the active run's id* — is being thrown away every time.

4. **There are no timeouts anywhere.** `api()` `:322`, `readHubSessionRaw` `:594`, `preflightHub` `:667` — all bare `fetch`. A half-open TCP connect blocks the probe loop indefinitely. Fatal for any watchdog.

5. **`prog-stop` doesn't stop anything and un-greys buttons mid-flight.** `progAbort` is created at `:280` and **never passed to any fetch**. `:1037` re-enables `launch`/`restart` while the flow is still awaiting, so a second `runHubFlow` can start; both will `location.href`. Same class: `autoPending` (`:1396-1405`) fires `tryOpenLive` unawaited and unlocked, racing `autoLock`'s 3-second `openLast()` (`:900`).

6. **Only two tunnel legs existed in your run.** One «пробую резервный…» line (`:689`, only for `i>0`) ⇒ `sessionBases` returned exactly 2 bases ⇒ `s.ngrok` was empty. Either `NGROK_AUTHTOKEN` is empty (hub.yml prints `::notice::NGROK_AUTHTOKEN secret is empty - the ngrok reserve leg is off`) or the keeper died. Worth checking that run's log before blaming the panel.

7. **`hub/src/main/assets/hub/index.html` is not syntax-checked by CI.** `js-syntax.yml` extracts and `node --check`s the inline script of `agent/hub/index.html` — a *different* page (`<title>Zen Agent</title>`, 1331 lines). Your file, the one on the phone, has no syntax gate at all.

---

## 3. Design, in priority order

**P0 — one honest, authenticated session read.** Extract `readSessionFresh(token, {activeRunId})` → `{s, src, err}` where `src ∈ {raw,api,none}` and `err ∈ {offline, notfound, unauthorized, http}`. It must (a) fetch **both** paths and keep both results, picking the greater `Date.parse(startedAt)` with `runNumber` as tie-break; (b) if the winner's `runId` ≠ `activeRunId`, spend exactly **one** `readHubSessionViaApi` call and prefer that; (c) only return `notfound` when both paths genuinely 404'd — a thrown fetch is `offline`, never `notfound`. `readHubSessionRaw` stays as a thin wrapper so `readHubSession` (`:609`) and the existing suite keep working.

**P1 — `detectSessionConflict` returns `{kind, run}`; `tryOpenLive(token, run)` uses it.** Three lines, the highest value-per-line change in the file. Then inside `tryOpenLive`: drop the `:543` early-out. If `s.runId !== run.id` → «файл сессии от прошлого рана; текущий #N ещё не опубликовал адрес» and fall into the wait path. If `!s` → report `offline`/`notfound` distinctly, never «туннель мёртв».

**P2 — the repair ladder `recoverLive(token, s, run)` → `{ok, base, url, action}`.** Ordered, and the ordering *is* the safety argument:

1. One API re-read + re-probe. (1 quota, 0 destructive.)
2. **Enqueue `reopen-tunnel`**: `GET` `control/queue.json` for the sha, `PUT {seq: Date.now(), op:'reopen-tunnel', target:'hub', from:'panel'}`. Then poll raw (free) every 10 s for ≤120 s for a changed `url`/`ngrok`; on change, re-probe. (2 quota, 0 destructive, keeps the 5h33m run, its repos and its terminals.) If `control/heartbeat-hub.json` is missing or >6 min stale, skip to step 3 — nothing on the runner can heal itself.
3. Only then restart — through `restartRunner` (`:573`), never the inline duplicate at `:986-998`.

**Gate for P2 step 3 — all five must hold:** `isHubRun(run)`; no non-hub session run in `listActiveRuns(isSessionRun)`; `GET /actions/runs/{runId}` confirms an ACTIVE status **twice, 60 s apart** (so a transient API blip can't trigger it); `localStorage.hub_autorepair === '1'`; and a persisted budget of ≤3 restarts / 24 h. Never within 10 min of a run's birth.

**Answer to your explicit question — run alive 5h33m, tunnel dead:** step 2. Reopen the tunnel on the live runner. `tunnel_keeper.sh` already tries this on its own (`MAIN_FAILS >= 3` → `open_main` → `publish_pair`), so often the fresh URL is already on the branch and the panel just never re-read it. The ladder makes the panel a participant instead of a bystander. A restart is the last resort, and by then the blast radius is already bounded: `backup-work.sh` every 300 s and `auto-ship.sh` every 180 s per repo (hub.yml), so the worst case is minutes of unshipped diff — not five hours of session.

**P3 — `runHubFlow`'s message (`:1012`).** Make `tryOpenLive` return `{ok, reason}` with `reason ∈ {opened, offline, notfound, stale-file, still-booting, dead-tunnel, token-mismatch, run-gone}` and one honest sentence each. The string «закрыт чужим токеном запуска» may only appear when at least one probe received an actual HTTP 401 from a hub that answered — today's `:555` regex cannot tell those apart from a dead socket.

**P4 — `openLast` (`:858`) gets the same fallback.** After both stored bases fail: fresh read → `firstReachableBase(sessionBases(s), await hubCandidates(s), s.runId)` → `saveLast` → navigate. This is what actually kills the manual loop, because the 3-second auto-open (`:900`) goes through it.

**P5 — a watchdog, journal-only.** On load, on `visibilitychange`, on `online`: if `readLast()` exists and `!document.hidden`, every 45 s read the session file raw (free). If `s.runId` differs from the one recorded in `hub_last`, or the current base fails two preflights in a row, run the ladder. Single-flight, abortable. **It must never touch `prog*`** — only the journal and a small badge, or it will stomp on a user's in-flight flow.

**P6 — the plumbing the above needs.** One `let flow = null` mutex across `runHubFlow`/`openSlot`/`openLast`/`tryOpenLive`/`autoPending`/`autoLock`; thread `progAbort.signal` into `api()` and `preflightHub` plus `AbortSignal.timeout(8000)`; stop `:1037` from re-enabling buttons until the flow actually returns.

**Explicitly not doing:** reordering `readSlotRaw` (see #6 above), and any "try more hosts" fallback — see risks.

---

## 4. Risks

- **Token safety.** The spare is a real run-scoped credential (it opens the gate). `firstReachableBase` sends *every* candidate to *every* base, so adding bases multiplies exposure. Hard rule for the ladder: **no host outside the session file is ever contacted**, and the queue write goes only to `api.github.com`. Do not add a fallback host list.
- **Quota.** P0 costs ≤1 request per reconnect, not per poll — keep it that way. The real bomb is `waitForRunsToStop` (`:513`, default **400 attempts × 3 s**); when called from auto-repair pass explicit small args. Also kill the fire-and-forget `followRun` at `:942` when the flow ends — it currently keeps polling for 7.5 min after a *successful* open, which compounds badly under a repeating loop.
- **Progress UI.** Any watchdog calling `progStart`/`progFinish` will fight the user. Restrict it to the journal.
- **Offline.** Every tier degrades silently: `navigator.onLine === false` or a failed raw read ⇒ skip the tick, no error, no `progFinish`, no budget spend. A phone in a lift must not accumulate red journal lines.
- **Suite regressions.** `hub-connect-e2e.js` `c16` asserts `cands.list.length === 2` and `c17` calls `window.tryOpenLive('ghp_x')` with one argument — P1 must keep `run` optional. And with `describeBaseFailure`'s call site fixed, `c12b/c13/c14` still pass (they call it directly) but `c18`'s expectation about the openSlot message changes.

---

## 5. Test plan

Tooling: **jsdom, Node, no deps beyond `jsdom`** — `tests/hub-connect-e2e.js` already loads this exact `index.html` (`:5`), stubs `fetch` (`:19`), and drives `tryOpenLive` directly (`c17`). Extend that file; do not create a new harness.

Stub additions needed: a mutable `liveSession` (already exists), a second `contents` branch shape for the flat path, a recorder for `PUT /contents/control/queue.json`, a recorder for `GET .../contents/control/heartbeat-hub.json`, and a `logs` array fed from `#log` after each call.

| id | case |
|---|---|
| `t1` | active run id ≠ file `runId` ⇒ no «ещё не сообщил» line, no `return false` |
| `t2` | raw returns stale, contents returns fresh ⇒ the fresh one wins |
| `t3` | both raw paths parse, `live/` older ⇒ assert the chosen contract explicitly |
| `t4` | both fetches throw ⇒ `err === 'offline'`, **not** `'notfound'` |
| `t5` | all bases dead, run active, heartbeat fresh ⇒ `cancelOrder.length === 0` **and** one `reopen-tunnel` PUT recorded |
| `t6` | after the PUT the next raw poll returns a new url ⇒ returns true, `hub_last` carries the new base |
| `t7` | heartbeat stale + run confirmed active twice + opt-in + budget ⇒ exactly one cancel, one dispatch |
| `t8` | same, budget exhausted ⇒ zero cancels |
| `t9` | openSlot failure with a launch token present ⇒ message names the mismatch, not «нет zt» |
| `t10` | `openLast`, both stored bases dead, fresh live file ⇒ true, `hub_last` updated |
| `t11` | two overlapping watchdog triggers ⇒ one reconcile (count probe calls) |
| `t12` | `prog-stop` mid-`waitForRunsToStop` ⇒ flow aborts, buttons stay disabled until it returns |

Plus one CI fix: add `hub/src/main/assets/hub/index.html` to the inline-script extractor in `.github/workflows/js-syntax.yml` — today only `agent/hub/index.html` is checked, and that is a different page.
</task_result>
</task>

#     - BOTH VMs run this daemon, each with its own CONTROL_TARGET
#     - liveness is verifiable from outside: control/heartbeat-<vm>.json is
#       rewritten every 2 minutes with a process census
#     - this daemon can REPAIR, not only report: reopen-tunnel and up-hub fix
#       the exact failure mode of a dead cloudflared / dead hub server without
#       needing the job's keep-alive step at all

# CHANNEL (session-state branch)
#   control/queue.json             one slot: { seq, op, target?, from? }

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Remote-control + heartbeat daemon for one runner VM (Z10 round 2).
#
# WHY ROUND 2
#   Round 1 proved the queue works, but run 175 showed it lives on the wrong
#   assumption: the workflow starts TWO VMs (hub web + VNC desktop) and the
#   hub VM's agent itself can die, taking every step with it while detached
#   daemons keep breathing. So now:
#     - BOTH VMs run this daemon, each with its own CONTROL_TARGET
#     - liveness is verifiable from outside: control/heartbeat-<vm>.json is
#       rewritten every 2 minutes with a process census
#     - this daemon can REPAIR, not only report: reopen-tunnel and up-hub fix
#       the exact failure mode of a dead cloudflared / dead hub server without
#       needing the job's keep-alive step at all
#
# CHANNEL (session-state branch)
#   control/queue.json             one slot: { seq, op, target?, from? }
#                                  target = hub | vnc | any (default any)
#   control/results/<seq>-<vm>.json per-VM ack
#   control/heartbeat-<vm>.json    liveness + process census every 2 min
#
# WHITELIST (never arbitrary shell)
#   ping, backup-now, handoff-save, restart-hub, up-hub, reopen-tunnel
set -uo pipefail

HUB_LOGS="${HUB_LOGS:-$HOME/.npm-hub/logs}"
mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS" 2>/dev/null || true
VM="${CONTROL_TARGET:-hub}"
log() { echo "[hub-control:$VM $(date -u '+%H:%M:%S')] $*" | tee -a "$HUB_LOGS/hub-control-$VM.log"; }

TOKEN="${GH_TOKEN:-${GITHUB_TOKEN:-}}"
if [ -z "$TOKEN" ]; then
  log "no token - the command queue stays cold"
  exit 1
fi
REPO="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:-sj0404-collab/zen-panel}"
BRANCH="${CONTROL_BRANCH:-session-state}"
INTERVAL="${CONTROL_INTERVAL:-20}"
HEARTBEAT_SEC="${CONTROL_HEARTBEAT_SEC:-120}"
API="https://api.github.com/repos/$REPO/contents"
QUEUE_PATH="control/queue.json"
SEEN_FILE="$HUB_LOGS/hub-control-$VM.seen"
SEEN="$(cat "$SEEN_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
TOOLS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
HUB_PORT="${HUB_PORT:-8090}"

trap 'log "stopped"; exit 0' TERM INT

api_get() {
  local body
  body="$(curl -sf -m 20 -H "Authorization: token $TOKEN" "$API/$1?ref=$BRANCH" 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
  echo "$body"
}

api_put() {
  local b64 sha
  b64="$(printf '%s' "$2" | base64 -w0)"
  sha="$(api_get "$1" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin).get("sha",""))' 2>/dev/null || echo)"
  if [ -n "$sha" ]; then
    curl -sf -m 25 -X PUT -H "Authorization: token $TOKEN" "$API/$1" \
      -d "{\"message\":\"control: ack $1\",\"content\":\"$b64\",\"branch\":\"$BRANCH\",\"sha\":\"$sha\"}" >/dev/null
  else
    curl -sf -m 25 -X PUT -H "Authorization: token $TOKEN" "$API/$1" \
      -d "{\"message\":\"control: ack $1\",\"content\":\"$b64\",\"branch\":\"$BRANCH\"}" >/dev/null
  fi
}

publish_url() {  # $1 = slot, $2 = new tunnel base url (no trailing slash)
  local slot="$1" base="$2" rv
  if [ "$slot" = "hub-linux" ]; then
    rv="$(cat "$HUB_LOGS/hub-url2" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    GH_TOKEN="$TOKEN" bash "$TOOLS_DIR/publish_session.sh" \
      "slot=hub-linux" "kind=NPM-Hub" "os=linux" \
      "url=$base" "hubUrl=$base" "desktop=$base/d" "mobile=$base/m" \
      ${rv:+"url2=$rv"} \
      "auth=без пароля" "label=${HUB_LABEL:-hub}" 2>&1 | tail -1
  else
    rv="$(cat "$HUB_LOGS/vnc-url2" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    GH_TOKEN="$TOKEN" bash "$TOOLS_DIR/publish_session.sh" \
      "slot=vnc" "kind=Linux-VNC" "os=linux" \
      "url=$base/vnc.html" "novncUrl=$base/vnc.html" \
      ${rv:+"url2=$rv"} \
      "label=${HUB_LABEL:-hub}" 2>&1 | tail -1
  fi
}

run_op() {
  local pid url
  case "$1" in
    ping)
      echo "pong from $VM $(date -Iseconds)"
      ;;
    backup-now)
      GH_TOKEN="$TOKEN" GITHUB_TOKEN="$TOKEN" WORK_BACKUP_ROOT="$HOME" \
        bash "$TOOLS_DIR/backup-work.sh" --once
      ;;
    restart-hub)
      pid="$(tr -dc '0-9' < "$HUB_LOGS/hub.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
      if [ -n "${pid:-}" ] && kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
        kill "$pid" && echo "hub pid $pid signalled"
      else
        echo "no live hub pid (already down?)"
      fi
      ;;
    up-hub)
      if [ "$VM" != "hub" ]; then echo "the npm-hub server lives on the hub VM not $VM"; return 0; fi
      pid="$(tr -dc '0-9' < "$HUB_LOGS/hub.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
      [ -n "${pid:-}" ] && kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null && { echo "hub already running (pid $pid)"; return 0; }
      (
        cd "$TOOLS_DIR/../npm-hub" || exit 1
        HUB_PORT_STRICT=1 HUB_TOKEN="${HUB_TOKEN_VALUE:-}" HUB_LABEL="${HUB_LABEL:-hub}" \
          GH_TOKEN="$TOKEN" PORT="$HUB_PORT" \
          SESSION_STARTED_MS="$(cat "$HOME/.npm-hub/session-start" 2>/dev/null || date +%s000)" \
          SESSION_LIMIT_MS=21600000 nohup node src/server.js >> "$HUB_LOGS/hub.log" 2>&1 &
        echo $! > "$HUB_LOGS/hub.pid"
      )
      sleep 2; echo "hub relaunched (pid $(cat "$HUB_LOGS/hub.pid" 2>/dev/null))"
      ;;
    reopen-tunnel)
      local port slot
      if [ "$VM" = "hub" ]; then port=8090; slot=hub-linux; else port=6081; slot=vnc; fi
      pid="$(tr -dc '0-9' < "$HUB_LOGS/cloudflared-$port.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
      [ -n "${pid:-}" ] && kill "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
      pkill -f "cloudflared [t]unnel --url http://127.0.0.1:$port" 2>/dev/null || true
      sleep 1
      url="$(bash "$TOOLS_DIR/open_tunnel.sh" "$port" "$HUB_LOGS/control-tunnel.log" 2>/dev/null || echo)"
      if [ -z "$url" ]; then echo "open_tunnel gave no URL"; return 1; fi
      [ "$VM" = "hub" ] && echo "$url" > "$HUB_LOGS/hub-url" || echo "$url" > "$HUB_LOGS/vnc-url"
      echo "tunnel up: $url"
      publish_url "$slot" "$url"
      ;;
    handoff-save)
      [ "$VM" = "hub" ] || { echo "handoff-save runs on the hub VM"; return 0; }
      GH_TOKEN="$TOKEN" GITHUB_TOKEN="$TOKEN" WORK_BACKUP_ROOT="$HOME" \
        bash "$TOOLS_DIR/handoff.sh"
      ;;
    *)
      echo "unknown op: $1" >&2
      return 64
      ;;
  esac
}

heartbeat() {
  local hb
  hb="$(python3 - <<PYH 2>/dev/null || echo ""
import json, subprocess, datetime
def pc(pat):
    try:
        return subprocess.run(["pgrep","-fc",pat], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10).stdout.strip()
    except Exception:
        return "?"
print(json.dumps({
    "vm": "$VM", "runId": "${GITHUB_RUN_ID:-local}",
    "at": datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"),
    "procs": {
        "hub_server": pc("node src/server.js"),
        "cloudflared": pc("cloudflared [t]unnel"),
        "backup_daemon": pc("[b]ackup-work.sh"),
        "snapshot_daemon": pc("[s]napshot-audit-code.sh"),
        "control_daemon": pc("[h]ub_control.sh"),
        "rescue_ssh": pc("[r]escue_ssh.sh"),
        "tunnel_keeper": pc("[t]unnel_keeper.sh"),
        "ngrok_keeper": pc("[n]grok_keeper.sh"),
    },
}, ensure_ascii=False))
PYH
)"
  [ -n "$hb" ] && api_put "control/heartbeat-$VM.json" "$hb" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
}

log "queue daemon up ($VM) on $BRANCH:$QUEUE_PATH (every ${INTERVAL}s; seen=$SEEN)"
boot_slot="$(api_get "$QUEUE_PATH" || true)"
if [ -n "$boot_slot" ]; then
  boot_seq="$(python3 -c 'import json,sys,base64; print(json.loads(base64.b64decode(json.load(sys.stdin)["content"])).get("seq",0))' <<<"$boot_slot" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
  if [[ "$boot_seq" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [ "$boot_seq" -gt "$SEEN" ] 2>/dev/null; then
    SEEN="$boot_seq"; echo "$SEEN" > "$SEEN_FILE"
    log "queue baseline set to #$SEEN (stale command - not executing)"
  fi
fi
heartbeat
LAST_BEAT=$SECONDS
while true; do
  sleep "$INTERVAL"
  if [ $((SECONDS - LAST_BEAT)) -ge "$HEARTBEAT_SEC" ]; then
    heartbeat; LAST_BEAT=$SECONDS
  fi
  slot="$(api_get "$QUEUE_PATH" || true)"
  [ -n "$slot" ] || continue
  read -r seq op target < <(python3 -c '
import json, sys
try:
    d = json.loads(sys.stdin.read())
    print(int(d.get("seq", 0)), str(d.get("op", ""))[:64], str(d.get("target", "any"))[:16])
except Exception:
    print(0, "", "any")
' <<<"$(python3 -c 'import json,sys,base64; c=json.load(sys.stdin)["content"]; print(base64.b64decode(c).decode(), end="")' <<<"$slot" 2>/dev/null)" 2>/dev/null || echo "0  any")
  [[ "$seq" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || continue
  [ "$seq" -le "$SEEN" ] 2>/dev/null && continue
  [ -n "$op" ] || continue
  { [ "$target" = "any" ] || [ "$target" = "$VM" ]; } || { log "skip #$seq ($op for target=$target)"; echo "$seq" > "$SEEN_FILE"; SEEN="$seq"; continue; }
  log "command #$seq: $op (target=$target)"
  out="$(run_op "$op" 2>&1 | tail -c 3000)"; rc=$?
  log "command #$seq rc=$rc"
  ack="$(python3 -c '
import json, sys, datetime
print(json.dumps({
    "seq": int(sys.argv[1]), "op": sys.argv[2], "vm": sys.argv[4],
    "ok": sys.argv[3] == "0", "rc": int(sys.argv[3]),
    "at": datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"),
    "runId": sys.argv[5],
    "out": sys.stdin.read()[-2800:],
}, ensure_ascii=False))
' "$seq" "$op" "$rc" "$VM" "${GITHUB_RUN_ID:-local}" <<<"$out" 2>/dev/null || echo "{\"seq\":$seq,\"ok\":false}")"
  if api_put "control/results/$seq-$VM.json" "$ack"; then
    echo "$seq" > "$SEEN_FILE"; SEEN="$seq"
  else
    log "ack push failed - the command WILL rerun until pushed"
  fi
done
