**Edit exactly ONE production file: `hub/src/main/assets/hub/index.html`.** Plus tests in `tests/hub-connect-e2e.js` and a CI tweak (see item 8). Do not touch anything else.

# Context: the bug the user is actually hitting

A phone panel user cannot ever reconnect to their hub. Verbatim journal lines from their screenshots:

```
00:40:56 Основной адрес молчит — пробую резервный...
00:40:56 Открыть не вышло: Адрес не отвечает — адрес прошлого запуска уже мёртв. ...жми «Остановить и перезапустить ранер».
01:20:20 Хаб уже запущен. Подбираю доступ...
01:21:03 Адрес хаба молчит (туннель мёртв — ран, скорее всего, остановлен извне). Нажмите «Остановить и перезапустить ранер».
01:25:16 Запуск уже идёт, но адрес хаб ещё не сообщил (или он уже выключен). Подожди пару минут и нажми «Запустить хаб» снова...
```

while the "Последние запуски" card showed **NPM Hub #385 running 5h33m** — the GitHub Actions run is ALIVE. The panel reads a STALE session file from the raw.githubusercontent.com CDN edge and concludes the tunnel is dead. There is a fully-implemented repair channel on the runner that the panel never uses.

# Root cause (already verified — trust this, but re-read the file to place your edits)

`tryOpenLive(token)` at index.html:541 — reached from `runHubFlow('launch')` at :1001-1008 when `detectSessionConflict(token) === 'hub'`:
- line 542 calls **`readHubSessionRaw()` only** (`:591`) — raw.githubusercontent, no token, no API fallback. Compare `waitForHub` at `:639`, which switches to the authenticated REST path after 3 stale reads (`staleReads >= 3`). The file's own comment at `:629-634` documents that the raw edge serves copies minutes old.
- Line 543-546 collapses `!s`, `state !== 'live'` and missing URL into ONE message — that is the verbatim 01:25:16 line.
- Lines 551-562: when every base × token candidate fails with a network-class reason, it prints the verbatim 01:21:03 line and `return false`. **No action.** But `restartRunner` (`:573`) and `cancelAndWait` (`:527`) are right there on the same page. Note `restartRunner` currently has ZERO call sites (dead code); the live restart is an inline duplicate at `:986-998`.
- `openLast()` (`:858`) probes only the two localStorage bases with a single token (`lastOriginToken().zt`, `:860`) — no pending zt, no spare, no `hubCandidates`, and it never re-reads the session file, so the "Открыть последний" button can never self-heal.
- `detectSessionConflict` (`:532-537`) throws away the run object it just fetched, reducing it to the string `'hub'`. `s.runId` in the session file plus that run's id is a free, decisive staleness signal, and `preflightHub` (`:672`) already arbitrates on exactly `j.runId`.
- `openSlot` (`:1237`) calls `describeBaseFailure(bases, probe.errors, candidates[candidates.length-1] || '', !!spare)` at `:1302`. `hubCandidates` (`:813`) always ends with the open gate `''`, so `zt` is ALWAYS `''` → `describeBaseFailure` (`:709`) always takes the "нет токена запуска" branch. Wrong diagnosis even when a launch token existed and was rejected.

# The thing you must wire up (highest value, do it first)

`tools/hub_control.sh` is a runner-side daemon already executing a whitelisted command queue on the `session-state` branch:

- `control/queue.json` — one slot: `{ seq, op, target?, from? }`; `target` = `hub | vnc | any`; `op` whitelist at `hub_control.sh:23` = `ping, backup-now, handoff-save, restart-hub, up-hub, reopen-tunnel`.
- `control/heartbeat-<vm>.json` — rewritten every 2 min with a process census (`hub_control.sh:144-170`).
- `control/results/<seq>-<vm>.json` — per-VM ack.
- **`reopen-tunnel` (`:119-131`)**: kills cloudflared, calls `open_tunnel.sh` for a fresh URL, writes `$HUB_LOGS/hub-url`, and calls `publish_url` (`:68-85`) → `publish_session.sh` which **republishes the session descriptor with the new URL**. So one queue write repairs a dead tunnel on a live runner and the panel's next raw read picks up the new address.
- The daemon writes the heartbeat via `api_put`, i.e. `PUT /repos/$REPO/contents/<path>?ref=session-state` with `{message, content: base64, branch, sha?}`. `sha` is optional (see `api_put` `:55-66`).

The panel currently contains ZERO references to `control/` (`grep -c 'control/' hub/src/main/assets/hub/index.html` → 0). Wiring it up is the whole fix.

Panel-side plumbing that already exists: `api(path, token, opts)` at `:322` (supports `method` + `body`, sends `Authorization: token …`, returns `null` on 404, `true` on 202/204); `parseSessionFile(f)` at `:584` (base64→JSON for a contents response); `GH` and `REPO` at `:200`.

# Implement, in this order

## 1. `readSessionFresh(token, opts)` — one honest, authenticated session read

Returns `{ s, src, err }` where `src ∈ {raw, api, none}` and `err ∈ {offline, notfound, stale-file, unauthorized, http}`.

Requirements:
- Fetch **both** paths (`live/session-hub-linux.json`, `session-hub-linux.json`) and keep both results; pick the one with the greater `Date.parse(s.startedAt || s.updated_at || 0)`, tie-break on `runNumber`/`runId`. (Keep `readHubSessionRaw` as a thin wrapper over the raw-only part so `readHubSession` at `:609` and existing tests keep working.)
- If a winner exists and `opts.activeRunId` is set and `String(s.runId) !== String(opts.activeRunId)`: spend exactly ONE `readHubSessionViaApi(token)` call (`:600`) and prefer that result. This is the whole bug: the raw edge is stale.
- A **thrown** fetch is `err: 'offline'`, NEVER `notfound`. Only return `notfound` when both paths genuinely came back 404/failed-to-parse. Offline must never be reported as "сессия не опубликована".
- Do NOT add any fallback host outside the session file. Token safety: the `spare` is a real run-scoped credential that opens the hub gate (`hubCandidates` `:813`, and `SPARE_TOKEN` in `npm-hub/src/server.js`); `firstReachableBase` sends every candidate to every base, so more bases = more exposure.

## 2. `detectSessionConflict` returns `{ kind, run }`

Keep `kind` exactly as today (`'hub'` / `'other'` / `null`) so `runHubFlow` keeps working, and return the run object. Update the one call site at `:1002`. **`tryOpenLive`'s `run` parameter MUST stay optional** — the existing test `tests/hub-connect-e2e.js` case `c17` calls `window.tryOpenLive('ghp_x')` with a single argument.

## 3. `recoverLive(token, s, run)` — the ordered repair ladder

Return `{ ok, base, zt, url, action, reason }`. The ordering IS the safety argument, do not reorder:

**Step 1 — re-read and re-probe.** One `readSessionFresh` + `firstReachableBase`. 1 API request, 0 destructive.

**Step 2 — `reopen-tunnel` on the live runner.** This is the fix for "run alive 5h33m, tunnel dead"; it keeps the run, its repos and its terminals.
  a. Read `control/heartbeat-hub.json` (raw, free). If it is missing, unparseable, or its `at` is older than 6 minutes → the daemon is dead, skip to step 3.
  b. `GET /repos/${REPO}/contents/control/queue.json?ref=session-state` via `api()`, decode with `parseSessionFile`, read its `seq`.
  c. `PUT /repos/${REPO}/contents/control/queue.json` with body `{message, content: base64(JSON.stringify({seq: <newSeq>, op:'reopen-tunnel', target:'hub', from:'panel'})), branch:'session-state', sha}`. Omit `sha` if the GET returned null. `newSeq` must be strictly greater than the previous seq and greater than `Date.now()`-ish so it is always fresh — the daemon skips any `seq <= SEEN` (`hub_control.sh:199`), so use `Math.max(prevSeq + 1, Date.now())`.
  d. Poll raw `live/session-hub-linux.json` **every 10 s for at most 120 s** (raw is free — do not use the API here) for a `url`/`hubUrl`/`ngrok` that differs from the one we started with. On change, re-probe with `firstReachableBase`. Must be abortable via the shared cancel flag.
  e. Log each step in plain Russian, journal only.

**Step 3 — last resort: restart the runner through `restartRunner` (`:573`)**, never through the inline duplicate at `:986-998`. Wire `runHubFlow`'s `kind === 'restart'` branch to call `restartRunner` instead of duplicating it, and delete the duplicate.

**GATE — step 3 must fire only when ALL of these hold** (any one missing → stop and report honestly, do not cancel anything):
  - `run` is present and `isHubRun(run)`;
  - `listActiveRuns(token, isSessionRun)` shows no non-hub session run;
  - `GET /repos/${REPO}/actions/runs/{runId}` confirms an ACTIVE status **twice, 60 s apart**, so a transient API blip cannot trigger it;
  - `localStorage.getItem('hub_autorepair') === '1'`;
  - a persisted budget of at most 3 restarts per rolling 24 h is not exhausted;
  - the run is at least 10 minutes old (never restart a run that just started).

**Explicit answer to the design question:** for "run alive 5h33m, tunnel dead" the answer is step 2, NOT a restart. A restart is only correct once the tunnel keeper has provably had its chance and failed.

## 4. Honest diagnostics

Make `tryOpenLive` return `{ ok, reason }` with `reason ∈ {opened, offline, notfound, stale-file, still-booting, dead-tunnel, token-mismatch, run-gone}`.

- The string «закрыт чужим токеном запуска» may **only** appear when at least one probe got a real HTTP 401 from a hub that actually answered. Today the regex at `:555` cannot distinguish a 401 from a dead socket — that is why the user is told the wrong thing.
- Inside `tryOpenLive`, drop the `:543` early-out. If `s.runId !== run.id` → say «файл сессии от прошлого рана; текущий #N ещё не опубликовал адрес» and fall into the wait path (`waitForHub`).
- Update `runHubFlow`'s `progFinish(false, ...)` at `:1012` to state the real reason.

## 5. `openLast()` (`:858`) gets the same fallback

After both stored bases fail: fresh `readSessionFresh` → `firstReachableBase(sessionBases(s), await hubCandidates(s), s.runId)` → `saveLast` → navigate. This is what actually kills the manual loop, because the 3-second auto-open at `:900` routes through `openLast`.

## 6. Watchdog (journal-only, never touches `prog*`)

On load, on `visibilitychange`, and on `online`: if `readLast()` exists and `document.hidden` is false, every 45 s do a **raw** (free) session read. If `s.runId` differs from the one recorded in `hub_last`, or the current base fails two preflights in a row, run the ladder. Single-flight and abortable.
- Skip the tick silently when `navigator.onLine === false` or the raw read threw. No red journal lines, no `progFinish`, no budget spend while offline.
- Never call `progStart`/`progFinish`/`busy` — it will stomp on a user's in-flight flow.

## 7. Plumbing the above needs

- One `let flow = null` mutex across `runHubFlow`, `openSlot`, `openLast`, `tryOpenLive`, `autoPending` (`:1396-1405`) and `autoLock` (`:887-912`). `autoPending` currently fires `tryOpenLive` unawaited and unlocked, racing `autoLock`'s 3-second `openLast()`.
- Thread timeouts into the fetches: `api()` (`:322`), `readHubSessionRaw` (`:594`) and `preflightHub` (`:667`) are all bare `fetch` with no timeout — a half-open TCP connect blocks the probe loop forever. Use `AbortSignal.timeout(8000)` (and compose with the flow's cancel signal where you can).
- `$('prog-stop')` at `:1037` re-enables `launch`/`restart` while the flow is still awaiting, so a second `runHubFlow` can start and both will `location.href`. Do not re-enable until the flow actually returns. (`progAbort` is created at `:280` and never passed to any fetch — either wire it or delete it.)
- Kill the fire-and-forget `followRun` at `:942` when the flow ends; it keeps polling for 7.5 min after a *successful* open, which compounds badly under a repeating watchdog.

## 8. CI + tests

- `.github/workflows/js-syntax.yml` currently `node --check`s the inline script of `agent/hub/index.html` — a **different page**. Add `hub/src/main/assets/hub/index.html` to the extractor so the page the user actually runs gets a syntax gate.
- Extend `tests/hub-connect-e2e.js` (jsdom + Node; it already loads this exact file at `:5` and stubs `fetch` at `:19`). Do NOT create a new harness. Keep cases `c1`–`c18` passing unless an expectation is provably wrong (`c18` asserts the openSlot failure message, which you are deliberately changing — update it and say why in the commit body). Add stubs: a second contents-branch shape for the flat path, a recorder for `PUT /contents/control/queue.json`, a recorder for `GET .../contents/control/heartbeat-hub.json`, and a journal recorder fed from `#log`.

Cases to add (ids are suggestions): `t1` active run id ≠ file `runId` ⇒ no «ещё не сообщил» line and no bare `return false`; `t2` raw stale + contents fresh ⇒ fresh wins; `t3` both raw paths parse ⇒ assert the documented pick; `t4` both fetches throw ⇒ `err === 'offline'`, NOT `'notfound'`; `t5` all bases dead + run active + heartbeat fresh ⇒ zero cancels AND exactly one `reopen-tunnel` PUT; `t6` after the PUT the next raw poll returns a new url ⇒ returns true and `hub_last` carries the new base; `t7` heartbeat stale + run confirmed active twice + opt-in + budget ⇒ exactly one cancel and one dispatch; `t8` same but budget exhausted ⇒ zero cancels; `t9` openSlot failure WITH a launch token present ⇒ message names the mismatch, not «нет zt»; `t10` `openLast`, both stored bases dead, fresh live file ⇒ true, `hub_last` updated; `t11` two overlapping watchdog triggers ⇒ one reconcile.

# Non-negotiables

- The page must never require a manual button press to recover. That is the user's explicit ask.
- Never kill a healthy run to fix a dead tunnel. The ladder order is the safety argument.
- Never contact a host that is not in the session file, and never put a raw GitHub token in a URL.
- Keep GitHub API quota in mind: raw is free, the API costs quota. `waitForRunsToStop` (`:513`) defaults to **400 attempts × 3 s** — when called from auto-repair, pass small explicit args.
- Preserve the existing style: 2-space indent, Russian journal strings, explanatory comments in the same voice as the surrounding ones (they explain *why*, not *what*).
- User-facing strings in Russian; code identifiers/comments in the file's existing mixed style.

# Verify before you report

- Run the repo's test suite the way the repo runs it — read `TESTING.md` and `.github/workflows/tests.yml` and use the real command.
- Confirm `grep -c 'control/' hub/src/main/assets/hub/index.html` is now non-zero.

прогнать руками, и какие поломки известны прямо сейчас.

Документ описывает **проверку**, а не разработку. Каждому пункту дан ID
(`T-xx`), чтобы результат можно было отметить и не потерять.

---

## 0. Текущее состояние (на момент последней правки)

| Область | Состояние |
|---|---|
| `node --check` по JS | зелёный (`JS syntax`) |
| `bash -n` по `tools/*.sh` и всем `run:`-шагам | зелёный (проверено вручную, в CI напрямую нет) |
| 11 сьютов в `tests/` (10 js + 1 shell) | зелёные в CI |
| Из них без зависимостей (7 сьютов) | зелёные локально на Windows: 291 проверка, 1 осознанный skip |
| Сборка APK | зелёная: `v1.299`, `hub-v1.299` (коммит `ab63545`) |
| Живой прогон сессии | подтверждён 26.09: запуск → туннель → отмена → слоты `ended` |
| Живой прогон с `HUB_TOKEN` (gate) | **не проверен** — сервер со стартом на gate вживую не запускался |
| Ручные сценарии (VNC, терминалы, файлы, git, mobile) | **не проводились** |

Пробелы покрытия перечислены в §4.

---

## 1. Уровни проверки

| Уровень | Что ловит | Как запустить | Когда |
|---|---|---|---|
| L0 Синтаксис | опечатки в JS/YAML/sh | `JS syntax` (CI) | на каждый push |
| L1 Регрессия UI | логика панелей и хаба без сети | `Tests` (CI) → `tests/npm test` | на каждый push |
| L2 Shell | синтаксис и логика `tools/*.sh` | `bash -n tools/*.sh`, `tests/work-backup-test.sh` | локально перед коммитом |
| L3 Интеграция | живой runner: туннель, PTY, VNC, gate | ручной прогон сессии | после изменения `npm-hub/src` или workflows |
| L4 Приёмка | сценарий целиком на телефоне | ручной чек-лист §3 | перед релизом APK |

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Remote-control + heartbeat daemon for one runner VM (Z10 round 2).
#
# WHY ROUND 2
#   Round 1 proved the queue works, but run 175 showed it lives on the wrong
#   assumption: the workflow starts TWO VMs (hub web + VNC desktop) and the
#   hub VM's agent itself can die, taking every step with it while detached
#   daemons keep breathing. So now:
#     - BOTH VMs run this daemon, each with its own CONTROL_TARGET
#     - liveness is verifiable from outside: control/heartbeat-<vm>.json is
#       rewritten every 2 minutes with a process census
#     - this daemon can REPAIR, not only report: reopen-tunnel and up-hub fix
#       the exact failure mode of a dead cloudflared / dead hub server without
#       needing the job's keep-alive step at all
#
# CHANNEL (session-state branch)
#   control/queue.json             one slot: { seq, op, target?, from? }
#                                  target = hub | vnc | any (default any)
#   control/results/<seq>-<vm>.json per-VM ack
#   control/heartbeat-<vm>.json    liveness + process census every 2 min
#
# WHITELIST (never arbitrary shell)
#   ping, backup-now, handoff-save, restart-hub, up-hub, reopen-tunnel
set -uo pipefail

HUB_LOGS="${HUB_LOGS:-$HOME/.npm-hub/logs}"
mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS" 2>/dev/null || true
VM="${CONTROL_TARGET:-hub}"
log() { echo "[hub-control:$VM $(date -u '+%H:%M:%S')] $*" | tee -a "$HUB_LOGS/hub-control-$VM.log"; }

TOKEN="${GH_TOKEN:-${GITHUB_TOKEN:-}}"
if [ -z "$TOKEN" ]; then
  log "no token - the command queue stays cold"
  exit 1
fi
REPO="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:-sj0404-collab/zen-panel}"
BRANCH="${CONTROL_BRANCH:-session-state}"
INTERVAL="${CONTROL_INTERVAL:-20}"
HEARTBEAT_SEC="${CONTROL_HEARTBEAT_SEC:-120}"
API="https://api.github.com/repos/$REPO/contents"
QUEUE_PATH="control/queue.json"
SEEN_FILE="$HUB_LOGS/hub-control-$VM.seen"
SEEN="$(cat "$SEEN_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
TOOLS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
HUB_PORT="${HUB_PORT:-8090}"

trap 'log "stopped"; exit 0' TERM INT

api_get() {
  local body
  body="$(curl -sf -m 20 -H "Authorization: token $TOKEN" "$API/$1?ref=$BRANCH" 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
  echo "$body"
}

api_put() {
  local b64 sha
  b64="$(printf '%s' "$2" | base64 -w0)"
  sha="$(api_get "$1" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin).get("sha",""))' 2>/dev/null || echo)"
  if [ -n "$sha" ]; then
    curl -sf -m 25 -X PUT -H "Authorization: token $TOKEN" "$API/$1" \
      -d "{\"message\":\"control: ack $1\",\"content\":\"$b64\",\"branch\":\"$BRANCH\",\"sha\":\"$sha\"}" >/dev/null
  else
    curl -sf -m 25 -X PUT -H "Authorization: token $TOKEN" "$API/$1" \
      -d "{\"message\":\"control: ack $1\",\"content\":\"$b64\",\"branch\":\"$BRANCH\"}" >/dev/null
  fi
}

publish_url() {  # $1 = slot, $2 = new tunnel base url (no trailing slash)
  local slot="$1" base="$2" rv
  if [ "$slot" = "hub-linux" ]; then
    rv="$(cat "$HUB_LOGS/hub-url2" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    GH_TOKEN="$TOKEN" bash "$TOOLS_DIR/publish_session.sh" \
      "slot=hub-linux" "kind=NPM-Hub" "os=linux" \
      "url=$base" "hubUrl=$base" "desktop=$base/d" "mobile=$base/m" \
      ${rv:+"url2=$rv"} \
      "auth=без пароля" "label=${HUB_LABEL:-hub}" 2>&1 | tail -1
  else
    rv="$(cat "$HUB_LOGS/vnc-url2" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    GH_TOKEN="$TOKEN" bash "$TOOLS_DIR/publish_session.sh" \
      "slot=vnc" "kind=Linux-VNC" "os=linux" \
      "url=$base/vnc.html" "novncUrl=$base/vnc.html" \
      ${rv:+"url2=$rv"} \
      "label=${HUB_LABEL:-hub}" 2>&1 | tail -1
  fi
}

run_op() {
  local pid url
  case "$1" in
    ping)
      echo "pong from $VM $(date -Iseconds)"
      ;;
    backup-now)
      GH_TOKEN="$TOKEN" GITHUB_TOKEN="$TOKEN" WORK_BACKUP_ROOT="$HOME" \
        bash "$TOOLS_DIR/backup-work.sh" --once
      ;;
    restart-hub)
      pid="$(tr -dc '0-9' < "$HUB_LOGS/hub.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
      if [ -n "${pid:-}" ] && kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
        kill "$pid" && echo "hub pid $pid signalled"
      else
        echo "no live hub pid (already down?)"
      fi
      ;;
    up-hub)
      if [ "$VM" != "hub" ]; then echo "the npm-hub server lives on the hub VM not $VM"; return 0; fi
      pid="$(tr -dc '0-9' < "$HUB_LOGS/hub.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
      [ -n "${pid:-}" ] && kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null && { echo "hub already running (pid $pid)"; return 0; }
      (
        cd "$TOOLS_DIR/../npm-hub" || exit 1
        HUB_PORT_STRICT=1 HUB_TOKEN="${HUB_TOKEN_VALUE:-}" HUB_LABEL="${HUB_LABEL:-hub}" \
          GH_TOKEN="$TOKEN" PORT="$HUB_PORT" \
          SESSION_STARTED_MS="$(cat "$HOME/.npm-hub/session-start" 2>/dev/null || date +%s000)" \
          SESSION_LIMIT_MS=21600000 nohup node src/server.js >> "$HUB_LOGS/hub.log" 2>&1 &
        echo $! > "$HUB_LOGS/hub.pid"
      )
      sleep 2; echo "hub relaunched (pid $(cat "$HUB_LOGS/hub.pid" 2>/dev/null))"
      ;;
    reopen-tunnel)
      local port slot
      if [ "$VM" = "hub" ]; then port=8090; slot=hub-linux; else port=6081; slot=vnc; fi
      pid="$(tr -dc '0-9' < "$HUB_LOGS/cloudflared-$port.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
      [ -n "${pid:-}" ] && kill "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
      pkill -f "cloudflared [t]unnel --url http://127.0.0.1:$port" 2>/dev/null || true
      sleep 1
      url="$(bash "$TOOLS_DIR/open_tunnel.sh" "$port" "$HUB_LOGS/control-tunnel.log" 2>/dev/null || echo)"
      if [ -z "$url" ]; then echo "open_tunnel gave no URL"; return 1; fi
      [ "$VM" = "hub" ] && echo "$url" > "$HUB_LOGS/hub-url" || echo "$url" > "$HUB_LOGS/vnc-url"
      echo "tunnel up: $url"
      publish_url "$slot" "$url"
      ;;
    handoff-save)
      [ "$VM" = "hub" ] || { echo "handoff-save runs on the hub VM"; return 0; }
      GH_TOKEN="$TOKEN" GITHUB_TOKEN="$TOKEN" WORK_BACKUP_ROOT="$HOME" \
        bash "$TOOLS_DIR/handoff.sh"
      ;;
    *)
      echo "unknown op: $1" >&2
      return 64
      ;;
  esac
}

heartbeat() {
  local hb
  hb="$(python3 - <<PYH 2>/dev/null || echo ""
import json, subprocess, datetime
def pc(pat):
    try:
        return subprocess.run(["pgrep","-fc",pat], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10).stdout.strip()
    except Exception:
        return "?"
print(json.dumps({
    "vm": "$VM", "runId": "${GITHUB_RUN_ID:-local}",
    "at": datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"),
    "procs": {
        "hub_server": pc("node src/server.js"),
        "cloudflared": pc("cloudflared [t]unnel"),
        "backup_daemon": pc("[b]ackup-work.sh"),
        "snapshot_daemon": pc("[s]napshot-audit-code.sh"),
        "control_daemon": pc("[h]ub_control.sh"),
        "rescue_ssh": pc("[r]escue_ssh.sh"),
        "tunnel_keeper": pc("[t]unnel_keeper.sh"),
        "ngrok_keeper": pc("[n]grok_keeper.sh"),
    },
}, ensure_ascii=False))
PYH
)"
  [ -n "$hb" ] && api_put "control/heartbeat-$VM.json" "$hb" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
}

log "queue daemon up ($VM) on $BRANCH:$QUEUE_PATH (every ${INTERVAL}s; seen=$SEEN)"
boot_slot="$(api_get "$QUEUE_PATH" || true)"
if [ -n "$boot_slot" ]; then
  boot_seq="$(python3 -c 'import json,sys,base64; print(json.loads(base64.b64decode(json.load(sys.stdin)["content"])).get("seq",0))' <<<"$boot_slot" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
  if [[ "$boot_seq" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [ "$boot_seq" -gt "$SEEN" ] 2>/dev/null; then
    SEEN="$boot_seq"; echo "$SEEN" > "$SEEN_FILE"
    log "queue baseline set to #$SEEN (stale command - not executing)"
  fi
fi
heartbeat
LAST_BEAT=$SECONDS
while true; do
  sleep "$INTERVAL"
  if [ $((SECONDS - LAST_BEAT)) -ge "$HEARTBEAT_SEC" ]; then
    heartbeat; LAST_BEAT=$SECONDS
  fi
  slot="$(api_get "$QUEUE_PATH" || true)"
  [ -n "$slot" ] || continue
  read -r seq op target < <(python3 -c '
import json, sys

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Remote-control + heartbeat daemon for one runner VM (Z10 round 2).
#
# WHY ROUND 2
#   Round 1 proved the queue works, but run 175 showed it lives on the wrong
#   assumption: the workflow starts TWO VMs (hub web + VNC desktop) and the
#   hub VM's agent itself can die, taking every step with it while detached
#   daemons keep breathing. So now:
#     - BOTH VMs run this daemon, each with its own CONTROL_TARGET
#     - liveness is verifiable from outside: control/heartbeat-<vm>.json is
#       rewritten every 2 minutes with a process census
#     - this daemon can REPAIR, not only report: reopen-tunnel and up-hub fix
#       the exact failure mode of a dead cloudflared / dead hub server without
#       needing the job's keep-alive step at all

# CHANNEL (session-state branch)
#   control/queue.json             one slot: { seq, op, target?, from? }
#                                  target = hub | vnc | any (default any)
#   control/results/<seq>-<vm>.json per-VM ack
#   control/heartbeat-<vm>.json    liveness + process census every 2 min
#
# WHITELIST (never arbitrary shell)
#   ping, backup-now, handoff-save, restart-hub, up-hub, reopen-tunnel
set -uo pipefail

HUB_LOGS="${HUB_LOGS:-$HOME/.npm-hub/logs}"
mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS" 2>/dev/null || true
VM="${CONTROL_TARGET:-hub}"
log() { echo "[hub-control:$VM $(date -u '+%H:%M:%S')] $*" | tee -a "$HUB_LOGS/hub-control-$VM.log"; }

TOKEN="${GH_TOKEN:-${GITHUB_TOKEN:-}}"
if [ -z "$TOKEN" ]; then
  log "no token - the command queue stays cold"
  exit 1
fi
REPO="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:-sj0404-collab/zen-panel}"
BRANCH="${CONTROL_BRANCH:-session-state}"
INTERVAL="${CONTROL_INTERVAL:-20}"
HEARTBEAT_SEC="${CONTROL_HEARTBEAT_SEC:-120}"
API="https://api.github.com/repos/$REPO/contents"
QUEUE_PATH="control/queue.json"
SEEN_FILE="$HUB_LOGS/hub-control-$VM.seen"
SEEN="$(cat "$SEEN_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
TOOLS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
HUB_PORT="${HUB_PORT:-8090}"

trap 'log "stopped"; exit 0' TERM INT

api_get() {
  local body
  body="$(curl -sf -m 20 -H "Authorization: token $TOKEN" "$API/$1?ref=$BRANCH" 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
  echo "$body"
}

api_put() {
  local b64 sha
  b64="$(printf '%s' "$2" | base64 -w0)"
  sha="$(api_get "$1" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin).get("sha",""))' 2>/dev/null || echo)"
  if [ -n "$sha" ]; then
    curl -sf -m 25 -X PUT -H "Authorization: token $TOKEN" "$API/$1" \
      -d "{\"message\":\"control: ack $1\",\"content\":\"$b64\",\"branch\":\"$BRANCH\",\"sha\":\"$sha\"}" >/dev/null
  else
    curl -sf -m 25 -X PUT -H "Authorization: token $TOKEN" "$API/$1" \
      -d "{\"message\":\"control: ack $1\",\"content\":\"$b64\",\"branch\":\"$BRANCH\"}" >/dev/null
  fi
}

publish_url() {  # $1 = slot, $2 = new tunnel base url (no trailing slash)
  local slot="$1" base="$2" rv
  if [ "$slot" = "hub-linux" ]; then
    rv="$(cat "$HUB_LOGS/hub-url2" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    GH_TOKEN="$TOKEN" bash "$TOOLS_DIR/publish_session.sh" \
      "slot=hub-linux" "kind=NPM-Hub" "os=linux" \
      "url=$base" "hubUrl=$base" "desktop=$base/d" "mobile=$base/m" \
      ${rv:+"url2=$rv"} \
      "auth=без пароля" "label=${HUB_LABEL:-hub}" 2>&1 | tail -1
  else
    rv="$(cat "$HUB_LOGS/vnc-url2" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    GH_TOKEN="$TOKEN" bash "$TOOLS_DIR/publish_session.sh" \
      "slot=vnc" "kind=Linux-VNC" "os=linux" \
      "url=$base/vnc.html" "novncUrl=$base/vnc.html" \
      ${rv:+"url2=$rv"} \
      "label=${HUB_LABEL:-hub}" 2>&1 | tail -1
  fi
}

run_op() {
  local pid url
  case "$1" in
    ping)
      echo "pong from $VM $(date -Iseconds)"
      ;;
    backup-now)
      GH_TOKEN="$TOKEN" GITHUB_TOKEN="$TOKEN" WORK_BACKUP_ROOT="$HOME" \
        bash "$TOOLS_DIR/backup-work.sh" --once
      ;;
    restart-hub)
      pid="$(tr -dc '0-9' < "$HUB_LOGS/hub.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
      if [ -n "${pid:-}" ] && kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
        kill "$pid" && echo "hub pid $pid signalled"
      else
        echo "no live hub pid (already down?)"
      fi
      ;;
    up-hub)
      if [ "$VM" != "hub" ]; then echo "the npm-hub server lives on the hub VM not $VM"; return 0; fi
      pid="$(tr -dc '0-9' < "$HUB_LOGS/hub.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
      [ -n "${pid:-}" ] && kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null && { echo "hub already running (pid $pid)"; return 0; }
      (
        cd "$TOOLS_DIR/../npm-hub" || exit 1
        HUB_PORT_STRICT=1 HUB_TOKEN="${HUB_TOKEN_VALUE:-}" HUB_LABEL="${HUB_LABEL:-hub}" \
          GH_TOKEN="$TOKEN" PORT="$HUB_PORT" \
          SESSION_STARTED_MS="$(cat "$HOME/.npm-hub/session-start" 2>/dev/null || date +%s000)" \
          SESSION_LIMIT_MS=21600000 nohup node src/server.js >> "$HUB_LOGS/hub.log" 2>&1 &
        echo $! > "$HUB_LOGS/hub.pid"
      )
      sleep 2; echo "hub relaunched (pid $(cat "$HUB_LOGS/hub.pid" 2>/dev/null))"
      ;;
    reopen-tunnel)
      local port slot
      if [ "$VM" = "hub" ]; then port=8090; slot=hub-linux; else port=6081; slot=vnc; fi
      pid="$(tr -dc '0-9' < "$HUB_LOGS/cloudflared-$port.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
      [ -n "${pid:-}" ] && kill "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
      pkill -f "cloudflared [t]unnel --url http://127.0.0.1:$port" 2>/dev/null || true
      sleep 1
      url="$(bash "$TOOLS_DIR/open_tunnel.sh" "$port" "$HUB_LOGS/control-tunnel.log" 2>/dev/null || echo)"
      if [ -z "$url" ]; then echo "open_tunnel gave no URL"; return 1; fi
      [ "$VM" = "hub" ] && echo "$url" > "$HUB_LOGS/hub-url" || echo "$url" > "$HUB_LOGS/vnc-url"
      echo "tunnel up: $url"
      publish_url "$slot" "$url"
      ;;
    handoff-save)
      [ "$VM" = "hub" ] || { echo "handoff-save runs on the hub VM"; return 0; }
      GH_TOKEN="$TOKEN" GITHUB_TOKEN="$TOKEN" WORK_BACKUP_ROOT="$HOME" \
        bash "$TOOLS_DIR/handoff.sh"
      ;;
    *)
      echo "unknown op: $1" >&2
      return 64
      ;;
  esac
}

def pc(pat):
    try:

    except Exception:

        "tunnel_keeper": pc("[t]unnel_keeper.sh"),
        "ngrok_keeper": pc("[n]grok_keeper.sh"),
    },
}, ensure_ascii=False))
PYH
)"

log "queue daemon up ($VM) on $BRANCH:$QUEUE_PATH (every ${INTERVAL}s; seen=$SEEN)"
boot_slot="$(api_get "$QUEUE_PATH" || true)"
if [ -n "$boot_slot" ]; then

parts.text:
Repo: /home/runner/work/zen-panel/zen-panel/fork — "Zen Panel", an Android panel + GitHub-Actions-based "NPM Hub" runner. Main UI under test: `hub/src/main/assets/hub/index.html` (single 1408-line file, vanilla JS).

## User report (from phone screenshots, decoded)

The user cannot connect to their hub/runner. Verbatim log lines from the journal:

```
00:37:33 Список сессий: Failed to fetch
00:39:53 Список сессий: Failed to fetch

00:40:56 Открыть не вышло: Адрес не отвечает — адрес прошлого запуска уже мёртв. Если хаб жив — «Запустить хаб» подберёт доступ, иначе жми «Остановить и перезапустить ранер».
00:41:48 Список сессий: Failed to fetch
00:41:58 Основной адрес молчит — пробую резервный...
00:41:58 Открыть не вышло: Адрес не отвечает — адрес прошлого запуска уже мёртв...

01:19:56 Основной адрес молчит — пробую резервный...
01:19:56 Открыть не вышло: Адрес не отвечает — адрес прошлого запуска уже мёртв...
01:20:20 Хаб уже запущен. Подбираю доступ...
01:21:03 Основной адрес молчит — пробую резервный...
01:21:03 Адрес хаба молчит (туннель мёртв — ран, скорее всего, остановлен извне). Нажмите «Остановить и перезапустить ранер».
01:25:16 Запуск уже идёт, но адрес хаб ещё не сообщил (или он уже выключен). Подожди пару минут и нажми «Запустить хаб» снова — страница подключится к уже идущему.
```

Meanwhile the "Последние запуски" card showed **NPM Hub Build #385 running for 5h33m** — i.e. the GitHub Actions run IS alive. So: run alive, but the panel can never reconnect. The user is trapped in a manual loop: press "Запустить хаб" → "Хаб уже запущен. Подбираю доступ…" → "Адрес хаба молчит (туннель мёртв)…" → dead end, must manually press "Остановить и перезапустить ранер".

## User's explicit goals
1. Fix the connection bug so it self-heals.
2. "хочу чтобы аи мог работать автоматически без моего вмешательства" — the panel must recover on its own, no manual button presses.
3. Earlier user asked: can the runner live in Docker so they connect by IP? (Not the main ask now; just context that they want the runner always-on and reachable by a stable address.)
4. Earlier: agent needs full access including /tmp, download and install packages — so full-auto operation must not be sandboxed away.

## Code facts I already established (verify, don't trust blindly)

- `tryOpenLive(token)` — index.html:541. Called from `runHubFlow('launch')` when `detectSessionConflict(token) === 'hub'` (index.html:1001-1008).
- `tryOpenLive` line 542 reads the session file via **`readHubSessionRaw()` ONLY** — never the authenticated API path.
- `readHubSessionRaw()` — index.html:591 — fetches `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/${REPO}/session-state/{live/session-hub-linux.json, session-hub-linux.json}?t=<cachebust>`, no token.
- The file itself already documents (index.html:629-634) that **raw.githubusercontent.com serves edge copies that can be minutes stale**, and that `waitForHub()` therefore switches to the REST contents API after 3 stale reads (`staleReads >= 3`). **`tryOpenLive` has no such fallback.**
- Consequence A: `tryOpenLive` reads a stale `state:'ended'` file → prints the exact 01:25:16 message "Запуск уже идёт, но адрес хаб ещё не сообщил (или он уже выключен)" → returns false, even though the hub is live and its address is published. Dead end.
- Consequence B: `tryOpenLive` reads a stale `state:'live'` file holding the PREVIOUS run's dead ngrok URL → probes it → "Failed to fetch" → prints the exact 01:21:03 message "Адрес хаба молчит (туннель мёртв...)" → returns false. Dead end.
- `firstReachableBase(bases, ztOrCandidates, runId)` — index.html:685. Walks bases × token candidates, returns `{base, zt, errors}`; every failure reason is collected in `errors[]`.
- When ALL probes fail with network-class reasons (`/failed to fetch|networkerror|load failed/i`), `tryOpenLive` lines 554-557 concludes "туннель мёртв" and tells the user to press the restart button manually. No automatic action is taken, even though `restartRunner(token, zt, runner)` (index.html:573) and `cancelAndWait(token)` (index.html:527) exist on the very same page and do exactly the needed work.
- `runHubFlow('launch')` lines 1005-1008: when `tryOpenLive` returns false it calls `progFinish(false, 'Доступ не подошёл — хаб закрыт чужим токеном запуска. Нажми «Остановить и перезапустить ранер».')` — i.e. the false diagnosis "чужим токеном" is printed even when the real cause was a dead tunnel or a stale read.

Now let me look at the test suite files, particularly hub-gate-test.js and hub-connect-e2e.js, and tests/package.json to understand the testing style.

Also let me verify specific claims:

1. `tryOpenLive(token)` at line 541 reads session via `readHubSessionRaw()` only — CONFIRMED, line 542.
2. `readHubSessionRaw()` at 591 — CONFIRMED (well, the function starts at 591 with the comment at 588-590; `async function readHubSessionRaw() {` is at line 591). It fetches both paths raw, no token. CONFIRMED.
3. Stale detection in waitForHub at staleReads >= 3, line 639. CONFIRMED. tryOpenLive has no such fallback. CONFIRMED.
4. Consequence A: tryOpenLive reads stale `state:'ended'` → prints "Запуск уже идёт, но адрес хаб ещё не сообщил (или он уже выключен)" line 544. CONFIRMED. Note: BUT — is it truly a stale read? If state is 'ended' and the run is alive, that's a stale read. Actually also could be genuinely: run alive but hub session ended (hub process died but the run is doing other steps?). Hmm. Either way, tryOpenLive doesn't check the run state.
5. Consequence B: stale `live` file with previous run's dead ngrok URL → probe fails → "Адрес хаба молчит (туннель мёртв…)" at line 557. CONFIRMED.
6. `firstReachableBase` at 685 — CONFIRMED. Errors collected. Note that it logs "Основной адрес молчит — пробую резервный…" at 689 for i>0. That matches the log lines at 00:40:56 / 01:19:56 — so `bases.length > 1`, meaning sessionBases returned 2+ bases (ngrok + hubUrl/url + url2 — with dedup). So the reserve base exists. Both bases failed → but only ONE "пробую резервный" line appears, meaning bases.length === 2 exactly.

Wait — an important detail: the log line "Основной адрес молчит — пробую резервный…" appears once per i>0. With 3 bases you'd see it twice. In the screenshot-1 case (00:40:56) we see one, so bases.length==2. That means `s.ngrok` and `s.hubUrl||s.url` differ, and `s.url2` either missing or equal. Good detail.

Hmm, but there's a subtlety: `firstReachableBase` loops bases outer, candidates inner. So for i=0 (main base) it tries ALL token candidates (up to 4 fetches) before moving to base 1. So a single "пробую резервный" means base 0 failed on all candidates.

7. When ALL probes fail network-class → tryOpenLive says "туннель мёртв" and tells user to press restart manually — lines 554-557. CONFIRMED, no auto action.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Publish the live session's connection details so the panel can show them.
#
# The job summary already prints the address, user and password, but it is
# prose meant for a human with a browser: not machine-readable, and on a phone
# it is several taps behind the Actions UI. The panel is where the session is
# started, so it is where the credentials belong.
#
# They go to an orphan branch, session-state, as session.json. An orphan branch
# keeps this churn out of the history of main and lets the file be replaced
# wholesale every time without ever conflicting.
#
# WHO CAN READ THIS
#   On a public repository the branch is public, and so is the password in it.
#   That is the same exposure as the run summary, which is also public - but it
#   is worth being explicit, because a password on a web page feels different
#   from one in a log. Everything here dies with the runner within six hours,
#   and any secret in it is regenerated per run. If that is not acceptable,
#   make the repository private; the panel reads it with the same token either
#   way.
#
# TWO DESKS AT ONCE
#   Pass slot=linux, slot=windows or slot=agent and the entry lands in its own
#   file - session-linux.json, session-windows.json, session-agent.json,
#   session-opencode.json and session-hub.json - so
#   agent/opencode/hub take an -linux/-windows suffix (one file per OS, so two
#   runners stop overwriting each other); the bare slot stays for old runs.
#   the two desks and the agent never overwrite each other. Without a slot the
#   old single session.json is used, which keeps the older workflows working
#   unchanged.
#
#   The panel reads all three and shows whichever are live.
#
# MODELS AND SAVED SNAPSHOTS
#   Sessions alone do not survive usefully: which model answered, which died,
#   which recovered - that roster lives in ~/.zen_free_models.json on the
#   runner and dies with it. So every session also publishes its models:

#       kind=CLI-агент json=$HOME/.zen_free_models.json
#   file= overrides the target on the branch (validated: only the known
#   mailboxes are accepted, so a typo cannot spray files across the branch).
#   json= merges a local JSON file into the payload - with secrets scrubbed:
#   any key looking like a key/token/secret/password is dropped, because
#   opencode.json holds API keys and this branch may be public. Pass scrub=0
#   to disable.
#
# LAYOUT OF THE BRANCH (it used to be one pile in the root)
#   live/session-<slot>.json      the live descriptor, one per slot
#   live/handoff.json             the relay limits + the relay's live status
#   models/models-<slot>.json     the model roster of that session
#   snapshots/audit.json          the audit trail (was audit.json)
#   snapshots/code.json           the code snapshot (was code.json)
#   chats/<repo>.json             OpenCode chat bundles (unchanged)

#       saved-<slot>-<stamp>.json    the «Сохранить» snapshots

# record is filed under today (UTC).

JSON_FILES=()

EXPLICIT_STARTED_AT=0

    slot=windows)  FILE="live/session-windows.json" ;;
    slot=agent)    FILE="live/session-agent.json" ;;

    slot=agent-windows)  FILE="live/session-agent-windows.json" ;;
    slot=opencode) FILE="live/session-opencode.json" ;;
    slot=opencode-linux) FILE="live/session-opencode-linux.json" ;;
    slot=opencode-windows) FILE="live/session-opencode-windows.json" ;;
    slot=hub)      FILE="live/session-hub.json" ;;
    slot=hub-linux)      FILE="live/session-hub-linux.json" ;;
    slot=hub-windows)    FILE="live/session-hub-windows.json" ;;

  local wd
  wd="$(date -u -d "$d" '+%a' 2>/dev/null || true)"
  case "$wd" in
    Mon|Tue|Wed|Thu|Fri|Sat|Sun) : ;;
    *) wd="$(python3 -c "import datetime,sys;print(datetime.date.fromisoformat(sys.argv[1]).strftime('%a'))" "$d" 2>/dev/null || echo "")" ;;

        return {k: scrub(v) for k, v in o.items() if not SECRET_RE.search(str(k))}

    path = path.strip()
    if not path:
        continue

        with open(path, encoding='utf-8') as f:

        merged = scrub(merged)

# the staging file ends up empty and the script reports "nothing to publish"
# and exits 0. The step goes green and no address is ever published. That is
# exactly what happened: the Windows desk was up and reachable, and the panel

    json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2).encode('utf-8'))

new_number = str(new.get("runNumber", ""))
if not (re.fullmatch(r"\d+", old_number) and re.fullmatch(r"\d+", new_number)):

# initial publish (hub.yml) runs BEFORE the tunnel keeper's reserve is up, so it
# carries no url2; if that initial publish retries after a keeper publish that
# DID set url2, the whole-file overwrite would erase the reserve and the panel
# would lose its only fallback. Carry url2 over from the on-branch descriptor

            v = json.load(f)

    raise SystemExit(1)

new_run = str(new.get('runId', '')) or run_id

    raise SystemExit(1)

# simply did not know about them must not erase either (same race as url2).

    if not new.get(key) and old.get(key):
        new[key] = old[key]

    json.dump(new, f, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)
    f.write('\n')

import json, sys
try:
    print(json.load(open(sys.argv[1], encoding='utf-8')).get('runId', ''))
except Exception:
    print('')
PY
)

    EXISTING_STARTED_AT=$(python3 - "$FILE" <<'PY'
import json, sys
try:
    print(json.load(open(sys.argv[1], encoding='utf-8')).get('startedAt', ''))
except Exception:
    print('')
PY
)

      python3 - "$STAGE" "$EXISTING_STARTED_AT" <<'PY'

path, started = sys.argv[1:]
try:
    with open(path, encoding='utf-8') as f:
        data = json.load(f)
    data['startedAt'] = started
    with open(path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        json.dump(data, f, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)
        f.write('\n')

    print('publish_session: could not preserve startedAt: %s' % e, file=sys.stderr)
    raise SystemExit(1)
PY
    fi

mkdir -p "$(dirname "$FILE")"
carry_url2
cp "$STAGE" "$FILE"
git config user.email "session@symbiosis"
git config user.name  "Session state"
git add "$FILE"

if git diff --cached --quiet; then
  echo "publish_session: unchanged"
  exit 0
fi

git commit -q -m "session $(date -u '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')"

# NOT a force push any more.
#
# Two desks publish to this branch at the same time, and -f made the second
# writer erase the first: the Linux desk cloned the branch before the Windows
# desk existed, then force-pushed its own single-file tree over it. Measured -
# session-windows.json was written by a step that reported success, and the
# branch afterwards held only session-linux.json.
#
# So: fetch, replay this one file on top of whatever is there now, push
# normally, and retry if someone else got in between. Each desk only ever
# touches its own file, so the merge is trivial and cannot conflict.
pushed=0
for attempt in $(seq 1 12); do
  if git push -q origin "HEAD:$BRANCH" 2>/dev/null; then
    pushed=1
    break
  fi
  echo "publish_session: push attempt $attempt failed; refreshing $BRANCH" >&2
  if git fetch -q origin "$BRANCH" 2>/dev/null; then
    git reset -q --hard FETCH_HEAD
    if session_publish_blocked; then
      echo "publish_session: $FILE is owned by a newer run; left alone"
      exit 0
    fi
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$FILE")"
    carry_url2
    cp "$STAGE" "$FILE"
    git add "$FILE"
    git commit -q -m "session $(date -u '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')" 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
  delay=$((attempt * 2))
  [ "$delay" -gt 30 ] && delay=30
  sleep "$delay"
done

if [ "$pushed" = 1 ]; then
  echo "publish_session: published $FILE to $BRANCH"
else
  echo "publish_session: push failed after retries" >&2
  exit 1
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# One-time reorganisation of the session-state branch: from one pile in the
# root into folders that say what each thing IS.
#
#   live/session-<slot>.json      the live descriptor of a slot
#   live/handoff.json             the relay limits + its live status
#   models/models-<slot>.json     the model roster of that session
#   snapshots/audit.json          the audit trail
#   snapshots/code.json           the code snapshot
#   history/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<Wd>/    everything historical, by day and weekday
#   chats/, artifacts/            unchanged
#
# WHY IT IS SAFE TO RUN TWICE, OR NOT AT ALL
#   Every reader tries the new path first and falls back to the old name, so a
#   branch that was never migrated keeps working, and a half-migrated branch is
#   still readable. The migration only ever MOVES files (git mv, so history is
#   kept) and never rewrites their content.
#
#   Note that publish_session.sh already writes into the new layout, so files
#   that appeared after the deploy are skipped (the source no longer exists).
#
# USAGE
#   migrate_session_state.sh            migrate the branch over the network
#   SESSION_STATE_URL=file:///tmp/x.git migrate_session_state.sh   (local test)
set -uo pipefail

BRANCH="session-state"
HUB_LOGS="${HUB_LOGS:-$HOME/.npm-hub/logs}"
mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS" 2>/dev/null || true
log() { echo "[migrate-session-state $(date -u '+%H:%M:%S')] $*" | tee -a "$HUB_LOGS/migrate-session-state.log"; }

REMOTE="${SESSION_STATE_URL:-https://x-access-token:${GH_TOKEN:-${GITHUB_TOKEN:-}}@github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:-}.git}"
if [ -z "${SESSION_STATE_URL:-}" ] && [ -z "${GH_TOKEN:-}${GITHUB_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
  log "no GitHub token; set GH_TOKEN or SESSION_STATE_URL"
  exit 1
fi

WORK="$(mktemp -d)" || { log "cannot create a work directory"; exit 1; }
cleanup() { rm -rf "$WORK"; }
trap cleanup EXIT

if ! git clone -q --depth 1 --branch "$BRANCH" "$REMOTE" "$WORK/state" 2>/dev/null; then
  log "no $BRANCH branch yet; nothing to migrate"
  exit 0
fi
cd "$WORK/state" || exit 1

moved=0
move() {
  [ -e "$1" ] || return 0
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$2")" || return 1
  if git mv -q "$1" "$2" 2>/dev/null || mv -f "$1" "$2" 2>/dev/null; then
    moved=$((moved + 1))
    return 0
  fi
  log "could not move $1 -> $2"
  return 1
}

# 1. the live descriptors
for f in session.json session-*.json handoff.json; do
  [ -e "$f" ] || continue
  move "$f" "live/$f"
done

# 2. the model rosters
for f in models-*.json; do
  [ -e "$f" ] || continue
  move "$f" "models/$f"
done

# 3. the audit/code pair
for f in audit.json code.json; do
  [ -e "$f" ] || continue
  move "$f" "snapshots/$f"
done

# 4. the historical bundles, filed under the day and the weekday in their name
#    (saved/<name>-YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS.json -> history/YYYY-MM-DD/Wd/<name>-<stamp>.json)
if [ -d saved ]; then
  for f in saved/*.json; do
    [ -e "$f" ] || continue
    base="$(basename "$f")"
    day=""
    if [[ "$base" =~ ([0-9]{8})T[0-9]{6} ]]; then
      raw="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
      day="${raw:0:4}-${raw:4:2}-${raw:6:2}"
    else
      day="$(date -u '+%Y-%m-%d')"
    fi
    wd="$(python3 -c "import datetime,sys;print(datetime.date.fromisoformat(sys.argv[1]).strftime('%a'))" "$day" 2>/dev/null || echo '---')"
    move "$f" "history/$day/$wd/saved-$base"
  done
  rmdir saved 2>/dev/null || true
fi

if [ "$moved" -eq 0 ]; then
  log "nothing to migrate - the branch is already in folders"
  exit 0
fi

git add -A >/dev/null 2>&1
if git diff --cached --quiet; then
  log "nothing to migrate - the branch is already in folders"
  exit 0
fi

git config user.email "migrate@zen-panel"
git config user.name  "Session state migration"
git commit -q -m "session-state: split the root into live/, models/, snapshots/, history/"

pushed=0
for attempt in $(seq 1 8); do
  if git push -q origin "HEAD:$BRANCH" 2>/dev/null; then
    pushed=1
    break
  fi
  # Somebody published while we worked: rebase our moves on top and try again.
  git fetch -q origin "$BRANCH" 2>/dev/null || true
  git rebase -q FETCH_HEAD >/dev/null 2>&1 || git reset -q --hard FETCH_HEAD
  sleep $((attempt * 2))
done

if [ "$pushed" = 1 ]; then
  log "migrated $moved file(s) into folders on $BRANCH"
  exit 0
fi
log "push failed after retries; the branch is untouched (nothing was force-pushed)"
exit 1

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Publish the live session's connection details so the panel can show them.
#
# The job summary already prints the address, user and password, but it is
# prose meant for a human with a browser: not machine-readable, and on a phone
# it is several taps behind the Actions UI. The panel is where the session is
# started, so it is where the credentials belong.
#
# They go to an orphan branch, session-state, as session.json. An orphan branch
# keeps this churn out of the history of main and lets the file be replaced
# wholesale every time without ever conflicting.
#
# WHO CAN READ THIS
#   On a public repository the branch is public, and so is the password in it.
#   That is the same exposure as the run summary, which is also public - but it
#   is worth being explicit, because a password on a web page feels different
#   from one in a log. Everything here dies with the runner within six hours,
#   and any secret in it is regenerated per run. If that is not acceptable,
#   make the repository private; the panel reads it with the same token either
#   way.
#
# TWO DESKS AT ONCE
#   Pass slot=linux, slot=windows or slot=agent and the entry lands in its own
#   file - session-linux.json, session-windows.json, session-agent.json,
#   session-opencode.json and session-hub.json - so
#   agent/opencode/hub take an -linux/-windows suffix (one file per OS, so two
#   runners stop overwriting each other); the bare slot stays for old runs.
#   the two desks and the agent never overwrite each other. Without a slot the
#   old single session.json is used, which keeps the older workflows working
#   unchanged.
#
#   The panel reads all three and shows whichever are live.
#
# MODELS AND SAVED SNAPSHOTS
#   Sessions alone do not survive usefully: which model answered, which died,
#   which recovered - that roster lives in ~/.zen_free_models.json on the
#   runner and dies with it. So every session also publishes its models:
#
#     publish_session.sh slot=agent file=models-agent.json \
#       kind=CLI-агент json=$HOME/.zen_free_models.json
#   file= overrides the target on the branch (validated: only the known
#   mailboxes are accepted, so a typo cannot spray files across the branch).
#   json= merges a local JSON file into the payload - with secrets scrubbed:
#   any key looking like a key/token/secret/password is dropped, because
#   opencode.json holds API keys and this branch may be public. Pass scrub=0
#   to disable.
#
# LAYOUT OF THE BRANCH (it used to be one pile in the root)
#   live/session-<slot>.json      the live descriptor, one per slot
#   live/handoff.json             the relay limits + the relay's live status
#   models/models-<slot>.json     the model roster of that session
#   snapshots/audit.json          the audit trail (was audit.json)
#   snapshots/code.json           the code snapshot (was code.json)
#   chats/<repo>.json             OpenCode chat bundles (unchanged)
#   history/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<Wd>/    everything historical, by day and weekday:
#       run-<runNumber>.json         one record per run: success or failure
#       saved-<slot>-<stamp>.json    the «Сохранить» snapshots
#       audit-<slot>-<stamp>.json
#       opencode-<stamp>.json
#   artifacts/<file>              files the user pushed from the hub
#   Every reader tries the new path first and falls back to the old root name,
#   so a branch that was never migrated keeps working.
#
#   publish_session.sh journal=1 writes the run record:
#     publish_session.sh journal=1 slot=hub-linux conclusion=success \
#       startedAt=... endedAt=...
#
# Usage: publish_session.sh key=value ...
#   Recognised keys are passed straight through to JSON, so a new session type
#   can add a field without touching this script.

set -uo pipefail

BRANCH="session-state"
FILE="live/session.json"
JOURNAL=0
# journal_date can come as an argument or from the environment; without it the
# record is filed under today (UTC).
JOURNAL_DATE="${JOURNAL_DATE:-}"

# A slot is a routing instruction, not data: pull it out of the arguments
# before they become JSON.
ARGS=()
JSON_FILES=()
FILE_OVERRIDE=""
SCRUB=1
EXPLICIT_STARTED_AT=0
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    startedAt=*)   EXPLICIT_STARTED_AT=1; ARGS+=("$arg") ;;
    journal_date=*) JOURNAL_DATE="${arg#journal_date=}" ;;
    slot=linux)    FILE="live/session-linux.json" ;;
    slot=windows)  FILE="live/session-windows.json" ;;
    slot=agent)    FILE="live/session-agent.json" ;;
    slot=agent-linux)    FILE="live/session-agent-linux.json" ;;
    slot=agent-windows)  FILE="live/session-agent-windows.json" ;;
    slot=opencode) FILE="live/session-opencode.json" ;;
    slot=opencode-linux) FILE="live/session-opencode-linux.json" ;;
    slot=opencode-windows) FILE="live/session-opencode-windows.json" ;;
    slot=hub)      FILE="live/session-hub.json" ;;
    slot=hub-linux)      FILE="live/session-hub-linux.json" ;;
    slot=hub-windows)    FILE="live/session-hub-windows.json" ;;
    slot=phone)    FILE="live/session-phone.json" ;;
    slot=vnc)      FILE="live/session-vnc.json" ;;
    slot=*)        ;;   # unknown slot: ignore rather than write a stray file
    file=*)        FILE_OVERRIDE="$arg" ;;
    journal=1)     JOURNAL=1 ;;
    scrub=0)       SCRUB=0 ;;
    json=*)        # A Windows path (C:\Users\..) breaks mingw python; slashes
                   # work for both Windows and mingw python, so normalise.
                   _jv="${arg#json=}"; _jv="${_jv//\\//}"; JSON_FILES+=("$_jv") ;;
    *)            ARGS+=("$arg") ;;
  esac
done
set -- ${ARGS+"${ARGS[@]}"}

# A file= override that is not one of the known names is refused outright -
# the branch is a fixed set of mailboxes, not a scratch disk. The caller keeps
# using the old flat names; the layout below turns them into the new folders.
if [ -n "$FILE_OVERRIDE" ]; then
  _f="${FILE_OVERRIDE#file=}"
  if [[ "$_f" =~ ^models-(linux|windows|agent(-linux|-windows)?|opencode(-linux|-windows)?|hub(-linux|-windows)?)\.json$ ]] || \
     [[ "$_f" =~ ^(audit|code)\.json$ ]] || \
     [[ "$_f" =~ ^chats/[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,80}\.json$ ]] || \
     [[ "$_f" =~ ^saved/(audit|code)(-[a-z0-9-]+)?-[0-9]{8}T[0-9]{6}\.json$ ]] || \
     [[ "$_f" =~ ^saved/opencode-[0-9]{8}T[0-9]{6}\.json$ ]] || \
     [[ "$_f" =~ ^saved/(linux|windows|agent(-linux|-windows)?|opencode(-linux|-windows)?|hub(-linux|-windows)?)-[0-9]{8}T[0-9]{6}\.json$ ]] || \
     [[ "$_f" =~ ^history/[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}/(Mon|Tue|Wed|Thu|Fri|Sat|Sun)/[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,90}\.json$ ]]; then
    FILE="$_f"
  else
    echo "publish_session: rejected file override: $_f" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
fi

# ── the layout: one flat pile sorted into folders ─────────────────────────
# Everything used to sit in the branch root, which made "what is this file and
# when is it from" a guessing game. Now: live/ for what is alive right now,
# models/ for the roster, snapshots/ for the audit/code pair, and history/ for
# everything historical, filed under the day and the weekday it belongs to.
#
# date_of_day <YYYYMMDD or YYYY-MM-DD> -> "YYYY-MM-DD/Tue"
history_bucket() {
  local raw="$1" d=""
  if [[ "$raw" =~ ^([0-9]{4})([0-9]{2})([0-9]{2})$ ]]; then
    d="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}-${BASH_REMATCH[2]}-${BASH_REMATCH[3]}"
  elif [[ "$raw" =~ ^([0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2})$ ]]; then
    d="$raw"
  else
    d="$(date -u '+%Y-%m-%d')"
  fi
  local wd
  wd="$(date -u -d "$d" '+%a' 2>/dev/null || true)"
  case "$wd" in
    Mon|Tue|Wed|Thu|Fri|Sat|Sun) : ;;
    *) wd="$(python3 -c "import datetime,sys;print(datetime.date.fromisoformat(sys.argv[1]).strftime('%a'))" "$d" 2>/dev/null || echo "")" ;;
  esac
  [ -n "$wd" ] || wd="---"
  printf '%s/%s' "$d" "$wd"
}

# A date out of a <name>-YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS.json stamp; today when there is none.
stamp_bucket() {
  local name="$1" raw=""
  if [[ "$name" =~ ([0-9]{8})T[0-9]{6} ]]; then raw="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"; fi
  history_bucket "$raw"
}

layout_file() {
  local f="$1" bucket
  case "$f" in
    live/*|chats/*|history/*|artifacts/*) printf '%s' "$f"; return 0 ;;
  esac
  case "$f" in
    session*.json) printf 'live/%s' "$f"; return 0 ;;
    models-*.json) printf 'models/%s' "$f"; return 0 ;;
    audit.json|code.json) printf 'snapshots/%s' "$f"; return 0 ;;
    handoff.json) printf 'live/handoff.json'; return 0 ;;
  esac
  if [[ "$f" == saved/* ]]; then
    # saved/audit-hub-20260102T030405.json -> history/2026-01-02/Fri/saved-audit-hub-...
    bucket="$(stamp_bucket "${f#saved/}")"
    printf 'history/%s/saved-%s' "$bucket" "${f#saved/}"
    return 0
  fi
  printf '%s' "$f"
}

if [ "$JOURNAL" = "1" ]; then
  _num="${GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER:-0}"
  [ -n "$_num" ] || _num=0
  bucket="$(history_bucket "$JOURNAL_DATE")"
  FILE="history/$bucket/run-$_num.json"
fi
FILE="$(layout_file "$FILE")"
export SCRUB
export JSON_MERGE="$(printf '%s\n' "${JSON_FILES[@]}")" 

# A unique staging file per invocation. A fixed /tmp/session.json is shared by
# every caller on the machine, and two publishes running at once overwrote each
# other's payload - caught by a local race test, where the Windows entry ended
# up carrying the Linux address. Staged under ~/.npm-hub/tmp, never /tmp.
WORK=""
mkdir -p "$HOME/.npm-hub/tmp" || exit 1
if ! STAGE="$(TMPDIR="$HOME/.npm-hub/tmp" mktemp -t session.XXXXXX.json)"; then
  echo "publish_session: cannot create staging file" >&2
  exit 1
fi
cleanup_publish() {
  cd / 2>/dev/null || true
  [ -n "$STAGE" ] && rm -f "$STAGE"
  [ -n "$WORK" ] && rm -rf "$WORK"
}
trap cleanup_publish EXIT

python3 - "$@" <<'PY' > "$STAGE"
import json, os, re, sys, datetime

SECRET_RE = re.compile(r'key|token|secret|passw|auth|credential|private|bearer', re.I)

def scrub(o):
    if isinstance(o, dict):
        return {k: scrub(v) for k, v in o.items() if not SECRET_RE.search(str(k))}
    if isinstance(o, list):
        return [scrub(v) for v in o]
    return o

data = {}
# Local JSON files first, so explicit key=value arguments win over them.
for path in (os.environ.get('JSON_MERGE') or '').splitlines():
    path = path.strip()
    if not path:
        continue
    try:
        with open(path, encoding='utf-8') as f:
            merged = json.load(f)
    except Exception as e:
        sys.stderr.write('publish_session: json=%s skipped (%s)\n' % (path, e))
        continue
    if not isinstance(merged, dict):
        sys.stderr.write('publish_session: json=%s skipped (not an object)\n' % path)
        continue
    if os.environ.get('SCRUB', '1') != '0':
        merged = scrub(merged)
    data.update(merged)
for arg in sys.argv[1:]:
    if '=' not in arg:
        continue
    key, value = arg.split('=', 1)
    if value != '':
        data[key] = value

data.setdefault('startedAt', datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)
                .replace(microsecond=0).isoformat().replace('+00:00', 'Z'))
data.setdefault('state', 'live')
data['runId'] = os.environ.get('GITHUB_RUN_ID', '')
data['runNumber'] = os.environ.get('GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER', '')
data['repo'] = os.environ.get('GITHUB_REPOSITORY', '')
# Write bytes, not text.
#
# Python on the Windows runner defaults stdout to cp1252, and the moment a
# value contains Cyrillic - "Стол Windows" - print() raises UnicodeEncodeError,
# the staging file ends up empty and the script reports "nothing to publish"
# and exits 0. The step goes green and no address is ever published. That is
# exactly what happened: the Windows desk was up and reachable, and the panel
# showed nothing. Measured in the run log, not guessed.
sys.stdout.buffer.write(
    json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2).encode('utf-8'))
sys.stdout.buffer.write(b"\n")
PY

if [ ! -s "$STAGE" ]; then
  echo "publish_session: staging file is empty" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# SESSION_STATE_URL exists for local tests: point it at a file:// bare
# repo and the whole publish runs without touching github.com.
REMOTE="${SESSION_STATE_URL:-https://x-access-token:${GH_TOKEN:-${GITHUB_TOKEN:-}}@github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:-}.git}"
if [ -z "${SESSION_STATE_URL:-}" ] && [ -z "${GH_TOKEN:-}${GITHUB_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
  echo "publish_session: no GitHub token" >&2
  exit 1
fi

if ! WORK="$(mktemp -d)"; then
  echo "publish_session: cannot create work directory" >&2
  exit 1
fi
cd "$WORK" || exit 1

# A shallow clone of one branch, or a fresh orphan when it does not exist yet.
if git clone -q --depth 1 --branch "$BRANCH" \
    "${REMOTE}" state 2>/dev/null; then
  cd state || exit 1
else
  git clone -q --depth 1 \
    "${REMOTE}" state || exit 1
  cd state || exit 1
  git checkout -q --orphan "$BRANCH"
  git rm -rqf . 2>/dev/null || true
fi

IS_SESSION_FILE=0
case "$FILE" in
  live/session.json|live/session-*.json) IS_SESSION_FILE=1 ;;
esac

session_publish_blocked() {
  [ -f "$FILE" ] || return 1
  python3 - "$FILE" "$STAGE" "${GITHUB_RUN_ID:-}" <<'PY'
import json, os, re, sys
file_path, stage_path, run_id = sys.argv[1:]

def read(path):
    try:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            value = json.load(f)
        return value if isinstance(value, dict) else {}
    except Exception:
        return {}

old = read(file_path)
new = read(stage_path)
if not old:
    raise SystemExit(1)
is_session = os.path.basename(file_path).startswith("session")
old_state = str(old.get("state", ""))
new_state = str(new.get("state", ""))
old_run = str(old.get("runId", ""))
new_run = str(new.get("runId", "")) or run_id
if is_session and new_state == "ended":
    if old_state != "ended" and (not old_run or old_run != new_run):
        raise SystemExit(0)
    raise SystemExit(1)
if is_session and new_state != "live":
    raise SystemExit(1)
if not is_session and old_state == "ended":
    raise SystemExit(1)
if not old_run or not new_run or old_run == new_run:
    raise SystemExit(1)
old_number = str(old.get("runNumber", ""))
new_number = str(new.get("runNumber", ""))
if not (re.fullmatch(r"\d+", old_number) and re.fullmatch(r"\d+", new_number)):
    raise SystemExit(0)
raise SystemExit(1 if int(new_number) > int(old_number) else 0)
PY
}

if session_publish_blocked; then
  echo "publish_session: $FILE is owned by a newer run; left alone"
  exit 0
fi

# The reserve address must survive a republish that does not know about it. The
# initial publish (hub.yml) runs BEFORE the tunnel keeper's reserve is up, so it
# carries no url2; if that initial publish retries after a keeper publish that
# DID set url2, the whole-file overwrite would erase the reserve and the panel
# would lose its only fallback. Carry url2 over from the on-branch descriptor
# when the incoming payload omits it and both belong to the same run.
carry_url2() {
  [ "$IS_SESSION_FILE" = 1 ] || return 0
  [ -f "$FILE" ] || return 0
  python3 - "$FILE" "$STAGE" "${GITHUB_RUN_ID:-}" <<'PY'
import json, sys
file_path, stage_path, run_id = sys.argv[1:]

def read(p):
    try:
        with open(p, encoding='utf-8') as f:
            v = json.load(f)
        return v if isinstance(v, dict) else {}
    except Exception:
        return {}

old = read(file_path)
new = read(stage_path)
if new.get('state') != 'live':
    raise SystemExit(1)
old_run = str(old.get('runId', ''))
new_run = str(new.get('runId', '')) or run_id
if old_run and new_run and old_run != new_run:
    raise SystemExit(1)
# url2 = cloudflared reserve, ngrok = third provider leg: a republish that
# simply did not know about them must not erase either (same race as url2).
carried = []
for key in ('url2', 'ngrok'):
    if not new.get(key) and old.get(key):
        new[key] = old[key]
        carried.append(key)
if not carried:
    raise SystemExit(1)
with open(stage_path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    json.dump(new, f, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)
    f.write('\n')
print('publish_session: preserved ' + ', '.join(carried) + ' from the live descriptor', file=sys.stderr)
PY
}

if [ "$IS_SESSION_FILE" = 1 ] && [ "$EXPLICIT_STARTED_AT" -eq 0 ] && [ -f "$FILE" ]; then
  EXISTING_RUN=$(python3 - "$FILE" <<'PY'
import json, sys
try:
    print(json.load(open(sys.argv[1], encoding='utf-8')).get('runId', ''))
except Exception:
    print('')
PY
)
  if [ -z "${GITHUB_RUN_ID:-}" ] || [ "$EXISTING_RUN" = "${GITHUB_RUN_ID:-}" ]; then
    EXISTING_STARTED_AT=$(python3 - "$FILE" <<'PY'
import json, sys
try:
    print(json.load(open(sys.argv[1], encoding='utf-8')).get('startedAt', ''))
except Exception:
    print('')
PY
)
    if [ -n "$EXISTING_STARTED_AT" ]; then
      python3 - "$STAGE" "$EXISTING_STARTED_AT" <<'PY'
import json, sys
path, started = sys.argv[1:]
try:
    with open(path, encoding='utf-8') as f:
        data = json.load(f)
    data['startedAt'] = started
    with open(path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        json.dump(data, f, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)
        f.write('\n')
except Exception as e:
    print('publish_session: could not preserve startedAt: %s' % e, file=sys.stderr)
    raise SystemExit(1)
PY
    fi
  fi
fi

mkdir -p "$(dirname "$FILE")"
carry_url2
cp "$STAGE" "$FILE"
git config user.email "session@symbiosis"
git config user.name  "Session state"
git add "$FILE"

if git diff --cached --quiet; then
  echo "publish_session: unchanged"
  exit 0
fi

git commit -q -m "session $(date -u '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')"

# NOT a force push any more.
#
# Two desks publish to this branch at the same time, and -f made the second
# writer erase the first: the Linux desk cloned the branch before the Windows
# desk existed, then force-pushed its own single-file tree over it. Measured -
# session-windows.json was written by a step that reported success, and the
# branch afterwards held only session-linux.json.
#
# So: fetch, replay this one file on top of whatever is there now, push
# normally, and retry if someone else got in between. Each desk only ever
# touches its own file, so the merge is trivial and cannot conflict.
pushed=0
for attempt in $(seq 1 12); do
  if git push -q origin "HEAD:$BRANCH" 2>/dev/null; then
    pushed=1
    break
  fi
  echo "publish_session: push attempt $attempt failed; refreshing $BRANCH" >&2
  if git fetch -q origin "$BRANCH" 2>/dev/null; then
    git reset -q --hard FETCH_HEAD
    if session_publish_blocked; then
      echo "publish_session: $FILE is owned by a newer run; left alone"
      exit 0
    fi
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$FILE")"
    carry_url2
    cp "$STAGE" "$FILE"
    git add "$FILE"
    git commit -q -m "session $(date -u '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')" 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
  delay=$((attempt * 2))
  [ "$delay" -gt 30 ] && delay=30
  sleep "$delay"
done

if [ "$pushed" = 1 ]; then
  echo "publish_session: published $FILE to $BRANCH"
else
  echo "publish_session: push failed after retries" >&2
  exit 1
fi
=== migrate ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# One-time reorganisation of the session-state branch: from one pile in the
# root into folders that say what each thing IS.
#
#   live/session-<slot>.json      the live descriptor of a slot
#   live/handoff.json             the relay limits + its live status
#   models/models-<slot>.json     the model roster of that session
#   snapshots/audit.json          the audit trail
#   snapshots/code.json           the code snapshot
#   history/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<Wd>/    everything historical, by day and weekday
#   chats/, artifacts/            unchanged
#
# WHY IT IS SAFE TO RUN TWICE, OR NOT AT ALL
#   Every reader tries the new path first and falls back to the old name, so a
#   branch that was never migrated keeps working, and a half-migrated branch is
#   still readable. The migration only ever MOVES files (git mv, so history is
#   kept) and never rewrites their content.
#
#   Note that publish_session.sh already writes into the new layout, so files
#   that appeared after the deploy are skipped (the source no longer exists).
#
# USAGE
#   migrate_session_state.sh            migrate the branch over the network
#   SESSION_STATE_URL=file:///tmp/x.git migrate_session_state.sh   (local test)
set -uo pipefail

BRANCH="session-state"
HUB_LOGS="${HUB_LOGS:-$HOME/.npm-hub/logs}"
mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS" 2>/dev/null || true
log() { echo "[migrate-session-state $(date -u '+%H:%M:%S')] $*" | tee -a "$HUB_LOGS/migrate-session-state.log"; }

REMOTE="${SESSION_STATE_URL:-https://x-access-token:${GH_TOKEN:-${GITHUB_TOKEN:-}}@github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:-}.git}"
if [ -z "${SESSION_STATE_URL:-}" ] && [ -z "${GH_TOKEN:-}${GITHUB_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
  log "no GitHub token; set GH_TOKEN or SESSION_STATE_URL"
  exit 1
fi

WORK="$(mktemp -d)" || { log "cannot create a work directory"; exit 1; }
cleanup() { rm -rf "$WORK"; }
trap cleanup EXIT

if ! git clone -q --depth 1 --branch "$BRANCH" "$REMOTE" "$WORK/state" 2>/dev/null; then
  log "no $BRANCH branch yet; nothing to migrate"
  exit 0
fi
cd "$WORK/state" || exit 1

moved=0
move() {
  [ -e "$1" ] || return 0
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$2")" || return 1
  if git mv -q "$1" "$2" 2>/dev/null || mv -f "$1" "$2" 2>/dev/null; then
    moved=$((moved + 1))
    return 0
  fi
  log "could not move $1 -> $2"
  return 1
}

# 1. the live descriptors
for f in session.json session-*.json handoff.json; do
  [ -e "$f" ] || continue
  move "$f" "live/$f"
done

# 2. the model rosters
for f in models-*.json; do
  [ -e "$f" ] || continue
  move "$f" "models/$f"
done

# 3. the audit/code pair
for f in audit.json code.json; do
  [ -e "$f" ] || continue
  move "$f" "snapshots/$f"
done

# 4. the historical bundles, filed under the day and the weekday in their name
#    (saved/<name>-YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS.json -> history/YYYY-MM-DD/Wd/<name>-<stamp>.json)
if [ -d saved ]; then
  for f in saved/*.json; do
    [ -e "$f" ] || continue
    base="$(basename "$f")"
    day=""
    if [[ "$base" =~ ([0-9]{8})T[0-9]{6} ]]; then
      raw="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
      day="${raw:0:4}-${raw:4:2}-${raw:6:2}"
    else
      day="$(date -u '+%Y-%m-%d')"
    fi
    wd="$(python3 -c "import datetime,sys;print(datetime.date.fromisoformat(sys.argv[1]).strftime('%a'))" "$day" 2>/dev/null || echo '---')"
    move "$f" "history/$day/$wd/saved-$base"
  done
  rmdir saved 2>/dev/null || true
fi

if [ "$moved" -eq 0 ]; then
  log "nothing to migrate - the branch is already in folders"
  exit 0
fi

git add -A >/dev/null 2>&1
if git diff --cached --quiet; then
  log "nothing to migrate - the branch is already in folders"
  exit 0
fi

git config user.email "migrate@zen-panel"
git config user.name  "Session state migration"
git commit -q -m "session-state: split the root into live/, models/, snapshots/, history/"

pushed=0
for attempt in $(seq 1 8); do
  if git push -q origin "HEAD:$BRANCH" 2>/dev/null; then
    pushed=1
    break
  fi
  # Somebody published while we worked: rebase our moves on top and try again.
  git fetch -q origin "$BRANCH" 2>/dev/null || true
  git rebase -q FETCH_HEAD >/dev/null 2>&1 || git reset -q --hard FETCH_HEAD
  sleep $((attempt * 2))
done

if [ "$pushed" = 1 ]; then
  log "migrated $moved file(s) into folders on $BRANCH"
  exit 0
fi
log "push failed after retries; the branch is untouched (nothing was force-pushed)"
exit 1

=== tunnel_keeper ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Dual-tunnel keeper (Z11): one endpoint, TWO public addresses, all the time.
#
# WHY
#   A quick tunnel dies eventually; when it is the only address the user's
#   phone instantly shows «Не открывается» until somebody repairs it. With a
#   reserve address always warm, the app just walks over to it (see the hub
#   APK: url2 fallback) while this daemon resurrects the main one. Repair no
#   longer depends on the job's keep-alive step being alive: this loop owns
#   both addresses by itself.
#
# WHAT IT OWNS
#   main    the workflow's own address (opened by the job, refreshed by the
#           watchdog when that survives - this daemon only fills in when the
#           address dropped and stayed dropped for ~a minute)
#   reserve TUNNEL_TAG=reserve, its own pid/url/log files, refreshed here on
#           every death and republished straight into the session descriptor
#
# PUBLISHED KEYS (preserved by url2-merge upstream in this workflow)
#   hub: url, hubUrl, desktop, mobile + url2 (reserve base)
#   vnc: url, novncUrl (+ url /vnc.html) + url2 (reserve base)
set -uo pipefail

VM="${1:-hub}"          # hub | vnc
HUB_LOGS="${HUB_LOGS:-$HOME/.npm-hub/logs}"
mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS" 2>/dev/null || true
TOOLS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
TOKEN="${GH_TOKEN:-${GITHUB_TOKEN:-}}"
[ -z "$TOKEN" ] && { echo "[tunnel-keeper] no token" >&2; exit 1; }

if [ "$VM" = "vnc" ]; then
  PORT=6081; SLOT=vnc; URLFILE="$HUB_LOGS/vnc-url"; HEALTH_PATH="/vnc.html"
  R_URLFILE="$HUB_LOGS/vnc-url2"
else
  PORT=8090; SLOT=hub-linux; URLFILE="$HUB_LOGS/hub-url"; HEALTH_PATH="/"
  R_URLFILE="$HUB_LOGS/hub-url2"
fi
INTERVAL="${KEEPER_INTERVAL:-20}"
MAIN_FAILS=0
# After a reserve open fails, stop retrying every loop. A quick tunnel that
# Cloudflare refuses (HTTP 429, "too many tunnels") only gets angrier when asked
# every 20 seconds; waiting minutes is what lets it succeed. The count is also
# how many loops to skip before touching the reserve again.
RESERVE_COOLDOWN="${KEEPER_RESERVE_COOLDOWN:-15}"
RESERVE_SKIP=0

log() { echo "[tunnel-keeper:$VM $(date -u '+%H:%M:%S')] $*" | tee -a "$HUB_LOGS/tunnel-keeper.log"; }

healthy() {  # $1 = url
  [ -n "$1" ] && bash "$TOOLS_DIR/tunnel_health.sh" "$1" "$HEALTH_PATH" >/dev/null 2>&1
}

url_for_pidfile() {  # $1 = pidfile path
  local p
  [ -f "$1" ] || return 1
  p="$(tr -dc '0-9' < "$1" 2>/dev/null || true)" || true
  [ -n "${p:-}" ] && kill -0 "$p" 2>/dev/null || return 1
  cat "${1%.pid}.url" 2>/dev/null || true
}

publish_pair() {  # args k=v ... (always includes both base urls we know)
  local main reserve
  main="$(cat "$URLFILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  reserve="$(cat "$R_URLFILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  if [ "$SLOT" = "hub-linux" ]; then
    GH_TOKEN="$TOKEN" bash "$TOOLS_DIR/publish_session.sh" \
      "slot=hub-linux" "kind=NPM-Hub" "os=linux" \
      ${main:+"url=$main"} ${main:+"hubUrl=$main"} ${main:+"desktop=$main/d"} ${main:+"mobile=$main/m"} \
      ${reserve:+"url2=$reserve"} \
      "auth=без пароля" "label=${HUB_LABEL:-hub}" 2>&1 | tail -1
  else
    GH_TOKEN="$TOKEN" bash "$TOOLS_DIR/publish_session.sh" \
      "slot=vnc" "kind=Linux-VNC" "os=linux" \
      ${main:+"url=$main/vnc.html"} ${main:+"novncUrl=$main/vnc.html"} \
      ${reserve:+"url2=$reserve"} \
      "label=${HUB_LABEL:-hub}" 2>&1 | tail -1
  fi
}

open_reserve() {
  local url
  # Drop any previously published reserve BEFORE opening: if this open fails the
  # client must not keep probing a dead address (a stale url2 is exactly what
  # made the panel report «ни основной, ни резервный адрес не отвечает»).
  rm -f "$R_URLFILE"
  url="$(TUNNEL_TAG=reserve bash "$TOOLS_DIR/open_tunnel.sh" "$PORT" "$HUB_LOGS/tunnel-reserve.log" 2>/dev/null || echo)"
  if [ -n "$url" ]; then
    echo "$url" > "$R_URLFILE"
    log "reserve tunnel up: $url"
    RESERVE_SKIP=0
    return 0
  fi
  RESERVE_SKIP="$RESERVE_COOLDOWN"
  log "reserve tunnel reopen failed; backing off $RESERVE_COOLDOWN loops (see tunnel-reserve.log)"
  return 1
}

open_main() {
  local url

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Dual-tunnel keeper (Z11): one endpoint, TWO public addresses, all the time.
#
# WHY
#   A quick tunnel dies eventually; when it is the only address the user's
#   phone instantly shows «Не открывается» until somebody repairs it. With a
#   reserve address always warm, the app just walks over to it (see the hub
#   APK: url2 fallback) while this daemon resurrects the main one. Repair no
#   longer depends on the job's keep-alive step being alive: this loop owns
#   both addresses by itself.
#
# WHAT IT OWNS
#   main    the workflow's own address (opened by the job, refreshed by the
#           watchdog when that survives - this daemon only fills in when the
#           address dropped and stayed dropped for ~a minute)
#   reserve TUNNEL_TAG=reserve, its own pid/url/log files, refreshed here on
#           every death and republished straight into the session descriptor
#
# PUBLISHED KEYS (preserved by url2-merge upstream in this workflow)
#   hub: url, hubUrl, desktop, mobile + url2 (reserve base)
#   vnc: url, novncUrl (+ url /vnc.html) + url2 (reserve base)

VM="${1:-hub}"          # hub | vnc
HUB_LOGS="${HUB_LOGS:-$HOME/.npm-hub/logs}"
mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS" 2>/dev/null || true
TOOLS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

[ -z "$TOKEN" ] && { echo "[tunnel-keeper] no token" >&2; exit 1; }

  PORT=6081; SLOT=vnc; URLFILE="$HUB_LOGS/vnc-url"; HEALTH_PATH="/vnc.html"
  R_URLFILE="$HUB_LOGS/vnc-url2"
else
  PORT=8090; SLOT=hub-linux; URLFILE="$HUB_LOGS/hub-url"; HEALTH_PATH="/"
  R_URLFILE="$HUB_LOGS/hub-url2"
fi
INTERVAL="${KEEPER_INTERVAL:-20}"
MAIN_FAILS=0

# Cloudflare refuses (HTTP 429, "too many tunnels") only gets angrier when asked
# every 20 seconds; waiting minutes is what lets it succeed. The count is also
# how many loops to skip before touching the reserve again.

RESERVE_SKIP=0

log() { echo "[tunnel-keeper:$VM $(date -u '+%H:%M:%S')] $*" | tee -a "$HUB_LOGS/tunnel-keeper.log"; }

healthy() {  # $1 = url
  [ -n "$1" ] && bash "$TOOLS_DIR/tunnel_health.sh" "$1" "$HEALTH_PATH" >/dev/null 2>&1
}

url_for_pidfile() {  # $1 = pidfile path
  local p
  [ -f "$1" ] || return 1
  p="$(tr -dc '0-9' < "$1" 2>/dev/null || true)" || true
  [ -n "${p:-}" ] && kill -0 "$p" 2>/dev/null || return 1
  cat "${1%.pid}.url" 2>/dev/null || true
}

publish_pair() {  # args k=v ... (always includes both base urls we know)
  local main reserve
  main="$(cat "$URLFILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  reserve="$(cat "$R_URLFILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  if [ "$SLOT" = "hub-linux" ]; then
    GH_TOKEN="$TOKEN" bash "$TOOLS_DIR/publish_session.sh" \
      "slot=hub-linux" "kind=NPM-Hub" "os=linux" \
      ${main:+"url=$main"} ${main:+"hubUrl=$main"} ${main:+"desktop=$main/d"} ${main:+"mobile=$main/m"} \
      ${reserve:+"url2=$reserve"} \
      "auth=без пароля" "label=${HUB_LABEL:-hub}" 2>&1 | tail -1
  else
    GH_TOKEN="$TOKEN" bash "$TOOLS_DIR/publish_session.sh" \
      "slot=vnc" "kind=Linux-VNC" "os=linux" \
      ${main:+"url=$main/vnc.html"} ${main:+"novncUrl=$main/vnc.html"} \
      ${reserve:+"url2=$reserve"} \
      "label=${HUB_LABEL:-hub}" 2>&1 | tail -1
  fi
}

open_reserve() {
  local url
  # Drop any previously published reserve BEFORE opening: if this open fails the
  # client must not keep probing a dead address (a stale url2 is exactly what
  # made the panel report «ни основной, ни резервный адрес не отвечает»).
